# IMPERIA COLD WAR — Shared German dossier, East Berlin perspective
 cwgg_east_action_ask_credit:0 "Request Credit"
 cwgg_east_action_ask_credit_terms:0 "25 PP / 720 days\nRequest only; Bonn decides on the credit"
 cwgg_east_action_ask_credit_tt:0 "Through Schalck-Golodkowski, let Bonn know that the Republic's hard-currency position is 'tight'. Bonn decides.\n\n25 PP / 720 days\nRequest only; Bonn decides on the credit\nThe Federal Government decides whether to grant a credit.\nCooldown: 720 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_border_regime:0 "Border Regime"
 cwgg_east_action_border_regime_terms:0 "50 PP / 365 days\nExit pressure -5 / SED control +3"
 cwgg_east_action_border_regime_tt:0 "More mines, more dogs, more watchtowers - and an order to shoot.\n\n50 PP / 365 days\nExit pressure -5 / SED control +3\nGDR exit pressure: §Y-5§!\nSED control: §Y+3§!\nRequires an SED government.\nCooldown: 365 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_close_transit:0 "Close Access Routes"
 cwgg_east_action_close_transit_terms:0 "50 PP / 3 initiative / 730 days\nStarts a Transit Crisis"
 cwgg_east_action_close_transit_tt:0 "Close the transit routes to West Berlin 'for repairs'. A crisis is the point.\n\n50 PP / 3 initiative / 730 days\nStarts a Transit Crisis\nCosts §Y3§! initiative. Starts a §RTransit Crisis§! with the Federal Republic.\nCooldown: 730 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_consumer_imports:0 "Consumer Imports"
 cwgg_east_action_consumer_imports_terms:0 "30 PP / 365 days\nExit pressure -3 / Shortage +5 / Stability +2%"
 cwgg_east_action_consumer_imports_tt:0 "Jeans, coffee and VW Golfs bought in the West to quiet the people - on credit.\n\n30 PP / 365 days\nExit pressure -3 / Shortage +5 / Stability +2%\nGDR exit pressure: §Y-3§!\nGDR hard-currency shortage: §Y+5§!\nCooldown: 365 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_goodwill:0 "Offer Goodwill"
 cwgg_east_action_goodwill_terms:0 "25 PP / 2 initiative / 180 days\nClimate +6 / Border and exchange levers -1"
 cwgg_east_action_goodwill_tt:0 "Lower the compulsory exchange for pensioners, dismantle a stretch of spring guns - and let the diplomats talk about it.\n\n25 PP / 2 initiative / 180 days\nClimate +6 / Border and exchange levers -1\nCosts §Y2§! initiative. Climate §G+6§!; our levers §YBorder Regime§! and §YCompulsory Exchange§! §R-1§!.\nCooldown: 180 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_hva_offensive:0 "HVA in Bonn"
 cwgg_east_action_hva_offensive_terms:0 "25 PP / 2 initiative / 180 days\nPenetration +5 / Federal counter-intelligence remains active"
 cwgg_east_action_hva_offensive_tt:0 "Markus Wolf's Main Directorate for Reconnaissance sends more agents, more Romeos and more money west.\n\n25 PP / 2 initiative / 180 days\nPenetration +5 / Federal counter-intelligence remains active\nCosts §Y2§! initiative. Stasi penetration of Bonn §R+5§!.\nExisting federal counter-intelligence can expose or disrupt these networks.\nRequires an SED government.\nCooldown: 180 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_intershop:0 "Intershops"
 cwgg_east_action_intershop_terms:0 "40 PP / 365 days\nShortage -4 / Media reach +2 / Opposition +1"
 cwgg_east_action_intershop_tt:0 "Western goods for Western money: let citizens with D-Marks from relatives shop in special stores.\n\n40 PP / 365 days\nShortage -4 / Media reach +2 / Opposition +1\nGDR hard-currency shortage: §Y-4§!\nWestern media reach in the GDR: §Y+2§!\nGDR civic opposition: §Y+1§!\nCooldown: 365 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_koko:0 "KoKo"
 cwgg_east_action_koko_terms:0 "50 PP / 540 days\nShortage -6 / Dependence on Bonn +3"
 cwgg_east_action_koko_tt:0 "Schalck-Golodkowski's empire: arms trading, art sales, waste imports - anything for hard currency.\n\n50 PP / 540 days\nShortage -6 / Dependence on Bonn +3\nGDR hard-currency shortage: §Y-6§!\nGDR dependence on West German money: §Y+3§!\nCooldown: 540 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_nva_alert_down:0 "Lower NVA Alert"
 cwgg_east_action_nva_alert_down_terms:0 "0 PP / 30 days\nNVA alert -1 / Climate +2"
 cwgg_east_action_nva_alert_down_tt:0 "Stand the National People's Army down by one level.\n\n0 PP / 30 days\nNVA alert -1 / Climate +2\nNVA alert level §G-1§!, climate §G+2§!.\nCooldown: 30 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_nva_alert_up:0 "Raise NVA Alert"
 cwgg_east_action_nva_alert_up_terms:0 "0 PP / 30 days\nNVA alert +1 / Pressure +5 / Stability -1%"
 cwgg_east_action_nva_alert_up_tt:0 "Put the National People's Army on a higher state of readiness. Each level speeds up mobilisation and hardens war support: level 1 §G+10%§! / §G+2%§!, level 2 §G+25%§! / §G+5%§!, level 3 §G+50%§! / §G+10%§!. Needs the escalation ladder at §YCrisis§! (level 1), §YConfrontation§! (2), or §YWar Danger§!, a countdown or a fully alerted Bundeswehr (3).\n\n0 PP / 30 days\nNVA alert +1 / Pressure +5 / Stability -1%\nNVA alert level §R+1§!, escalation pressure §R+5§!.\nCooldown: 30 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_propose_unity_terms:0 "100 PP / 3 initiative\nBonn must accept before chapter talks begin"
 cwgg_east_action_propose_unity_tt:0 "Offer Bonn formal negotiations on the unity of Germany - on equal terms, with every chapter open. Needs three years of unbroken détente, a climate of at least 70, the Basic Treaty, the Permanent Representations and the traffic agreements in force, and culture or the state visit.\n\nDétente months: §Y[?GER.cwgg_detente_m|0]§!/36 | climate: §Y[?GER.cwgg_klima|0]§!\n\n100 PP / 3 initiative\nBonn must accept before chapter talks begin\n"
 cwgg_east_action_raise_exchange:0 "Raise Exchange"
 cwgg_east_action_raise_exchange_terms:0 "25 PP / 2 initiative / 365 days\nShortage -3 / Exit pressure +1 / Climate -6"
 cwgg_east_action_raise_exchange_tt:0 "Every Western visitor must change more D-Marks a day. Fewer visits, more hard currency.\n\n25 PP / 2 initiative / 365 days\nShortage -3 / Exit pressure +1 / Climate -6\nGDR hard-currency shortage: §Y-3§!\nGDR exit pressure: §Y+1§!\nCosts §Y2§! initiative. Our lever §YCompulsory Exchange§! §G+1§!, climate §R-6§!.\nCooldown: 365 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_recognition_drive:0 "Recognition Drive"
 cwgg_east_action_recognition_drive_terms:0 "200 PP / 365 days\nRecognition requests to UN member states"
 cwgg_east_action_recognition_drive_tt:0 "Request diplomatic recognition from UN member states. Each government decides whether to accept.\n\n200 PP / 365 days\nRecognition requests to UN member states\n\nCooldown: 365 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_reform_course:0 "Press Reform"
 cwgg_east_action_reform_course_terms:0 "75 PP / Once\nExit pressure -6 / SED control -6 / Opposition +3"
 cwgg_east_action_reform_course_tt:0 "Open the press and give dissidents room to speak while preserving a socialist government.\n\n75 PP / Once\nExit pressure -6 / SED control -6 / Opposition +3\nGDR civic opposition: §Y+3§!\nSED control: §Y-6§!\nGDR exit pressure: §Y-6§!\nWestern media reach in the GDR: §Y+3§!\nWestern media reach +3.\nRequires an SED government.\nMay be enacted once."
 cwgg_east_action_stasi_sweep:0 "State Security"
 cwgg_east_action_stasi_sweep_terms:0 "50 PP / 365 days\nOpposition -5 / SED control +2 / Media reach +1"
 cwgg_east_action_stasi_sweep_tt:0 "The Ministry for State Security infiltrates and decomposes ('Zersetzung') the peace and environment groups.\n\n50 PP / 365 days\nOpposition -5 / SED control +2 / Media reach +1\nGDR civic opposition: §Y-5§!\nSED control: §Y+2§!\nWestern media reach in the GDR: §Y+1§!\nRequires an SED government.\nCooldown: 365 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_tighten_border:0 "Strengthen Border"
 cwgg_east_action_tighten_border_terms:0 "25 PP / 2 initiative / 365 days\nBorder lever +1 / Exit pressure -3 / Pressure +8"
 cwgg_east_action_tighten_border_tt:0 "New fences, mines and SM-70 spring guns along the state border.\n\n25 PP / 2 initiative / 365 days\nBorder lever +1 / Exit pressure -3 / Pressure +8\nGDR exit pressure: §Y-3§!\nCosts §Y2§! initiative. Our lever §YBorder Regime§! §G+1§!, escalation pressure §R+8§!.\nRequires an SED government.\nCooldown: 365 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_transit_checks:0 "Transit Checks"
 cwgg_east_action_transit_checks_terms:0 "25 PP / 2 initiative / 180 days\nBerlin access -5 / Pressure +12 / Climate -5"
 cwgg_east_action_transit_checks_tt:0 "Hours of checks at Helmstedt and Dreilinden. West Berlin should remember whose territory it lies in.\n\n25 PP / 2 initiative / 180 days\nBerlin access -5 / Pressure +12 / Climate -5\nCosts §Y2§! initiative. Climate §R-5§!, escalation pressure §R+12§!, West Berlin's access §R-5§!.\nCooldown: 180 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_action_unity_position_terms:0 "0 PP / 30 days\nReview the DDR position on the current chapter"
 cwgg_east_action_unity_position_tt:0 "Restate East Berlin's position on the chapter now on the table. Chapter §Y[?GER.cwgg_u_cur|0]§! of five; agreed so far §Y[?GER.cwgg_u_agreed|0]§!; failed rounds §Y[?GER.cwgg_u_fail|0]§!/8.\n\n0 PP / 30 days\nReview the DDR position on the current chapter\n\nCooldown: 30 days, shared with the corresponding decision."
 cwgg_east_answer_1_tt:0 "§YBack Down§!\nFree at resolution. Choosing an answer starts a 30-day lock on the shared crisis instruction. The Federal Republic's current course remains confidential."
 cwgg_east_answer_2_tt:0 "§YStall§!\nFree at resolution. Choosing an answer starts a 30-day lock on the shared crisis instruction. The Federal Republic's current course remains confidential."
 cwgg_east_answer_3_tt:0 "§YEscalate§!\nCosts 1 initiative when the round resolves. Choosing an answer starts a 30-day lock on the shared crisis instruction. The Federal Republic's current course remains confidential."

The Federal Republic's current course remains confidential. Requires the Soviet Union to exist. This does not commit Moscow to intervene."
 cwgg_east_answer_5_tt:0 "§YMake a Counter-Offer§!\nCosts 1 initiative when the round resolves. Choosing an answer starts a 30-day lock on the shared crisis instruction. The Federal Republic's current course remains confidential."

localisation/english/COLDWAR_GER_1970_l_.text:
l_english:
 COLDWAR_GBR.1.a:0 "Lafontaine takes the party."
 COLDWAR_GBR.1.b:0 "Scharping holds on - the left is told to wait."
 COLDWAR_GBR.1.desc:0 "Twenty minutes of standing ovation. Oskar Lafontaine had not announced a candidacy; now the delegates demand one. Rudolf Scharping, the chairman, sits on the podium and knows that a vote tomorrow would be a vote of no confidence. In the corridors the Lower Saxony delegation counts heads for its own man - Gerhard Schröder, who wants the chancellorship more than the party."
 COLDWAR_GBR.1.t:0 "Mannheim"
 COLDWAR_GBR.10.a:0 "The party breaks with its past."
 COLDWAR_GBR.10.b:0 "Close ranks behind the old man."
 COLDWAR_GBR.10.desc:0 "The prosecutors, the press and the party's own young leaders demand the names. The old chancellor says he gave his word."
 COLDWAR_GBR.10.t:0 "The Word of Honour"
 COLDWAR_GBR.11.a:0 "Build it - Bavaria does not give way."
 COLDWAR_GBR.11.b:0 "Abandon it - reprocess in France instead."
 COLDWAR_GBR.11.desc:0 "Tens of thousands camp in the forest around the construction site; police use CS gas from helicopters. Austria protests, and the energy companies begin to doubt."
 COLDWAR_GBR.11.t:0 "The Battle of Wackersdorf"
 COLDWAR_GBR.12.a:0 "Ask for a vote of confidence and lose it on purpose."
 COLDWAR_GBR.12.b:0 "Seek a tolerance pact with the Greens."
 COLDWAR_GBR.12.c:0 "Govern on and dare them."
 COLDWAR_GBR.12.desc:0 "The opposition prepares a constructive vote of no confidence; the chancellor prepares an answer. Whoever moves first sets the terms."
 COLDWAR_GBR.12.t:0 "Seventeen Days"
 COLDWAR_GBR.13.a:0 "Schröder is the candidate."
 COLDWAR_GBR.13.b:0 "The chairman insists on his right."
 COLDWAR_GBR.13.desc:0 "Chairman, parliamentary leader and the premier of Lower Saxony pose for the photographers in Bonn, arms linked, smiles fixed. Behind the smiles one question: who will the party put on the posters? The Lower Saxony state election is two months away, and Schröder has announced that a single per cent lost will end his ambitions."
 COLDWAR_GBR.13.t:0 "The Troika"
 COLDWAR_GBR.14.a:0 "A pact: moderate wages, more apprenticeships."
 COLDWAR_GBR.14.b:0 "The talks collapse - and everybody blames the government."
 COLDWAR_GBR.14.desc:0 "The third round in the chancellery. IG Metall wants early retirement at sixty and refuses to talk about wage guidelines; the employers' federation wants exactly that and refuses to promise a single job in return. The chancellor has invited the press for seven o'clock."
 COLDWAR_GBR.14.t:0 "The Alliance for Jobs"
 COLDWAR_GBR.15.a:0 "The chancellor takes the party as well."
 COLDWAR_GBR.15.b:0 "Bring him back - at any price."
 COLDWAR_GBR.15.desc:0 "A Thursday evening in March: the finance minister and party chairman resigns from every office he holds, without a word to the press, and switches off his telephone. Bonn learns about it from the news agencies. The left of the party has lost its champion - and is looking for someone to blame."
 COLDWAR_GBR.15.t:0 "The Chairman Resigns"
 COLDWAR_GBR.2.a:0 "Form a red-green government."
 COLDWAR_GBR.2.b:0 "Without a majority: a pact for the next election."
 COLDWAR_GBR.2.desc:0 "SPD and Greens sit down to negotiate a federal government. Whether they can form one depends on the last election - and on what each side is willing to give up."
 COLDWAR_GBR.2.t:0 "Coalition with the Greens"
 COLDWAR_GBR.3.a:0 "Answer with reforms the voters can see."
 COLDWAR_GBR.3.b:0 "Answer with a tougher line on extremists."
 COLDWAR_GBR.3.c:0 "Ignore them - they will fade."
 COLDWAR_GBR.3.desc:0 "Polls show the small parties rising: the FDP as the only liberal opposition, the Greens or the far left among students, the NPD among the disappointed. The coalition must decide how to answer."
 COLDWAR_GBR.3.t:0 "The Edges Grow"
 COLDWAR_GBR.4.a:0 "A Christian-liberal coalition."
 COLDWAR_GBR.4.b:0 "A social-liberal coalition."
 COLDWAR_GBR.4.c:0 "No majority without them. Call an election."
 COLDWAR_GBR.4.desc:0 "The coalition committee meets for the last time. The chancellor's party can try a smaller coalition - but only if the numbers from the last election are there."
 COLDWAR_GBR.4.t:0 "The End of the Grand Coalition"
 COLDWAR_GBR.5.a:0 "A non-aggression pact: separate parties, one parliamentary group."
 COLDWAR_GBR.5.b:0 "Separate groups, separate campaigns."
 COLDWAR_GBR.5.c:0 "The CSU returns to Bavaria."
 COLDWAR_GBR.5.desc:0 "The two Union parties face each other at the conference table in Wildbad Kreuth. They can make peace on new terms - or go their separate ways for good."
 COLDWAR_GBR.5.t:0 "Kreuth, Again"
 COLDWAR_GBR.6.a:0 "Call an election and win a mandate of our own."
 COLDWAR_GBR.6.b:0 "Win over the FDP: a Christian-liberal coalition."
 COLDWAR_GBR.6.c:0 "Govern on, vote by vote."
 COLDWAR_GBR.6.desc:0 "Two deputies are rumoured to be wavering - and the Stasi's money has found its way to Bonn before. The chancellor must decide how to secure his majority."
 COLDWAR_GBR.6.t:0 "Two Votes"
 COLDWAR_GBR.7.a:0 "Govern pragmatically."
 COLDWAR_GBR.7.b:0 "Close Hanau - whatever the cost."
 COLDWAR_GBR.7.desc:0 "Fischer's first months in Wiesbaden: the Hanau nuclear fuel plants, the chemical industry, a coalition partner that wants jobs. The party base watches every compromise."
 COLDWAR_GBR.7.t:0 "The First Green Minister"
 COLDWAR_GBR.8.a:0 "The party follows its foreign minister."
 COLDWAR_GBR.8.b:0 "The party says no - the coalition breaks."
 COLDWAR_GBR.8.desc:0 "Delegates shout 'warmonger'. Fischer, his ear bleeding, speaks of Auschwitz and Srebrenica. The vote decides whether the coalition survives."
 COLDWAR_GBR.8.t:0 "The Bielefeld Party Congress"
 COLDWAR_GBR.9.a:0 "Späth challenges - and wins."
 COLDWAR_GBR.9.b:0 "The challenge collapses. Kohl remains."
 COLDWAR_GBR.9.desc:0 "The delegates wait for the challenger to declare. Kohl has counted the votes; the reformers have counted the polls."
 COLDWAR_GBR.9.t:0 "Bremen"
 COLDWAR_GBR.90.a:0 "Sanctions until the programme is dismantled."
 COLDWAR_GBR.90.b:0 "Prepare to disarm Germany by force."
 COLDWAR_GBR.90.b.tt:0 "§RCreates a war goal against the Federal Republic.§! Whoever chooses this is prepared to fight a nuclear power in the heart of Europe."
 COLDWAR_GBR.90.c:0 "Accept it - quietly."
 COLDWAR_GBR.90.desc:0 "Bonn has built a nuclear weapon. Every agreement since 1954 - the renunciation of ABC weapons, the Non-Proliferation Treaty, the Four Powers' rights - is being tested. The government must decide how to answer."
 COLDWAR_GBR.90.t:0 "Germany Has the Bomb"
 COLDWAR_GCIV.1.a:0 "The chancellor receives him publicly."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.1.b:0 "A private welcome - nothing for the cameras."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.1.desc:0 "Photographers have climbed the garden wall in Langenbroich. The Soviet embassy lets it be known that an official reception would be 'an unfriendly act'; the opposition demands one. The author himself wants only a desk and silence - and a word from the chancellor."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.1.t:0 "Solzhenitsyn in Germany"
 COLDWAR_GCIV.2.a:0 "A public statement and a parliamentary delegation."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.2.b:0 "Visas and scholarships for the persecuted, without fanfare."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.2.desc:0 "Václav Havel is in custody again. The embassy in Prague reports that a public statement from Bonn would make his release more likely - or less; the diplomats disagree. A group of Bundestag members wants to travel to Prague and visit the signatories in person."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.2.t:0 "Charter 77"
 COLDWAR_GCIV.3.a:0 "Binding targets - Germany leads by example."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.3.b:0 "A mandate to negotiate, nothing more."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.3.desc:0 "Four in the morning in the Congress Centre. The oil states want no targets at all, the island states want them now, Washington wants them later. The chair has one draft left and two ways to end the night."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.3.t:0 "The Climate Conference in Berlin"
 COLDWAR_GCIV.4.a:0 "Tighten the export laws - prison for the guilty."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.4.b:0 "Blame a few black sheep and move on."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.4.desc:0 "The New York Times calls it 'Auschwitz in the sand'. The chancellor's office has the files on its desk: more than fifty German firms have supplied Libya and Iraq with plants that can produce chemical weapons. The export laws allowed almost all of it."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.4.t:0 "Poison Gas from Lahr"
 COLDWAR_GCIV.5.a:0 "A Luftwaffe airlift directly to the camps."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.5.b:0 "Through the churches and the Red Cross only."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.5.desc:0 "The Derg in Addis Ababa demands that all aid go through its own ministries. The relief organisations warn that grain handed to the government will end up with the army. The Luftwaffe has Transall transport aircraft ready in Hanover."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.5.t:0 "The Famine in Ethiopia"
 COLDWAR_GCIV.6.a:0 "Special aid - and a word of regret."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.6.b:0 "Aid, yes. The past is for historians."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.6.desc:0 "SWAPO has won the election. Windhoek's new government invites the Federal Republic to the independence celebrations and asks, politely, what Germany intends to say about the years between 1904 and 1908."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.6.t:0 "Namibia Votes"
 COLDWAR_GCIV.7.a:0 "Back Contadora - peace before ideology."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.7.b:0 "Stand with Washington."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.7.desc:0 "The Contadora group - Mexico, Venezuela, Colombia and Panama - asks the Europeans to back its peace plan. Washington asks its allies not to legitimise the Sandinistas. Both requests arrive on the same day."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.7.t:0 "Central America"
 COLDWAR_GCIV.8.a:0 "Hope for the best."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.8.desc:0 "Monte Carlo, September 1993. Sydney, Beijing, Manchester, Istanbul and Berlin wait for the envelope. The bid committee has been too generous with gifts and too careless with dossiers on the IOC members' private lives; the newspapers have found out."
 COLDWAR_GCIV.8.t:0 "The IOC Decides"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.1.a:0 "We respect the court. This ends here."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.1.a.tt:0 "§GThe path ends for good.§! The republic has defended itself."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.1.b:0 "The court has no army. We ignore it."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.1.b.tt:0 "§RA constitutional crisis.§! Every other government will hear of it."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.1.desc:0 "The Federal Constitutional Court has opened proceedings under Article 21 of the Basic Law to ban the NPD as unconstitutional, and has issued an injunction against the government's emergency plans. The president of the court says the Basic Law 'does not provide for its own abolition'."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.1.t:0 "Karlsruhe Moves"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.10.a:0 "We condemn it."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.10.b:0 "This is Germany's own affair."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.10.desc:0 "The West German government has suspended the Bundestag and handed power to a 'National Directorate'. In the heart of Europe, between NATO and the Warsaw Pact, a democracy has ended."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.10.t:0 "Dictatorship in Bonn"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.20.a:0 "Suspend Bonn from the Alliance."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.20.a.tt:0 "If Bonn is still a member, it §Rleaves NATO§! (one member's decision is enough)."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.20.b:0 "Economic sanctions."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.20.c:0 "Invoke the Allied reserved rights - prepare to intervene."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.20.c.tt:0 "The Western Allies never gave up their rights for Germany as a whole and Berlin. §RCreates a war goal to restore the Basic Law.§! The Allies would be marching into the country they once liberated - and rebuilt."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.20.d:0 "Condemn it, but keep the channels open."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.20.desc:0 "Bonn's new rulers still sit in NATO's councils, still command twelve divisions assigned to the Alliance, still hold the codes of the nuclear sharing arrangements. Every member government must decide what the Alliance owes a dictatorship."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.20.t:0 "The Alliance and the Directorate"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.25.a:0 "Welcome back. Lift our measures."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.25.b:0 "Trust will have to be earned."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.25.desc:0 "Bonn has lifted the emergency decrees, recalled the Bundestag and announced free elections. The question is whether the world will take the Germans back - again."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.25.t:0 "The Republic Returns"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.3.a:0 "Count the votes."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.3.a.tt:0 "§Y40%§! (more without a government majority, if the emergency laws were tied to the court or with a popularly elected president) that the Bundestag replaces the chancellor - the path ends. Otherwise the generals must choose."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.3.desc:0 "The opposition and the government's own dissidents table a constructive vote of no confidence. If they find a majority for another chancellor, the emergency is over before it began."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.3.t:0 "The Vote in the Bundestag"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.30.a:0 "Invoke the enemy-state clauses of the UN Charter."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.30.a.tt:0 "Articles 53 and 107 allow action against a former enemy state that resumes an aggressive policy. §RCreates a war goal against the Federal Republic.§! The road to the Rhine has been planned since 1945; now it would be driven."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.30.b:0 "Alert the Group of Soviet Forces and guarantee our allies."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.30.c:0 "Sanctions and a note of protest."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.30.desc:0 "Twenty-five years after the Great Patriotic War, nationalists rule in Bonn. The marshals want to know whether the Group of Soviet Forces in Germany is to be placed on alert. The Foreign Ministry reminds the Politburo that the UN Charter still names Germany an 'enemy state'."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.30.t:0 "Revanchism in Power"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.31.a:0 "Prepare for every eventuality."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.31.a.tt:0 "§RCreates a war goal against the Federal Republic.§! The plans in the General Staff's safe stop being exercises."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.31.b:0 "Reinforce the Western Group of Forces."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.31.c:0 "Watch and wait."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.31.desc:0 "Bonn is rearming outside every Alliance quota and has torn up the treaties of the 1970s. The General Staff asks for permission to prepare for every eventuality."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.31.t:0 "The Directorate Arms"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.32.a:0 "Any attack on the GDR is an attack on the Soviet Union."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.32.b:0 "Strike before the Directorate does."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.32.b.tt:0 "§RCreates a war goal against the Federal Republic.§! A pre-emptive war on German soil - the nightmare of every planner since 1949."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.32.desc:0 "The National Directorate claims the territory of the German Democratic Republic and has issued a war goal against East Berlin. Every treaty since 1945 is at stake."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.32.t:0 "Bonn Claims the GDR"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.4.a:0 "Await their answer."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.4.a.tt:0 "§Y50%§! that the generals refuse (more with the Innere Führung reforms and NATO integration) - then the path ends."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.4.desc:0 "The chief of staff of the Bundeswehr is asked whether the armed forces will carry out the government's orders. The officers swore an oath to the Basic Law, not to a government; the Innere Führung taught them to refuse unlawful orders."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.4.t:0 "The Generals' Answer"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.40.a:0 "The anti-fascist protective wall was right."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.40.b:0 "Appeal to the United Nations."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.40.desc:0 "The GDR has always called the Federal Republic a revanchist state. Now Bonn's own government seems determined to prove it. The National People's Army is put on alert; the Politburo asks Moscow for guarantees."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.40.t:0 "Fascism on Our Border"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.45.a:0 "Ask Moscow for protection."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.45.b:0 "Mobilise and appeal to the West."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.45.desc:0 "The National Directorate has declared the Warsaw Treaty of 1970 void - including the recognition of the Oder-Neisse line. Every Polish family that was moved west in 1945 understands what that means."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.45.t:0 "Bonn Tears Up the Warsaw Treaty"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.5.a:0 "Let them march."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.5.b:0 "Ban the march as a threat to public order."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.5.desc:0 "Trade unions, churches, students and the Greens call a day of protest against the 'march to the right'. Hundreds of thousands fill the Bonn Hofgarten."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.5.t:0 "The Other Germany Takes to the Streets"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.6.a:0 "The Basic Law holds."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.6.desc:0 "The constructive vote of no confidence succeeds. The Bundestag elects a new chancellor, who lifts the emergency decrees in his first act. The republic has defended itself - narrowly."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.6.t:0 "A New Chancellor"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.60.a:0 "Arrest them."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.60.b:0 "Make concessions."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.60.desc:0 "Leaflets at the universities, a strike at the Ruhr pits, a broadcast from a hidden transmitter: 'The Basic Law lives.' The Directorate's police know the names of some of them."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.60.t:0 "The Resistance"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.7.a:0 "It is over."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.7.desc:0 "The inspector general announces on television that the Bundeswehr 'stands on the ground of the Basic Law' and will not act against the Bundestag. The government's authority collapses within hours."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.7.t:0 "The Generals Refuse"
 COLDWAR_GDARK.8.a:0 "The way is open."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.8.desc:0 "The generals declare the armed forces 'neutral in a political dispute'. Nobody will stop the government - and everybody understands what that means."
 COLDWAR_GDARK.8.t:0 "The Army Stands Aside"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.10.a:0 "We sign. The Alliance stands."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.10.b:0 "Washington does not need a declaration."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.10.desc:0 "The ambassador of the Federal Republic has asked for an urgent appointment and delivers a proposal from Bonn. Bonn proposes a joint declaration on the future of the Alliance: American troops stay in Europe, the Europeans carry more of the burden, and both sides consult before they act.\n\nThe cabinet must weigh what the Germans offer against what saying yes would mean - at home, with our neighbours and with our allies."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.10.t:0 "The Atlantic Declaration"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.100.a:0 "Warsaw accepts the credit."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.100.b:0 "Warsaw will not trade people."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.100.desc:0 "The ambassador of the Federal Republic has asked for an urgent appointment and delivers a proposal from Bonn. Bonn offers a billion marks in low-interest credits and a pension settlement. In return 125,000 ethnic Germans may leave for the Federal Republic over four years.\n\nThe cabinet must weigh what the Germans offer against what saying yes would mean - at home, with our neighbours and with our allies."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.100.t:0 "Credits for Emigration"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.101.a:0 "A good day for German diplomacy."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.101.desc:0 "The answer arrives by diplomatic cable, sooner than the Foreign Office expected: [From.GetName] has accepted. 'Credits for Emigration' is no longer a proposal but policy - and the ministries in Bonn now have to make it work."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.101.t:0 "Credits for Emigration: Agreed"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.102.a:0 "Then not - for now."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.102.desc:0 "The ambassador's report is courteous and unambiguous: [From.GetName] will not accept 'Credits for Emigration'. In the Foreign Office the desk officers file the draft away - for another occasion, another approach, or another government."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.102.t:0 "Credits for Emigration: Refused"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.11.a:0 "A good day for German diplomacy."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.11.desc:0 "The answer arrives by diplomatic cable, sooner than the Foreign Office expected: [From.GetName] has accepted. 'The Atlantic Declaration' is no longer a proposal but policy - and the ministries in Bonn now have to make it work."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.11.t:0 "The Atlantic Declaration: Agreed"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.110.a:0 "Yugoslavia accepts."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.110.b:0 "Non-alignment means no conditions."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.110.desc:0 "The ambassador of the Federal Republic has asked for an urgent appointment and delivers a proposal from Bonn. Bonn offers long-term capital aid and a social insurance agreement for Yugoslav workers. In return Belgrade cooperates against terrorists who use the country as a refuge.\n\nThe cabinet must weigh what the Germans offer against what saying yes would mean - at home, with our neighbours and with our allies."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.110.t:0 "A Partnership with Belgrade"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.111.a:0 "A good day for German diplomacy."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.111.desc:0 "The answer arrives by diplomatic cable, sooner than the Foreign Office expected: [From.GetName] has accepted. 'A Partnership with Belgrade' is no longer a proposal but policy - and the ministries in Bonn now have to make it work."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.111.t:0 "A Partnership with Belgrade: Agreed"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.112.a:0 "Then not - for now."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.112.desc:0 "The ambassador's report is courteous and unambiguous: [From.GetName] will not accept 'A Partnership with Belgrade'. In the Foreign Office the desk officers file the draft away - for another occasion, another approach, or another government."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.112.t:0 "A Partnership with Belgrade: Refused"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.12.a:0 "Then not - for now."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.12.desc:0 "The ambassador's report is courteous and unambiguous: [From.GetName] will not accept 'The Atlantic Declaration'. In the Foreign Office the desk officers file the draft away - for another occasion, another approach, or another government."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.12.t:0 "The Atlantic Declaration: Refused"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.120.a:0 "Let them go."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.120.b:0 "They are Soviet citizens."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.120.desc:0 "The ambassador of the Federal Republic has asked for an urgent appointment and delivers a proposal from Bonn. Bonn asks Moscow to allow ethnic Germans to emigrate freely and offers economic cooperation and help with consumer goods in return.\n\nThe cabinet must weigh what the Germans offer against what saying yes would mean - at home, with our neighbours and with our allies."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.120.t:0 "Exit Permits for Soviet Germans"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.121.a:0 "A good day for German diplomacy."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.121.desc:0 "The answer arrives by diplomatic cable, sooner than the Foreign Office expected: [From.GetName] has accepted. 'Exit Permits for Soviet Germans' is no longer a proposal but policy - and the ministries in Bonn now have to make it work."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.121.t:0 "Exit Permits for Soviet Germans: Agreed"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.122.a:0 "Then not - for now."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.122.desc:0 "The ambassador's report is courteous and unambiguous: [From.GetName] will not accept 'Exit Permits for Soviet Germans'. In the Foreign Office the desk officers file the draft away - for another occasion, another approach, or another government."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.122.t:0 "Exit Permits for Soviet Germans: Refused"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.130.a:0 "We come to Bonn."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.130.b:0 "The time is not right."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.130.desc:0 "The ambassador of the Federal Republic has asked for an urgent appointment and delivers a proposal from Bonn. Bonn invites the Soviet leader for a state visit and proposes a joint declaration: the right of all peoples and states to determine their own fate, freely.\n\nThe cabinet must weigh what the Germans offer against what saying yes would mean - at home, with our neighbours and with our allies."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.130.t:0 "The Bonn Declaration"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.131.a:0 "A good day for German diplomacy."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.131.desc:0 "The answer arrives by diplomatic cable, sooner than the Foreign Office expected: [From.GetName] has accepted. 'The Bonn Declaration' is no longer a proposal but policy - and the ministries in Bonn now have to make it work."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.131.t:0 "The Bonn Declaration: Agreed"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.132.a:0 "Then not - for now."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.132.desc:0 "The ambassador's report is courteous and unambiguous: [From.GetName] will not accept 'The Bonn Declaration'. In the Foreign Office the desk officers file the draft away - for another occasion, another approach, or another government."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.132.t:0 "The Bonn Declaration: Refused"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.140.a:0 "We open the border."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.140.b:0 "We will not anger East Berlin."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.140.desc:0 "The ambassador of the Federal Republic has asked for an urgent appointment and delivers a proposal from Bonn. Bonn offers a credit of 500 million marks and asks Budapest to let the East German refugees in Hungary leave for the West.\n\nThe cabinet must weigh what the Germans offer against what saying yes would mean - at home, with our neighbours and with our allies."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.140.t:0 "The Hungarian Door"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.141.a:0 "A good day for German diplomacy."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.141.desc:0 "The answer arrives by diplomatic cable, sooner than the Foreign Office expected: [From.GetName] has accepted. 'The Hungarian Door' is no longer a proposal but policy - and the ministries in Bonn now have to make it work."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.141.t:0 "The Hungarian Door: Agreed"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.142.a:0 "Then not - for now."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.142.desc:0 "The ambassador's report is courteous and unambiguous: [From.GetName] will not accept 'The Hungarian Door'. In the Foreign Office the desk officers file the draft away - for another occasion, another approach, or another government."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.142.t:0 "The Hungarian Door: Refused"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.150.a:0 "China welcomes the Federal Republic."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.150.b:0 "Bonn is too close to Washington."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.150.desc:0 "The ambassador of the Federal Republic has asked for an urgent appointment and delivers a proposal from Bonn. The Federal Republic proposes diplomatic relations and a trade agreement. Beijing sees a counterweight to Moscow in Europe.\n\nThe cabinet must weigh what the Germans offer against what saying yes would mean - at home, with our neighbours and with our allies."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.150.t:0 "Diplomatic Relations with Bonn"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.151.a:0 "A good day for German diplomacy."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.151.desc:0 "The answer arrives by diplomatic cable, sooner than the Foreign Office expected: [From.GetName] has accepted. 'Diplomatic Relations with Bonn' is no longer a proposal but policy - and the ministries in Bonn now have to make it work."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.151.t:0 "Diplomatic Relations with Bonn: Agreed"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.152.a:0 "Then not - for now."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.152.desc:0 "The ambassador's report is courteous and unambiguous: [From.GetName] will not accept 'Diplomatic Relations with Bonn'. In the Foreign Office the desk officers file the draft away - for another occasion, another approach, or another government."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.152.t:0 "Diplomatic Relations with Bonn: Refused"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.160.a:0 "Agreed."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.160.b:0 "Our trade policy is our own."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.160.desc:0 "The ambassador of the Federal Republic has asked for an urgent appointment and delivers a proposal from Bonn. Bonn proposes regular government consultations with Tokyo on trade, currency and technology.\n\nThe cabinet must weigh what the Germans offer against what saying yes would mean - at home, with our neighbours and with our allies."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.160.t:0 "A German-Japanese Consultation"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.161.a:0 "A good day for German diplomacy."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.161.desc:0 "The answer arrives by diplomatic cable, sooner than the Foreign Office expected: [From.GetName] has accepted. 'A German-Japanese Consultation' is no longer a proposal but policy - and the ministries in Bonn now have to make it work."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.161.t:0 "A German-Japanese Consultation: Agreed"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.162.a:0 "Then not - for now."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.162.desc:0 "The ambassador's report is courteous and unambiguous: [From.GetName] will not accept 'A German-Japanese Consultation'. In the Foreign Office the desk officers file the draft away - for another occasion, another approach, or another government."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.162.t:0 "A German-Japanese Consultation: Refused"
 COLDWAR_GDIP.170.a:0 "India accepts."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.170.b:0 "We prefer Soviet terms."
 COLDWAR_GDIP.170.desc:0 "The ambassador of the Federal Republic has asked for an urgent appointment and delivers a proposal from Bonn. Bonn offers a long-term development partnership: capital aid, technical universities and industrial cooperation.\n\nThe cabinet must weigh what the Germans offer against what saying yes would mean - at home, with our neighbours and with our allies."

 COLDWAR_GDOM.1.a:0 "We have the two thirds. Pass it."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.1.b:0 "Pay the opposition's price for its votes."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.1.b.tt:0 "The opposition votes with us - and takes the credit (§Y75§! political power, the largest opposition party §R+1%§!)."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.1.c:0 "Without two thirds it cannot pass. Let it fall."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.1.desc:0 "The government asks the Bundestag to add national referendums and citizens' initiatives to the Basic Law. The Union warns of demagogues, the Greens cheer, the constitutional lawyers quote Weimar.\n\nAn amendment to the Basic Law needs two thirds of the Bundestag and of the Bundesrat."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.1.t:0 "Referendums in the Basic Law"
 COLDWAR_GDOM.10.a:0 "Citizenship by birth and dual citizenship."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.10.b:0 "Citizenship by birth - but choose one passport at 23."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.10.c:0 "Withdraw the bill."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.10.desc:0 "The government's citizenship reform reaches the Bundestag. In Hesse the Union collects signatures 'against dual citizenship' - and wins an election with them."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.10.t:0 "Two Passports?"
 COLDWAR_GDOM.11.a:0 "Pass the amnesty law."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.11.a.tt:0 "The FDP's own deputies might revolt - and the public will not forget."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.11.b:0 "Let the prosecutors do their work."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.11.desc:0 "Prosecutors want to charge Otto Graf Lambsdorff and Hans Friderichs with corruption. The parties' leaders have prepared a quiet way out: an amnesty for all illegal party donations of the past."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.11.t:0 "Cultivating the Political Landscape"
 COLDWAR_GDOM.2.a:0 "We have the two thirds. Pass it."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.2.b:0 "Pay the opposition's price for its votes."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.2.b.tt:0 "The opposition votes with us - and takes the credit (§Y75§! political power, the largest opposition party §R+1%§!)."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.2.c:0 "Without two thirds it cannot pass. Let it fall."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.2.desc:0 "The Bundestag debates a direct election of the Federal President by the people. Critics fear a 'substitute emperor'; supporters a closer bond between citizens and the state.\n\nAn amendment to the Basic Law needs two thirds of the Bundestag and of the Bundesrat."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.2.t:0 "Direct Election of the Federal President"
 COLDWAR_GDOM.3.a:0 "The Nordstaat: Hamburg, Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony together."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.3.b:0 "Only the small ones: the Saarland joins Rhineland-Palatinate."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.3.c:0 "The Länder have spoken. Leave the map as it is."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.3.desc:0 "The Ernst Commission's report lies on the table. Every option needs referendums in the Länder concerned - and the Bundesrat, where the Länder sit, must agree to its own abolition."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.3.t:0 "The Länder Reform"
 COLDWAR_GDOM.4.a:0 "We have the two thirds. Pass it."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.4.b:0 "Pay the opposition's price for its votes."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.4.b.tt:0 "The opposition votes with us - and takes the credit (§Y75§! political power, the largest opposition party §R+1%§!)."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.4.c:0 "Without two thirds it cannot pass. Let it fall."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.4.desc:0 "The coalition proposes to bind every use of the emergency laws to the Federal Constitutional Court and the Bundesrat.\n\nAn amendment to the Basic Law needs two thirds of the Bundestag and of the Bundesrat."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.4.t:0 "Tying the Emergency Constitution"
 COLDWAR_GDOM.5.a:0 "Pass it. Two parties are enough for Germany."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.5.b:0 "Withdraw it. The price is too high."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.5.desc:0 "The bill for a first-past-the-post system is before the Bundestag. The FDP calls it 'political murder', the small parties take to the streets, and the constitutional lawyers argue whether the Basic Law allows it at all."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.5.t:0 "The Majority Vote"
 COLDWAR_GDOM.6.a:0 "We have the two thirds. Pass it."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.6.b:0 "Pay the opposition's price for its votes."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.6.b.tt:0 "The opposition votes with us - and takes the credit (§Y75§! political power, the largest opposition party §R+1%§!)."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.6.c:0 "Without two thirds it cannot pass. Let it fall."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.6.desc:0 "The coalition wants to write the period solution into the Basic Law itself. The churches call for resistance.\n\nAn amendment to the Basic Law needs two thirds of the Bundestag and of the Bundesrat."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.6.t:0 "Overruling Karlsruhe"
 COLDWAR_GDOM.7.a:0 "We accept the ruling. An indications solution it is."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.7.b:0 "Amend the Basic Law to overrule the court."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.7.desc:0 "February 1975: the Federal Constitutional Court strikes down the period solution. The state has a duty to protect unborn life, the judges rule - two of them dissent sharply."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.7.t:0 "Karlsruhe on Paragraph 218"
 COLDWAR_GDOM.8.a:0 "The period solution."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.8.a.tt:0 "Bavaria and the Union will go to the §YConstitutional Court§!."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.8.b:0 "The indications solution."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.8.c:0 "Keep the old law."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.8.desc:0 "The Bundestag must choose between a period solution (no punishment in the first twelve weeks) and an indications solution (only for medical, ethical or social reasons). The churches, the women's movement and the Union all mobilise."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.8.t:0 "The Abortion Law"
 COLDWAR_GDOM.9.a:0 "A new census law with strict data protection."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.9.b:0 "Count them anyway - with fines for boycotters."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.9.desc:0 "December 1983: the Constitutional Court halts the census and invents a new basic right, 'informational self-determination'. The government must decide how to count its citizens - and how much to know about them."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.9.t:0 "The Census Boycott"
 COLDWAR_GDOM.90.a:0 "The people have spoken."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.90.desc:0 "The government's proposal wins the referendum. The opposition accepts the result - it has little choice."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.90.t:0 "The People Say Yes"
 COLDWAR_GDOM.91.a:0 "We accept the verdict."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.91.desc:0 "The referendum is lost. Commentators ask whether a chancellor who loses a vote on his own question can still govern."
 COLDWAR_GDOM.91.t:0 "The People Say No"
 COLDWAR_GER.1.a:0 "Dare more democracy."
 COLDWAR_GER.1.desc:0 "Twenty years after its founding the Federal Republic has, for the first time, a chancellor from the Social Democrats. Willy Brandt governs with Walter Scheel's Free Democrats and a majority of twelve seats - a majority that defections could erase in a single afternoon.\n\nIn the East stands a second German state that Bonn does not recognise. In the universities the revolt of 1968 is splitting into reform, sects and the first underground cells. And the economic miracle is slowing down."
 COLDWAR_GER.1.t:0 "The Social-Liberal Coalition"
 COLDWAR_GER.100.a:0 "ok"
 COLDWAR_GER.101.a:0 "Accept the resignations."
 COLDWAR_GER.101.b:0 "Sit it out."
 COLDWAR_GER.101.desc:0 "The Flick concern has paid millions to the parties through 'charitable' channels - and received tax relief on the sale of its Daimler shares. An accountant's notes say 'cultivating the political landscape'. The economics minister is indicted."
 COLDWAR_GER.101.t:0 "The Flick Affair"
 COLDWAR_GER.102.a:0 "Accept the resignations."
 COLDWAR_GER.102.b:0 "Sit it out."
 COLDWAR_GER.102.desc:0 "Lockheed is said to have paid bribes across the Western world to sell its aircraft - in Bonn, the name of the defence ministry of the Starfighter years keeps appearing."
 COLDWAR_GER.102.t:0 "The Lockheed Affair"
 COLDWAR_GER.103.a:0 "Accept the resignations."
 COLDWAR_GER.103.b:0 "Sit it out."
 COLDWAR_GER.103.desc:0 "A Land campaign has been run with a spy, a detective and an anonymous tax complaint against the opposition candidate. The minister-president gives his 'word of honour' - and is found dead in a Geneva hotel bathtub a few weeks later."
 COLDWAR_GER.103.t:0 "Waterkant Gate"
 COLDWAR_GER.104.a:0 "The unions must clean house."
 COLDWAR_GER.104.b:0 "A matter for the courts."
 COLDWAR_GER.104.desc:0 "The trade unions' housing company, the largest in Europe, has been run by managers who enriched themselves at the tenants' expense. The DGB's credibility is in tatters."
 COLDWAR_GER.104.t:0 "Neue Heimat"
 COLDWAR_GER.105.a:0 "Accept the resignations."
 COLDWAR_GER.105.b:0 "Sit it out."
 COLDWAR_GER.105.desc:0 "Cash in suitcases, accounts in Switzerland, donors whose names the former chancellor refuses to reveal because he has given his 'word of honour'. The party donations affair shakes the Union to its foundations."
 COLDWAR_GER.105.t:0 "Black Accounts"
 COLDWAR_GER.106.a:0 "Accept the resignations."
 COLDWAR_GER.106.b:0 "Sit it out."
 COLDWAR_GER.106.desc:0 "A minister's travel expenses, a state secretary's consultancy contracts, a party treasurer's memory gaps: Bonn has another affair. The magazines are delighted."
 COLDWAR_GER.106.t:0 "A Bonn Affair"
 COLDWAR_GER.110.a:0 "The road to the euro is open."
 COLDWAR_GER.110.b:0 "Europe stalls. The D-Mark remains."
 COLDWAR_GER.110.desc1:0 "Fifty-one percent. France has said yes to the Treaty on European Union by the narrowest margin. The single currency will come - and the Bundesbank's rules will come with it."
 COLDWAR_GER.110.desc2:0 "Non. French voters have rejected the Maastricht Treaty. Mitterrand's European project is in ruins; in Frankfurt, nobody is entirely unhappy."
 COLDWAR_GER.110.t:0 "France Votes on Maastricht"
 COLDWAR_GER.120.a:0 "Protest through the Western Allies."
 COLDWAR_GER.120.b:0 "Pay a higher transit lump sum."
 COLDWAR_GER.120.desc:0 "East German border guards hold up lorries for hours on the Helmstedt autobahn; a family is arrested for 'transit abuse'. The road to West Berlin is again a lever in someone else's hand."
 COLDWAR_GER.120.t:0 "Trouble on the Transit Routes"
 COLDWAR_GER.130.a:0 "Take them all in. They are Germans."
 COLDWAR_GER.130.b:0 "Quiet diplomacy. Do not destabilise the East."
 COLDWAR_GER.130.desc:0 "East Germans are leaving through every crack in the Iron Curtain: through Hungary, through the embassy in Prague, through the permanent mission in East Berlin. Reception camps in Gießen and Marienfelde overflow.\n\nGDR crisis index: §Y[?DDR.cwddr_crisis|0]§!"
 COLDWAR_GER.130.t:0 "The Exodus"
 COLDWAR_GER.131.a:0 "Sanctions against the regime."
 COLDWAR_GER.131.b:0 "Keep the channels open - for the prisoners' sake."
 COLDWAR_GER.131.desc:0 "The pictures smuggled out are blurred but unmistakable: armoured vehicles, water cannon, men with truncheons in front of the opera house. The GDR has chosen the Chinese solution."
 COLDWAR_GER.131.t:0 "Massacre in Leipzig"

 COLDWAR_GER.134.a:0 "Continue."
 COLDWAR_GER.135.a:0 "Continue."
 COLDWAR_GER.137.a:0 "Continue."

 COLDWAR_GER.141.a:0 "Continue."

 COLDWAR_GER.143.a:0 "Continue."
 COLDWAR_GER.145.a:0 "Continue."
 COLDWAR_GER.150.a:0 "A new Germany in Europe."
 COLDWAR_GER.150.desc:0 "At midnight the flag of the Federal Republic rises in front of the Reichstag. Germany, divided since 1945, is a single state again - and the largest country in Western Europe."
 COLDWAR_GER.150.t:0 "Germany Is United"
 COLDWAR_GER.19.a:0 "Count every vote."
 COLDWAR_GER.19.desc:0 "Deputies are leaving the coalition, or the arithmetic of the last election never quite worked. The opposition smells a constructive vote of no confidence. The whips have weeks, not months.\n\nGovernment §Y[?cwger_seats_gov|0]§! of §Y[?cwger_seats_total|0]§! seats, majority §Y[?cwger_majority|0]§!, defectors §Y[?cwger_defectors|0]§!."
 COLDWAR_GER.19.t:0 "The Majority Is Crumbling"
 COLDWAR_GER.20.a:0 "Fight for every vote."
 COLDWAR_GER.20.b:0 "Ask for confidence and lose it - let the voters decide."
 COLDWAR_GER.20.desc:0 "The opposition has tabled a motion under Article 67 of the Basic Law: it does not merely want to bring down the chancellor, it names a successor. The government's majority has melted to almost nothing. Whips count, recount and visit wavering deputies at home."
 COLDWAR_GER.20.t:0 "Constructive Vote of No Confidence"
 COLDWAR_GER.21.a:0 "A narrow escape."
 COLDWAR_GER.21.desc:0 "The opposition candidate falls two votes short. Bonn whispers that the votes were not all found by persuasion alone - years later it will turn out that the Ministry for State Security paid at least one deputy. For now, the government survives."
 COLDWAR_GER.21.t:0 "The Motion Fails"
 COLDWAR_GER.22.a:0 "The opposition takes over."
 COLDWAR_GER.22.desc:0 "The motion carries. Without an election, without a coalition agreement worth the name, the Federal Republic has a new head of government - the first time Article 67 has worked as its authors intended."
 COLDWAR_GER.22.t:0 "A New Chancellor"
 COLDWAR_GER.23.a:0 "To the voters."
 COLDWAR_GER.23.desc:0 "The chancellor has asked for the confidence of the house and, as arranged, not received it. The Federal President dissolves the Bundestag. The campaign begins at once."
 COLDWAR_GER.23.t:0 "The Bundestag Is Dissolved"
 COLDWAR_GER.24.a:0 "Keep the coalition the parties have agreed on."
 COLDWAR_GER.24.b:0 "A social-liberal coalition."
 COLDWAR_GER.24.c:0 "A Christian-liberal coalition."
 COLDWAR_GER.24.d:0 "A grand coalition under the Union."
 COLDWAR_GER.24.desc:0 "The votes are counted. In Bonn nobody governs alone: the parties above the five-percent hurdle sit down to divide ministries and principles. Who governs with whom depends on arithmetic - and on where the Free Democrats think their future lies.\n\nSeat shares: social-liberal §Y[?cwger_q_sl|%0]§!, Christian-liberal §Y[?cwger_q_cl|%0]§!, grand coalition §Y[?cwger_q_gc|%0]§!, red-green §Y[?cwger_q_rg|%0]§!."
 COLDWAR_GER.24.e:0 "A grand coalition under the SPD."
 COLDWAR_GER.24.f:0 "Red-green."
 COLDWAR_GER.24.t:0 "Coalition Talks"
 COLDWAR_GER.25.a:0 "The Länder have spoken."
 COLDWAR_GER.25.desc:0 "A state election turns into a referendum on Bonn. The federal government's parties lose ground, as governing parties usually do between Bundestag elections - and with it, perhaps, a vote in the Bundesrat."
 COLDWAR_GER.25.t:0 "Landtag Elections"
 COLDWAR_GER.26.a:0 "Keep the social-liberal coalition in office."
 COLDWAR_GER.26.b:0 "Let them go. We govern alone."
 COLDWAR_GER.26.c:0 "Concede on the budget."
 COLDWAR_GER.26.d:0 "The FDP switches sides."
 COLDWAR_GER.26.desc:0 "The economics minister has put his demands in writing: cuts to welfare, lower taxes on business, less state. The SPD calls it a divorce letter. The Free Democrats are looking across the aisle."
 COLDWAR_GER.26.t:0 "The Lambsdorff Paper"
 COLDWAR_GER.28.a:0 "Keep Brandt in office while the security failure is investigated."
 COLDWAR_GER.28.b:0 "The chancellor takes responsibility and resigns."
 COLDWAR_GER.28.desc:0 "Günter Guillaume, the chancellor's personal aide, has been arrested. He is an officer of the Ministry for State Security and has read everything that crossed the desk, including NATO papers on holiday in Norway. 'I am an officer of the National People's Army,' he tells the arresting officers."
 COLDWAR_GER.28.t:0 "The Spy in the Chancellery"
 COLDWAR_GER.29.a:0 "Good work, Cologne."
 COLDWAR_GER.29.desc:0 "Counter-intelligence has identified an aide in the Chancellery who receives coded radio messages from the East. He is quietly removed months before he could read anything that matters."
 COLDWAR_GER.29.t:0 "A Spy Caught Early"
 COLDWAR_GER.30.a:0 "Retain Barzel as chairman for now."
 COLDWAR_GER.30.b:0 "Helmut Kohl leads the party."
 COLDWAR_GER.30.c:0 "Strauß is the strongest man the Union has."
 COLDWAR_GER.30.desc:0 "The Union has lost the 1972 election badly. Rainer Barzel resigns the chairmanship. The 43-year-old minister-president of Rhineland-Palatinate, Helmut Kohl, wants the party - but Franz Josef Strauß wants the candidacy."
 COLDWAR_GER.30.t:0 "A New Chairman for the CDU"
 COLDWAR_GER.31.a:0 "Kohl remains the Union's candidate."
 COLDWAR_GER.31.b:0 "Strauß. The CSU gets its candidate."
 COLDWAR_GER.31.c:0 "Albrecht. The CDU decides."
 COLDWAR_GER.31.desc:0 "Who will be the Union's candidate for chancellor? The CDU's young modernisers favour Ernst Albrecht of Lower Saxony. The CSU will accept no one but Franz Josef Strauß. Kohl, the chairman, waits."
 COLDWAR_GER.31.t:0 "The K-Question"
 COLDWAR_GER.32.a:0 "Reconcile. The joint group is restored."
 COLDWAR_GER.32.b:0 "Let them go. A fourth party."
 COLDWAR_GER.32.desc:0 "After another lost election the CSU's deputies vote in Wildbad Kreuth to leave the joint parliamentary group. Strauß wants a fourth party that competes in every state. Kohl threatens to found a CDU branch in Bavaria."
 COLDWAR_GER.32.t:0 "Wildbad Kreuth"
 COLDWAR_GER.34.a:0 "Brandt remains chancellor."
 COLDWAR_GER.34.b:0 "Schmidt takes over."
 COLDWAR_GER.34.desc:0 "Willy Brandt has led the government through the treaties with the East. The party debates whether he should remain in office or hand the chancellorship to Helmut Schmidt."
 COLDWAR_GER.34.t:0 "The Chancellor's Succession"
 COLDWAR_GER.35.a:0 "Open Treaty 9 negotiations."
 COLDWAR_GER.35.a.tt:0 "custom_effect_tooltip = COLDWAR_GER_1970_tt_confed_open"
 COLDWAR_GER.35.b:0 "Leave the proposal under review."
 COLDWAR_GER.35.desc:0 "East Berlin has asked Bonn to open the existing Treaty Community negotiation. The request does not establish a confederation; both governments retain their existing treaty choices and ratification process."
 COLDWAR_GER.35.t:0 "East Berlin Requests Treaty Community Talks"
 COLDWAR_GER.36.a:0 "Innovation and justice."
 COLDWAR_GER.36.desc:0 "Oskar Lafontaine chairs the party, but Gerhard Schröder wins Lower Saxony with an absolute majority. Lafontaine steps aside: the SPD's candidate for chancellor is the man who once rattled the gates of the Chancellery and shouted 'I want in there!'"
 COLDWAR_GER.36.t:0 "The Candidate from Lower Saxony"
 COLDWAR_GER.37.a:0 "Kohl remains chairman."
 COLDWAR_GER.37.b:0 "Späth takes over."
 COLDWAR_GER.37.desc:0 "The Union is far behind in the polls. Heiner Geißler, Rita Süssmuth and Lothar Späth prepare to challenge Helmut Kohl at the Bremen party congress. Kohl has spent the summer on the telephone."
 COLDWAR_GER.37.t:0 "Bremen Party Congress"
 COLDWAR_GER.38.a:0 "Lafontaine continues as the candidate."
 COLDWAR_GER.38.b:0 "Johannes Rau steps in as candidate."
 COLDWAR_GER.38.desc:0 "At a campaign event in Cologne-Mülheim a mentally ill woman stabs Oskar Lafontaine in the neck with a knife. He survives by millimetres."
 COLDWAR_GER.38.t:0 "Attack in Cologne"
 COLDWAR_GER.40.a:0 "The treaty stands, and so does the claim to unity."
 COLDWAR_GER.40.b:0 "Criticise Munich for the lawsuit."
 COLDWAR_GER.40.desc:0 "Bavaria has sued against the Basic Treaty. The Federal Constitutional Court upholds it - but declares that the German Reich continues to exist in law, that the Federal Republic is identical with it, and that the inner-German border is a border like that between Länder of the Federal Republic."
 COLDWAR_GER.40.t:0 "Karlsruhe Rules on the Basic Treaty"
 COLDWAR_GER.49.a:0 "The search goes on."
 COLDWAR_GER.49.desc:0 "Police have raided a conspiratorial flat and arrested members of an armed group. Weapons, forged passports and plans for further attacks were found.\n\nRAF prisoners: §Y[?cwger_raf_prisoners|0]§! | active cadre: §Y[?cwger_raf_cadre|0]§!"
 COLDWAR_GER.49.t:0 "Arrests in the Underground"
 COLDWAR_GER.50.a:0 "A high-security trial in Stammheim."
 COLDWAR_GER.50.b:0 "Ordinary prisons, ordinary courts."
 COLDWAR_GER.50.desc:0 "The founders of the Red Army Faction are in prison. Outside, a new generation recruited from the support committees has one goal above all others: to free them."
 COLDWAR_GER.50.t:0 "The Second Generation"
 COLDWAR_GER.51.a:0 "Find the perpetrators."
 COLDWAR_GER.51.b:0 "No panic. The state will not be provoked."
 COLDWAR_GER.51.desc1:0 "Bombs at a US Army headquarters, a police station and a publishing house. The 'May Offensive' of the Red Army Faction kills four people and injures dozens. A letter claims the attacks for the 'Commando Petra Schelm'."
 COLDWAR_GER.51.desc2:0 "An explosive device has gone off at a military installation used by the Americans. The commando's letter names the Federal Republic an 'outpost of US imperialism' and demands the release of the prisoners."
 COLDWAR_GER.51.t:0 "Bomb Attack"
 COLDWAR_GER.52.a:0 "A state funeral. The republic will not bow."
 COLDWAR_GER.52.b:0 "Give the crisis staff what it needs."
 COLDWAR_GER.52.desc1:0 "A motorcycle pulls alongside a car at a traffic light. The Federal Prosecutor General and his driver die in a burst of automatic fire. The RAF calls it an 'execution'."
 COLDWAR_GER.52.desc2:0 "A sophisticated bomb triggered by a light barrier has killed one of the country's leading managers on his way to work. The third generation of the RAF strikes rarely - and with terrible precision. Investigators find almost nothing."
 COLDWAR_GER.52.t:0 "Assassination"
 COLDWAR_GER.53.a:0 "Exchange the prisoners."
 COLDWAR_GER.53.b:0 "The state does not yield."
 COLDWAR_GER.53.desc:0 "A convoy has been ambushed, the escorts shot, a prominent figure dragged into a car. The kidnappers demand the release of imprisoned comrades and an aircraft to a country of their choosing. The government forms a crisis staff."
 COLDWAR_GER.53.t:0 "Kidnapping"
 COLDWAR_GER.54.a:0 "The crisis staff takes over."
 COLDWAR_GER.54.desc1:0 "A commando of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine has hijacked a Lufthansa jet with 86 passengers to support the kidnappers' demands. The aircraft is hopping across the Mediterranean towards the Horn of Africa. The captain will be shot if the deadline passes."
 COLDWAR_GER.54.desc2:0 "The kidnappers have set a final deadline. Investigators believe they know the district where the hostage is held, but not the house."
 COLDWAR_GER.54.t:0 "The Ultimatum"
 COLDWAR_GER.55.a:0 "The state has proven itself."
 COLDWAR_GER.55.desc:0 "Shortly after midnight the commandos storm. Within minutes it is over: the hostages are free, the kidnappers dead or captured. 'Die Arbeit ist erledigt' - the job is done."
 COLDWAR_GER.55.t:0 "The Rescue"
 COLDWAR_GER.56.a:0 "The state could not yield."
 COLDWAR_GER.56.desc:0 "The body is found in the boot of a car. The commando's letter is three lines long. The crisis staff's strategy of firmness has cost a life, as everyone knew it might."
 COLDWAR_GER.56.t:0 "The Hostage Is Dead"
 COLDWAR_GER.57.a:0 "The official account stands."
 COLDWAR_GER.57.b:0 "An independent inquiry."
 COLDWAR_GER.57.desc:0 "The morning after, the leaders of the first generation are found dead or dying in their cells on the seventh floor of Stammheim prison. The authorities speak of suicide; the sympathisers of murder. The German Autumn is over - but it has changed the republic."
 COLDWAR_GER.57.t:0 "Death Night in Stammheim"
 COLDWAR_GER.58.a:0 "Rebuild the dragnet."
 COLDWAR_GER.58.b:0 "Offer a way out to those who want one."
 COLDWAR_GER.58.desc:0 "Nobody knows who they are. They leave no fingerprints, use no flats the police know, and strike the representatives of what they call the 'military-industrial complex'. The RAF has become a phantom."
 COLDWAR_GER.58.t:0 "The Third Generation"
 COLDWAR_GER.59.a:0 "Force-feeding. The law will be enforced."
 COLDWAR_GER.59.b:0 "Small concessions: shared yards, visits."
 COLDWAR_GER.59.desc:0 "The prisoners demand to be held together as prisoners of war. They refuse food. Holger Meins weighed 39 kilos when he died in 1974. Each day of the strike brings new sympathisers onto the streets."
 COLDWAR_GER.59.t:0 "Hunger Strike"
 COLDWAR_GER.60.a:0 "History will judge them."
 COLDWAR_GER.60.desc:0 "A typed letter of eight pages arrives at Reuters: 'Almost 28 years ago, on 14 May 1970, the RAF was born in a liberation action. Today we end this project.' The Red Army Faction is history."
 COLDWAR_GER.60.t:0 "The RAF Dissolves"
 COLDWAR_GER.61.a:0 "A catastrophe for the security services."
 COLDWAR_GER.61.desc:0 "An operation at a railway station in Mecklenburg was supposed to arrest two RAF members betrayed by an informant. A GSG 9 officer and a suspect are dead. Witnesses say the suspect was executed on the tracks. The Interior Minister and the Federal Prosecutor resign."
 COLDWAR_GER.61.t:0 "Bad Kleinen"
 COLDWAR_GER.62.a:0 "Ban the organisations behind it."
 COLDWAR_GER.62.b:0 "The work of isolated individuals."
 COLDWAR_GER.62.desc1:0 "A pipe bomb in a crowd. The perpetrator was a member of a 'military sports group' that trained in the woods with Wehrmacht surplus while the authorities spoke of hobbyists."
 COLDWAR_GER.62.desc2:0 "Petrol bombs through the window of a house where Turkish families live. Three dead, among them children. In other towns crowds applaud as hostels for asylum seekers burn."
 COLDWAR_GER.62.t:0 "Right-Wing Terror"
 COLDWAR_GER.65.a:0 "Hunt down the network."
 COLDWAR_GER.65.b:0 "Quiet diplomacy with the sponsors."
 COLDWAR_GER.65.desc1:0 "Palestinian and international commandos use West German soil as a battlefield: an attack at an airport, a bomb in a Jewish community centre. The trail leads to Beirut, Baghdad and Damascus."
 COLDWAR_GER.65.desc2:0 "A bomb in a Berlin discotheque frequented by American soldiers. Intercepted cables from the Libyan People's Bureau in East Berlin speak of a 'joyful event'."
 COLDWAR_GER.65.desc3:0 "PKK militants occupy consulates and set fire to Turkish businesses across the country. Ankara demands a ban."
 COLDWAR_GER.65.t:0 "International Terrorism"
 COLDWAR_GER.66.a:0 "This must never happen again."
 COLDWAR_GER.66.desc:0 "Members of Black September have broken into the Israeli team's quarters in the Olympic Village. Two athletes are dead, nine are hostages. The night ends at Fürstenfeldbruck airfield with all nine hostages dead after a botched rescue by Bavarian police with no special training and no radios.\n\n'The Games must go on,' says Avery Brundage."
 COLDWAR_GER.66.t:0 "Massacre in Munich"
 COLDWAR_GER.67.a:0 "Security planning paid off."
 COLDWAR_GER.67.desc:0 "Plain-clothes officers in the Olympic Village notice men in tracksuits climbing the fence at four in the morning. The attack on the Israeli team is stopped before it begins."
 COLDWAR_GER.67.t:0 "A Plot Foiled"
 COLDWAR_GER.70.a:0 "ok"
 COLDWAR_GER.71.a:0 "A quiet trial and a quiet exchange later."
 COLDWAR_GER.71.b:0 "A public trial. Everyone should know."
 COLDWAR_GER.71.desc:0 "The Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution has arrested an official who has passed files to the Ministry for State Security for years. The radio messages, the microdots, the dead drops on the Rhine promenade - all in the arrest report."
 COLDWAR_GER.71.t:0 "A Mole Unmasked"
 COLDWAR_GER.72.a:0 "Damage control in Brussels."
 COLDWAR_GER.72.b:0 "Blame the previous government."
 COLDWAR_GER.72.desc:0 "Material from the defence ministry has turned up in the files of the Warsaw Pact: deployment plans, codes, the timetable of the next exercise. Somewhere in Bonn sits a source the services have not found."
 COLDWAR_GER.72.t:0 "NATO Plans in East Berlin"
 COLDWAR_GER.73.a:0 "Tighten the security vetting of staff."
 COLDWAR_GER.73.b:0 "Let the courts handle it."
 COLDWAR_GER.73.desc:0 "A secretary in the Foreign Office has fallen in love with a charming man from Düsseldorf who turns out to be a captain of the HVA. Her lover has vanished; the magazines have the pictures."
 COLDWAR_GER.73.t:0 "The Romeo Affair"
 COLDWAR_GER.74.a:0 "Roll up the network."
 COLDWAR_GER.74.b:0 "Keep him secret and feed the HVA false trails."
 COLDWAR_GER.74.desc:0 "An officer of the GDR's foreign intelligence has walked into a West German police station with two suitcases of files. Dozens of agents in the Federal Republic have names now."
 COLDWAR_GER.74.t:0 "A Defector from the HVA"
 COLDWAR_GER.75.a:0 "ok"
 COLDWAR_GER.76.a:0 "The interior minister resigns."
 COLDWAR_GER.76.b:0 "Security comes first."
 COLDWAR_GER.76.desc:0 "Der Spiegel reveals that the Office for the Protection of the Constitution broke into the flat of a nuclear scientist and bugged it - without a warrant, on the minister's say-so, because he once met a man who knew a terrorist."
 COLDWAR_GER.76.t:0 "The Traube Affair"
 COLDWAR_GER.77.a:0 "A parliamentary inquiry."
 COLDWAR_GER.77.b:0 "National security - no comment."
 COLDWAR_GER.77.desc:0 "Eight years ago the secret service blew a hole in the wall of Celle prison and blamed the RAF - to smuggle an informant into the scene. Now a reporter has the files."
 COLDWAR_GER.77.t:0 "The Celle Hole"
 COLDWAR_GER.78.a:0 "Accept the resignation and rehabilitate the general."
 COLDWAR_GER.78.b:0 "Keep the minister."
 COLDWAR_GER.78.desc:0 "The Military Counter-Intelligence Service has driven a four-star general out of office on the strength of rumours from a Cologne bar. The rumours were false. The defence minister offers to resign."
 COLDWAR_GER.78.t:0 "The Kießling Affair"
 COLDWAR_GER.80.a:0 "Car-free Sundays and a speed limit."
 COLDWAR_GER.80.b:0 "An energy programme: coal and nuclear."
 COLDWAR_GER.80.c:0 "Let prices do the work."
 COLDWAR_GER.80.desc:0 "The Arab oil producers have cut their output and the price of crude has quadrupled. The Federal Republic imports almost all of its oil. The government orders car-free Sundays; children ride their bicycles down the empty Autobahn."
 COLDWAR_GER.80.t:0 "The Oil Shock"
 COLDWAR_GER.81.a:0 "Austerity."
 COLDWAR_GER.81.b:0 "A stimulus programme."
 COLDWAR_GER.81.desc:0 "Revolution in Iran, war between Iran and Iraq: the oil price doubles again. Unemployment passes one million for the first time since the fifties, and the deficit grows."
 COLDWAR_GER.81.t:0 "The Second Oil Shock"
 COLDWAR_GER.82.a:0 "Mediate: 38.5 hours, flexibly arranged."
 COLDWAR_GER.82.b:0 "Support the lockouts."
 COLDWAR_GER.82.desc:0 "IG Metall has called the biggest industrial action in the Federal Republic's history. The employers answer with lockouts. 'Work for all, shorter hours' against 'the German model is being destroyed'."
 COLDWAR_GER.82.t:0 "Strike for the 35-Hour Week"
 COLDWAR_GER.84.a:0 "Subsidise the steel works."
 COLDWAR_GER.84.b:0 "Restructure the Ruhr."
 COLDWAR_GER.84.desc:0 "Asian competition and overcapacity hit the Ruhr. Krupp wants to close Rheinhausen; workers occupy the Rhine bridge."
 COLDWAR_GER.84.t:0 "The Steel Crisis"
 COLDWAR_GER.85.a:0 "Accept the independence of the Bundesbank."
 COLDWAR_GER.85.b:0 "A public quarrel with Frankfurt."
 COLDWAR_GER.85.desc:0 "The Central Bank Council in Frankfurt has raised the discount rate against the express wishes of the government. Inflation, says the Bundesbank president, is the most unsocial tax of all."
 COLDWAR_GER.85.t:0 "The Bundesbank Says No"
 COLDWAR_GER.86.a:0 "Deliver anyway. Treaties are kept."
 COLDWAR_GER.86.b:0 "Bow to Washington."
 COLDWAR_GER.86.desc:0 "Washington has banned American firms and their licensees from supplying the Siberian gas pipeline. AEG, Mannesmann and their subcontractors face sanctions in the United States if they deliver the turbines Bonn has promised Moscow."
 COLDWAR_GER.86.t:0 "The Pipeline Embargo"
 COLDWAR_GER.90.a:0 "Dialogue with the movement."
 COLDWAR_GER.90.b:0 "Security policy is not made on the street."
 COLDWAR_GER.90.desc:0 "Three hundred thousand people fill the Bonn Hofgarten against the stationing of new American missiles. Heinrich Böll speaks, Petra Kelly speaks, so do SPD deputies. The chancellor's own party is marching against his policy."
 COLDWAR_GER.90.t:0 "The Hofgarten Demonstration"
 COLDWAR_GER.91.a:0 "Clear the site."
 COLDWAR_GER.91.b:0 "Halt construction until the courts decide."
 COLDWAR_GER.91.desc:0 "Tens of thousands march to the planned reactor site on the Elbe. Water cannon, helicopters, barbed wire. A 'civil war around a building site', the newspapers write."
 COLDWAR_GER.91.t:0 "Brokdorf"
 COLDWAR_GER.92.a:0 "Open the line to Moscow."
 COLDWAR_GER.92.b:0 "Stand firm with the alliance."
 COLDWAR_GER.92.desc:0 "A NATO command exercise has been followed by alarming Soviet reactions: aircraft on alert in East Germany, intelligence officers ordered to look for signs of a surprise attack. In Bonn the cabinet meets at night."
 COLDWAR_GER.92.t:0 "War Scare"
 COLDWAR_GER.93.a:0 "A new force in German politics."
 COLDWAR_GER.93.desc:0 "In Karlsruhe, environmentalists, pacifists, feminists, former Maoists and a few conservatives found a federal party: 'Die Grünen'. 'We are neither left nor right, we are in front.'"
 COLDWAR_GER.93.t:0 "The Greens Are Founded"
 COLDWAR_GER.94.a:0 "A new party on the right."
 COLDWAR_GER.94.desc:0 "Two CSU deputies, disgusted by the billion-mark credit for the GDR, found a party to the right of the Union. Franz Schönhuber, a former Waffen-SS man and television presenter, soon takes it over."
 COLDWAR_GER.94.t:0 "Die Republikaner"
 COLDWAR_GER.95.a:0 "Seek an asylum compromise."
 COLDWAR_GER.95.b:0 "Article 16 is not negotiable."
 COLDWAR_GER.95.desc:0 "More than four hundred thousand people apply for asylum in a single year - from Yugoslavia, Romania, Turkey and Africa. Municipalities run out of beds; tabloids run out of restraint. The right to asylum in Article 16 is unconditional - for now."
 COLDWAR_GER.95.t:0 "The Asylum Debate"
 COLDWAR_GER.96.a:0 "Create an environment ministry."
 COLDWAR_GER.96.b:0 "German reactors are safe."
 COLDWAR_GER.96.desc:0 "A reactor has exploded in the Ukraine. A radioactive cloud drifts over Bavaria; children are kept out of sandpits, lettuce is ploughed under, and the government takes days to give clear advice."
 COLDWAR_GER.96.t:0 "Chernobyl"
 COLDWAR_GER.97.a:0 "Filters for every power plant."
 COLDWAR_GER.97.b:0 "More research is needed."
 COLDWAR_GER.97.desc:0 "The forests are dying, says Der Spiegel: acid rain from coal power plants has damaged a third of the trees. The fear unites conservationists and conservative foresters."
 COLDWAR_GER.97.t:0 "Forest Dieback"
 COLDWAR_GER.98.a:0 "The Realos carry the vote."
 COLDWAR_GER.98.b:0 "The party leaves the coalition."
 COLDWAR_GER.98.desc:0 "The Greens' special congress on the Kosovo war. Outside, protesters scream 'warmonger'; inside, a paint bomb bursts the foreign minister's eardrum. Bleeding, he speaks anyway: 'Never again war - but also never again Auschwitz.'"
 COLDWAR_GER.98.t:0 "Bielefeld"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_africa_development:0 "Development Partnerships"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_africa_development_desc:0 "Wells in Mali, roads in Kenya, vocational schools in Togo, a hospital in Tanzania: German development partnerships span the continent. They are also part of a competition. In Mozambique, Angola and Ethiopia, the GDR's advisers train the police, the party and the secret service. In Africa, the inner-German conflict is fought with tractors and teachers."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_after_rostock:0 "Protect Refugees from Extremist Violence"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_after_rostock_desc:0 "Extremists exploit pressure on refugee accommodation to intimidate newcomers and turn neighbourhood disputes into political violence. The federal government must protect reception centres, enforce bans on violent organisations and support local police before threats become attacks. Civic solidarity matters, but the state must make its protection effective."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_agenda_reform:0 "Standort Deutschland"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_agenda_reform_desc:0 "High wages, high taxes, high social contributions and four million unemployed: in the 1990s the debate about Standort Deutschland - Germany as a place to do business - dominates every talk show. Companies threaten to move to Hungary or Alabama. The government must decide how much of the old Modell Deutschland it is willing to sacrifice to keep them."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_agenda_renewal:0 "An Agenda for Renewal"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_agenda_renewal_desc:0 "Unemployment benefit cut to one year, the trades opened, the job centres reformed from top to bottom: the hardest cuts to the welfare state the Federal Republic has ever seen - made by a Social Democrat. The economy will thank him in ten years. His party may not wait that long."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_airbus:0 "Airbus and Ariane"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_airbus_desc:0 "European champions where national ones failed: in Toulouse and Hamburg, the Airbus consortium builds airliners to challenge Boeing; in Kourou, in French Guiana, Ariane rockets launch European satellites. Germany pays a large share and gets a large share of the work. The rest of the world calls it subsidy. Europe calls it sovereignty."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_alliance_for_jobs:0 "The Alliance for Jobs"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_alliance_for_jobs_desc:0 "Unions, employers and the government around one table in the chancellery, as in the days of Concerted Action: wage restraint in exchange for training places, early retirement in exchange for new hiring. Everybody comes. Whether anybody gives is another matter."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_apartheid_sanctions:0 "Sanctions against Apartheid"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_apartheid_sanctions_desc:0 "Soweto, the state of emergency, the townships burning on the evening news: Bonn joins the European Community's sanctions against South Africa. No new investment, no iron and steel, no Krugerrands, no cooperation in nuclear matters. German companies have billions invested in the country. The government decides that some business is not worth having."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_arms_export_guidelines:0 "Arms Export Guidelines"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_arms_export_guidelines_desc:0 "No weapons into areas of tension: the guidelines of 1971 are strict - in principle. In practice every chancellor makes exceptions, for friends, for jobs, for strategic partners, and the exports quietly continue through licences, subsidiaries and partners abroad. The guidelines are a statement of conscience. Whether they are anything more depends on the government."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_army_of_unity:0 "Army of Unity"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_army_of_unity_desc:0 "The Bundeswehr takes over the National People's Army - an army trained for decades to fight it. The MiG-29 fighters are kept, the ships are sold, the tanks scrapped, and most of the officers dismissed. A few thousand East German soldiers are taken into the army of unity. For them, the citizen in uniform is a new idea; for the Bundeswehr, so are they."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_army_structure_3:0 "Army Structure 3"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_army_structure_3_desc:0 "Army Structure 3 reorganises the field army into thirty-three brigades in twelve divisions, every one of them assigned to NATO's command in war. More armour, more mechanised infantry, more mobility: the Bundeswehr is to be able to meet the Warsaw Pact's tank armies at the border rather than retreat to the Rhine."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_army_structure_4:0 "Army Structure 4"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_army_structure_4_desc:0 "Thirty-six brigades, smaller but heavier, with more tanks and fewer men in each, and territorial forces of reservists to defend the rear. Army Structure 4 is designed for a Warsaw Pact attack with little warning. It is also designed for a demographic problem that the planners already see coming: there will soon not be enough young men."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_army_structure_5:0 "Army Structure 5"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_army_structure_5_desc:0 "370,000 soldiers for the whole of Germany, as promised to Gorbachev in the Caucasus and written into the Two Plus Four Treaty. Fewer tanks, fewer divisions, and new crisis reaction forces for a world in which the threat no longer stands at the inner-German border. The Bundeswehr shrinks and changes its mission in the same decade. It is not sure what the mission is."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_art146_debate:0 "A New Constitution?"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_art146_debate_desc:0 "Article 146: the Basic Law shall cease to apply on the day on which a constitution freely adopted by the German people comes into force. The fathers of the Basic Law meant it for the day of unity. Draft a new constitution together, say the civil rights movements of the East and the left of the West. Join the Basic Law under Article 23, say Kohl and the Union - quickly, before the window closes."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_arte_channel:0 "A Channel for Europe"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_arte_channel_desc:0 "Kohl and Mitterrand agree on a television channel that belongs to neither nation: films without dubbing, documentaries at prime time, an evening programme for perhaps two per cent of the audience - and the conviction that two per cent of two nations is a beginning."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_asean_partners:0 "Partners in Southeast Asia"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_asean_partners_desc:0 "Five nations between Burma and the Philippines have formed a community to stand together against the Vietnamese advance and for their own prosperity. In 1980 the European Community signs a cooperation agreement with them - and German engineers follow the diplomats."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_asylum_compromise:0 "The Asylum Compromise"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_asylum_compromise_desc:0 "Rising asylum applications put reception centres, municipalities and the constitutional promise of protection under strain.
