 COLDWAR_GER_1970_recognise_croatia_desc:0 "Yugoslavia is falling apart, Serbian artillery is shelling Vukovar and Dubrovnik, and Genscher pushes the European Community to recognise Slovenia and Croatia as independent states. Paris and London are furious; they fear that recognition will fan the flames in Bosnia. A newly united Germany is accused of reviving the Balkan policies of the past."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_reconciliation_offer:0 "An Offer of Reconciliation"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_reconciliation_offer_desc:0 "The justice ministry offers early release to prisoners who credibly renounce violence. Each case must answer to the courts, the victims and a public that fears rewarding terror. A carefully limited offer could weaken the underground by giving its members a way out; the government's gesture cannot guarantee their response."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_red_green_federal:0 "The Red-Green Project"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_red_green_federal_desc:0 "A generation that once marched against the state now governs it. SPD and Greens form the first red-green federal government: an exit from nuclear power, a new citizenship law, an ecological tax reform. Former street fighters become ministers, former pacifists will have to decide on war. Power, it turns out, changes those who hold it."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_red_green_hesse:0 "Red-Green in Hesse"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_red_green_hesse_desc:0 "December 1985: Joschka Fischer is sworn in as Hesse's environment minister in white trainers. The first red-green coalition in a German state is a fragile experiment - the Greens want the Hanau nuclear plants closed, the SPD wants to govern - but the photograph goes around the world. A movement has entered the state."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_red_green_pact:0 "A Red-Green Pact"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_red_green_pact_desc:0 "Lafontaine offers the Greens what Brandt never offered: a coalition of equals rather than a junior partner to be tamed. The Realos are tempted by ministries and a chance to shut down the reactors. The Fundis want the withdrawal from NATO written into the coalition agreement. Whether the pact becomes a government depends on the voters - and on what each side is willing to give up."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_reforger:0 "REFORGER"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_reforger_desc:0 "Return of Forces to Germany: every autumn tens of thousands of American soldiers fly across the Atlantic, collect their tanks from depots in the Rhineland and practise the defence of the border alongside the Bundeswehr. Fields are churned up, villages blocked by convoys, farmers compensated. It is the visible proof that the Americans will come. The Soviets watch every exercise."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_regional_fund:0 "The Regional Fund"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_regional_fund_desc:0 "The Paris summit of December 1974 creates a European Regional Development Fund for the poorer regions of the Community: the Mezzogiorno, the west of Ireland, the north of England. Bonn pays the largest share and gets back the least. In return it buys the goodwill of Rome and Dublin for decades - and a Community that works for more than its richest members."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_renegotiate_treaties:0 "Renegotiate the Treaties"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_renegotiate_treaties_desc:0 "Chancellor Barzel wants the treaties - Bonn cannot afford to look like the enemy of détente - but on better terms: explicit reservations on German unity, on the rights of the expellees, on the status of Berlin. Moscow refuses to reopen signed agreements. The question is whether Bonn has enough to offer to make it change its mind."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_renew_grand_coalition:0 "Renew the Grand Coalition"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_renew_grand_coalition_desc:0 "Another four years together. The country is governed calmly, the big reforms pass, the budget is balanced. But the two great parties begin to look alike, their members ask what they are still fighting for, and the voters who want an alternative look for one beyond the two of them."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_renewable_research:0 "Solar and Wind Research"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_renewable_research_desc:0 "Growian, the giant wind turbine on the North Sea coast, is a failure: too big, too early, constantly breaking down. The research ministry's solar and wind programmes produce more reports than electricity. But the engineers learn, and the lessons of Growian's failure will be built into a generation of smaller, better machines."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_renounce_treaties:0 "Renounce the Eastern Treaties"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_renounce_treaties_desc:0 "Moscow, Warsaw, Prague, the Basic Treaty: 'treaties of renunciation', the Directorate calls them, signed by a republic that no longer exists and binding on no one. The notes are delivered to the embassies in a single morning. Twenty years of détente are torn up - and with them every guarantee that Germany's neighbours had learned to rely on."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_research_policy:0 "Federal Research Ministry"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_research_policy_desc:0 "Data processing programmes, nuclear research centres in Jülich and Karlsruhe, the Max Planck Society for basic research and the Fraunhofer institutes for application: the federal research ministry makes the state into a venture capitalist for technologies that no company would finance alone. Some bets pay off; others become museums."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_restore_basic_law:0 "Restore the Basic Law"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_restore_basic_law_desc:0 "The Directorate has failed - or has understood in time that it will. The Bundestag is recalled to Bonn, the decrees are lifted, the prisoners are released and free elections are announced. The Republic returns, battered and humbled. Whether the world believes it, and whether the Germans believe it themselves, is a different question."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_return_premium:0 "Return Premium"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_return_premium_desc:0 "10,500 marks, plus 1,500 for every child, for every guest worker who goes home for good. The Return Assistance Act of 1983 is the government's attempt to reverse the immigration it never admitted to. Some 250,000 people take the money and leave. Most of the others stay - now with the knowledge that the state would prefer them gone."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_rhineland_renewed:0 "The Rhineland Model Renewed"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_rhineland_renewed_desc:0 "No shock therapy: the chancellor keeps the social partnership and buys time with public money - investment in rail and schools, a training levy, early retirement paid for by the pension funds. The Federal Republic stays comfortable. It also stays slow."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_romanian_germans:0 "The Ransom of the Romanian Germans"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_romanian_germans_desc:0 "Ceaușescu's Romania sells its ethnic Germans: so many thousand marks for every Transylvanian Saxon and Banat Swabian allowed to leave, paid through secret accounts and negotiated by intelligence officers in hotel rooms. Bonn pays, quietly, and asks no questions about where the money goes. Over the years, two hundred thousand people come to the Federal Republic this way."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_rotation_principle:0 "The Rotation Principle"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_rotation_principle_desc:0 "No professional politicians: every Green member of the Bundestag gives up the seat after two years to a successor from the list. It is grassroots democracy in its purest form - and it produces a parliamentary group that never learns the job, loses its best people just as they become effective and gives the other parties endless material for jokes."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_ruhr_structural_change:0 "Structural Change in the Ruhr"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_ruhr_structural_change_desc:0 "Universities instead of coal pits, shopping centres instead of blast furnaces, a landscape park where the coking plant used to be. North Rhine-Westphalia sets out to reinvent its industrial heartland: slowly, expensively, with the unions at the table and the miners guaranteed that nobody will fall into unemployment. It takes a generation. Perhaps two."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_salzgitter:0 "The Salzgitter Registry"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_salzgitter_desc:0 "Since 1961 a central registry at the public prosecutor's office in Salzgitter, in Lower Saxony, has recorded every shot fired at the border, every death at the Wall and every political sentence in the GDR. The files are meant for the day when the guilty can be brought to trial. East Berlin demands its closure as the price for better relations. Bonn has to decide what the files are worth."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_saudi_tanks:0 "Leopards for Riyadh?"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_saudi_tanks_desc:0 "Saudi Arabia wants three hundred Leopard 2 tanks. The money is enormous, the jobs in Munich and Kassel are welcome - and the export guidelines forbid deliveries into areas of tension. Menachem Begin publicly calls Helmut Schmidt a man who served Hitler. The chancellor must decide whether the Federal Republic is a normal country that sells weapons like any other."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_schengen:0 "Schengen"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_schengen_desc:0 "June 1985, a riverboat on the Moselle at the Luxembourg village of Schengen: France, Germany and the Benelux countries agree to abolish the controls at their common borders. The customs posts on the Rhine bridges will disappear, and a lorry will drive from Rotterdam to Munich without stopping. The interior ministers worry about criminals; the citizens notice freedom."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_schmidt_alone:0 "Governing Without a Majority"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_schmidt_alone_desc:0 "The FDP has left the coalition; the chancellor stays. Helmut Schmidt governs with the SPD alone, from vote to vote, until the Bundestag either backs him or replaces him. It is the loneliest phase of his chancellorship - and in some ways the most impressive, as a man without a majority continues to govern by sheer authority."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_schmidt_legacy:0 "The Statesman's Farewell"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_schmidt_legacy_desc:0 "Whatever happens in the Bundestag, the chancellor uses his last months for what he does best: the world economy, the security of Europe, a speech to the Bundestag that both sides will quote for years. History will judge Helmut Schmidt more kindly than his party does. He seems to know it."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_schmidt_minority:0 "Schmidt Governs Alone"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_schmidt_minority_desc:0 "The FDP ministers have resigned, the chancellor remains. Helmut Schmidt governs with a minority government - a novelty in Bonn, and a countdown. Every law needs a majority found anew, every budget is a gamble, and the opposition is preparing the vote that will bring it to power."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_schmidt_snap_election:0 "Let the Voters Decide"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_schmidt_snap_election_desc:0 "The chancellor could wait for the opposition to bring him down. Or he could ask the Bundestag for a vote of confidence, lose it on purpose and let the Federal President dissolve parliament. It is constitutionally dubious and politically daring - and it lets the voters, not the coalition committees, decide who governs."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdi_research:0 "Partners in SDI Research"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdi_research_desc:0 "Reagan's Strategic Defense Initiative wants laser weapons and missile shields in space - and European laboratories to help build them. The Union sees contracts for German high technology and a place at the frontier of research. The SPD sees a new arms race that could undermine the ABM Treaty and détente itself. Both sides see Washington watching."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_bavarian_model:0 "The Bavarian Model"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_capital_berlin:0 "Capital of Germany"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_expo:0 "Expo Site"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_fulda_gap:0 "Fulda Gap Barrier Plans"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_garrison:0 "Franco-German Brigade"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_high_tech:0 "High-Tech Region"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_jena_revival:0 "Jena Reborn"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_merged_land:0 "Merged Land"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_neckar_valley:0 "Silicon Valley on the Neckar"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_nordstaat:0 "Nordstaat"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_olympic_city:0 "Olympic City"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_red_green_land:0 "Red-Green Land Government"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_ruhr_change:0 "Structural Change in the Ruhr"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_showcase:0 "Showcase of the West"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_steel_rescue:0 "Steel Rescue"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_un_city:0 "UN City Bonn"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sdm_wackersdorf:0 "Wackersdorf"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_second_cold_war:0 "Cold War Again"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_second_cold_war_desc:0 "The coup in Moscow has succeeded, or the Soviets have said no to unity, or the reform in the East has been crushed. Whatever the cause, divided Germany prepares for a long winter: the Wall stays, the missiles stay, the dream of the autumn is over. History has offered a window, and the window has closed."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_group:0 "The Security Group"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_group_desc:0 "The BKA's Security Group protects the constitutional organs: the federal president, the chancellor, the ministers. After the murders of Jürgen Ponto and Hanns Martin Schleyer the list grows to include bankers, judges, industrialists and diplomats - everyone the RAF might choose next. Armoured cars and bodyguards become the symbol of the German Autumn."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_programme_coordination:0 "Case Coordination"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_programme_coordination_terms:0 "25 PP / $0.035bn\n$0.003bn/week / 180 days"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_programme_coordination_tt:0 "Federal-State Case Coordination\n25 PP / $0.035bn + $0.003bn/week\n180 days / Wanted traces +8, then +1/month\nRequires BKA level 1 and active RAF cadres. Consolidate federal and state police case files. Each wanted person still at large gains +8 trace, then +1 trace/month for 180 days, capped at 100. Arrests still require the existing investigation process. Cooldown: 180 days.\nRequires §YBKA Expansion§!."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_programme_cost:0 "Additional programmes: §Y$[?cwsec_program_weekly_cost|3]bn/week§!"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_programme_judicial:0 "Judicial Review"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_programme_judicial_terms:0 "35 PP / $0.025bn\n$0.002bn/week / 180 days"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_programme_judicial_tt:0 "Judicial Review of Security Measures\n35 PP / $0.025bn + $0.002bn/week\nRule of law +3 / Milieu -3 / Security -2\nRequires milieu above 2, rule of law below 98 and security above 1. Review intrusive security measures: rule of law +3; milieu -3 immediately and -0.25/month for 180 days; security -2. Reduced intrusive powers constrain security capacity. Cooldown: 180 days.\nRequires §YData Protection§!."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_programme_medical:0 "Medical Review"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_programme_medical_terms:0 "35 PP / $0.030bn\n$0.003bn/week / 90 days"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_programme_medical_tt:0 "Independent Prison Medical Review\n35 PP / $0.030bn + $0.003bn/week\nHunger pressure -10 / Milieu -2 / Security -2\nRequires imprisoned RAF members, hunger-strike pressure above 9 and security above 1. Independent medical scrutiny reduces hunger pressure by 10 and milieu by 2; rule of law +2, security -2. Medical supervision costs $0.003bn/week for 90 days. The chosen prison regime remains in force. Cooldown: 180 days.\nRequires §YThe Stammheim Trial§!."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_programmes:0 "Security Programmes"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_state:0 "The Security State"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_security_state_desc:0 "Internment for terrorist sympathisers, an amendment to Article 102 to bring back the death penalty for hostage-takers, surveillance without a judge's warrant: in the crisis staff of 1977 such ideas were floated and quietly buried. Now they are written into law. The RAF wanted to provoke the state into revealing its 'fascist face'. Some will say it has succeeded."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_shipyard_crisis:0 "The Shipyard Crisis"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_shipyard_crisis_desc:0 "AG Weser in Bremen, one of the great shipyards of the world, closes in 1983 after a hundred and forty years. Asian yards build cheaper, and the merchant fleets no longer need German ships. Bremen, Kiel and Hamburg ask Bonn for money to save what is left. The question is whether the money buys a future or only time."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_shortcut_atlantic_anchor:0 "West"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_shortcut_chancellery:0 "Chancellery"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_shortcut_citizen_in_uniform:0 "Bundeswehr"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_shortcut_cultural_diplomacy:0 "World"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_shortcut_dp_hub:0 "Deutschlandpolitik"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_shortcut_energy_programme:0 "Energy"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_shortcut_internal_security:0 "Security"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_shortcut_social_market:0 "Economy"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_shorter_week:0 "Share the Work"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_shorter_week_desc:0 "Four million unemployed and an economy that produces more with fewer people every year. Lafontaine's answer: share the work. The 35-hour week, limits on overtime, a right to part-time employment - a programme for full employment paid for with time rather than money. The employers call it a recipe for decline; IG Metall has been demanding it for years."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_single_market:0 "The Single Market"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_single_market_desc:0 "The Single European Act of 1986 promises a Europe without internal borders by the end of 1992: goods, capital, services and people moving freely across the Community. For Germany's exporters it is the largest home market in the world. For Germany's beer brewers, insurers and craftsmen, it is the end of a great many comfortable national rules."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sister_war:0 "The War of the Sisters"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sister_war_desc:0 "Two Christian parties are fighting for the same voters in the same constituencies. The SPD smiles, the FDP rejoices at every split constituency, and the joint parliamentary group of the CDU and CSU in the Bundestag - the foundation of every Union government since 1949 - is about to break apart for good."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_situation_centre:0 "The Situation Centre"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_situation_centre_desc:0 "Until now the chancellor learned of a crisis from the morning papers or from a telephone call at midnight. A situation room in the chancellery changes that: BND assessments, the cables from the Permanent Representation in East Berlin and the crisis staff's lines all come together in one windowless room beneath the Palais. Whoever controls the information controls the government's first hour."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_small_parties_rise:0 "The Opposition Outside Parliament"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_small_parties_rise_desc:0 "With both big parties in the government, the opposition happens elsewhere: in the small parties of parliament, in the student unions, in the streets, and on the edges of the political spectrum where nobody in Bonn is looking. History has a precedent - the grand coalition of 1966 gave birth to the extra-parliamentary opposition and the NPD's best years."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_so_nicht:0 "'Not Like This!'"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_so_nicht_desc:0 "'Not like this!' Rainer Barzel's line on the Eastern treaties is a masterpiece of tactical ambiguity: no blanket rejection of reconciliation with the East, but no ratification on these terms. It keeps the CDU and the CSU together, keeps the expellees' associations on board - and leaves open what the Union would actually do in government."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_social_market:0 "The Social Market Economy at Twenty-Five"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_social_market_desc:0 "Twenty-five years after Ludwig Erhard abolished rationing overnight, the social market economy is the Federal Republic's founding myth: full employment, a hard Deutschmark and an export surplus that the world envies. But the miracle years are over. Growth is slowing, the guest workers are staying, and the unions want their share of the wealth they helped to create."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_social_union:0 "A Social Union"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_social_union_desc:0 "Pensions, health insurance and unemployment benefit for all Germans on the same terms: the offer of a social union makes a mixed economic order acceptable to the workers of the East, who fear that unity will cost them their jobs and their security. It is also an enormous bill for the West's taxpayers - and the bill will arrive whether or not unity does."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sole_mandate_renewed:0 "Renew the Sole Mandate"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_sole_mandate_renewed_desc:0 "Bonn alone speaks for Germany. Any state that recognises the GDR will lose its West German aid and its West German ambassador: the Hallstein Doctrine, revived. In 1955 it worked; in the 1970s the Third World has other options, and the GDR has friends with money of their own. The question is how many friends Bonn is prepared to lose."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_solidarity_pact:0 "The Solidarity Pact"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_solidarity_pact_desc:0 "Unity costs more than anyone admitted in 1990. The Solidarity Pact of 1993 is the answer: a solidarity surcharge on income tax, the German Unity Fund, and a new financial settlement between the Länder that brings the East into the federal equalisation. The West pays, the East receives, and both sides feel that the other is ungrateful."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_solidarity_support:0 "Parcels for Poland"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_solidarity_support_desc:0 "December 1981: General Jaruzelski declares martial law in Poland, Solidarność is banned and its leaders interned. Millions of West Germans send food parcels to Poland; the government sends money to the Catholic Church. The question in Bonn is whether it should also speak out for Solidarność - and what that would cost détente."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_solzhenitsyn_guest:0 "A Guest in the Eifel"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_solzhenitsyn_guest_desc:0 "February 1974: the Soviet Union expels Alexander Solzhenitsyn. The plane from Moscow lands in Frankfurt, and the first house that opens its door to him belongs to Heinrich Böll, in a village in the Eifel. The Kremlin is watching how Bonn receives its most famous exile."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_southern_enlargement:0 "Southern Enlargement"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_southern_enlargement_desc:0 "Greece in 1981, Spain and Portugal in 1986: young democracies, only a few years removed from the colonels, Franco and Salazar, join the Community. The Federal Republic's party foundations helped to build their parties; now German taxpayers help to build their roads. Europe has become the guarantee that the dictatorships do not return."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_soviet_germans:0 "The Soviet Germans"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_soviet_germans_desc:0 "Two million ethnic Germans live in Kazakhstan, Siberia and Kyrgyzstan, the descendants of those Stalin deported from the Volga in 1941. Under Gorbachev the gates begin to open - if Bonn asks, and if Bonn is prepared to receive them. Hundreds of thousands come every year at the peak: Germans by law, strangers in the country of their ancestors."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_soviet_withdrawal:0 "Pay for the Withdrawal"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_soviet_withdrawal_desc:0 "Three hundred and forty thousand Soviet soldiers and their families are stationed in the GDR. They must go home - to a country that has no flats, no barracks and no jobs for them. Bonn pays twelve billion marks to house them and a few billion more for their transport. The last Soviet soldiers leave Berlin on 31 August 1994. The Germans are free."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_spaeth_chancellor:0 "The Bremen Putsch"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_spaeth_chancellor_desc:0 "September 1989: the CDU's reformers want Lothar Späth instead of Helmut Kohl. Geißler, Süssmuth and Späth himself are ready; at the Bremen party congress, in the decisive moment, they lose their nerve. Here they need not. The 'cleverle' from Stuttgart becomes chancellor just as the Wall begins to crumble."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_spaeth_high_tech:0 "Späth's High-Tech State"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_spaeth_high_tech_desc:0 "Lothar Späth, 'the cleverle' from Stuttgart, has turned Baden-Württemberg into the most innovative state in the Federal Republic: research parks, technology transfer, venture capital, Daimler and Bosch working with the universities. Now the model is to go federal - and the Federal Republic is to become the Silicon Valley of Europe."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_spaeth_slow_unity:0 "Unity Without Haste"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_spaeth_slow_unity_desc:0 "Chancellor Späth will not promise blooming landscapes. Unity, he says, has to be earned and paid for: step by step, mark by mark, with a currency conversion that the East's factories can survive and a timetable that the West's taxpayers can accept. It is the voice of reason. Whether reason wins elections in a year of euphoria is another question."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_speak_for_dissidents:0 "Name the Prisoners"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_speak_for_dissidents_desc:0 "At every conference the German delegation reads out names: Sakharov, Orlov, Havel, Bahro. It is loud, it is public, and it makes the other side's diplomats walk out - but for the prisoners, a name known in the West is sometimes the only protection they have."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_spiritual_moral_turn:0 "The Spiritual-Moral Turn"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_spiritual_moral_turn_desc:0 "Helmut Kohl promises more than a change of government: a geistig-moralische Wende, a spiritual and moral turn. Less state, more family, more enterprise, an unashamed loyalty to the West and an end to the cultural dominance of the generation of 1968. What exactly that means in practice remains, as so often with this chancellor, pleasantly unclear."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_stammheim_trial:0 "The Stammheim Trial"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_stammheim_trial_desc:0 "A fortified courtroom built next to the prison at Stuttgart-Stammheim, defence lawyers excluded for alleged complicity, the defendants on hunger strike in protest against their conditions of detention. Holger Meins has already starved to death in his cell. The trial of the RAF's leaders is meant to show the strength of the rule of law. The world watches whether it does."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_stasi_files:0 "Open the Stasi Files"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_stasi_files_desc:0 "Six million files, a hundred and eighty kilometres of shelves, the record of a whole society spied upon by itself. Every citizen may now read what the Ministry for State Security wrote about them - and learn which friend, which colleague, which husband informed on them. The Gauck authority opens in January 1992. The country begins to read."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_state_of_the_republic:0 "State of the Bonn Republic"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_state_of_the_republic_desc:0 "The balance of security and liberty, the threat of terrorism, the pressure of scandals, and the Bundesbank's patience, all at once.\nSecurity state: §Y[?cwger_security|0]§! | Rule of law: §Y[?cwger_rechtsstaat|0]§!\nPeace movement: §Y[?cwger_peace_movement|0]§! | Burden of the East: §Y[?cwger_east_burden|0]§! | Stasi penetration §Y[?cwger_stasi_penetration|0]§! vs counter-intelligence §Y[?cwger_counterintel|0]§!\nTerror threat (left/right/foreign): §Y[?cwger_terror_left|0]§! / §Y[?cwger_terror_right|0]§! / §Y[?cwger_terror_foreign|0]§!\nBundestag: government §Y[?cwger_seats_gov|0]§! of §Y[?cwger_seats_total|0]§! seats (majority §Y[?cwger_majority|0]§!)."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_steel_crisis:0 "The Steel Crisis"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_steel_crisis_desc:0 "The steelworks of the Saar and the Ruhr are losing to Japan, Korea and Brazil, which produce cheaper and newer. Mergers, subsidies and quotas from Brussels are meant to slow the decline; in 1978 IG Metall calls the first long strike in the steel industry for the 35-hour week. Whole towns live from the blast furnaces. What happens to them when the fires go out?"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_stimulus_1975:0 "Stimulus Programme"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_stimulus_1975_desc:0 "The first real recession since the war: a million unemployed, short-time work in every industrial town, factories idle. The government reaches for Keynes - investment grants, construction programmes, regional aid - and borrows to pay for it. The Bundesbank watches with folded arms, ready to raise interest rates the moment it sees inflation."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_strauss_aerospace:0 "MBB and Airbus"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_strauss_aerospace_desc:0 "Strauß chairs the supervisory board of Airbus and wants a German aerospace champion to rival Boeing and Dassault: Messerschmitt-Bölkow-Blohm in Ottobrunn, fighter jets, satellites, helicopters. Defence contracts and research money flow south. In Hamburg and Bremen, where the other plants are, people ask why everything always ends up in Bavaria."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_strauss_east_credit:0 "The Surprising Credit"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_strauss_east_credit_desc:0 "Of all people, the man who denounced Ostpolitik as a sell-out arranges a loan of a billion marks for Erich Honecker - guaranteed by Bonn, negotiated with Alexander Schalck-Golodkowski. In return the GDR dismantles the automatic firing devices on the border. Only Nixon could go to China, they say in Bonn. Only Strauß could go to East Berlin."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_strauss_model:0 "The Bavarian Model"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_strauss_model_desc:0 "Chancellor Franz Josef Strauß: aerospace and nuclear power, low taxes and a strong police, a loud voice in Washington and an even louder one in his own cabinet. What Bavaria has become under the CSU - a farming state turned into a high-tech region - is now to become the model for the Federal Republic."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_strauss_moscow_flight:0 "Strauß Flies to Moscow"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_strauss_moscow_flight_desc:0 "December 1987: the Bavarian premier pilots his own Cessna through a snowstorm to Moscow. The anti-communist of the 1950s, the man who wanted nuclear weapons for the Bundeswehr, sits down with Mikhail Gorbachev - and comes home impressed. If Strauß says the Soviet Union has changed, even his own voters begin to believe it."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_strauss_of_the_right:0 "A Home on the Right"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_strauss_of_the_right_desc:0 "'There must be no democratically legitimate party to the right of the CSU.' Strauß's maxim was meant for Bavaria; now it is to apply to the whole country. The CSU absorbs the national conservatives, the disappointed expellees and the law-and-order voters before anyone further to the right can claim them. It is a strategy of containment - and a risk of contagion."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_street_and_ballot:0 "The Street and the Ballot Box"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_street_and_ballot_desc:0 "Torchlight marches in provincial towns, a 'national' newspaper at every kiosk, veterans' associations in the front row of the rallies. The far right no longer hides in back rooms; it marches with the government's blessing. And the other side takes to the streets as well: trade unions, churches, students. The Republic is being contested in the market squares."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_strong_state:0 "The Strong State"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_strong_state_desc:0 "Whoever attacks the state will meet the whole of the state: more police, more powers, more computers, and less patience with those who ask about the price. The government promises the citizens security. The intellectuals warn of a police state; the government answers that the real danger comes from those who shoot."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_support_round_table:0 "Support the Round Table"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_support_round_table_desc:0 "At the Round Table in East Berlin the SED sits opposite the new opposition: New Forum, Democracy Now, the Social Democrats of the East, pastors and environmental activists. They have courage but no money, no offices and no printing presses. Bonn sends them all three - quietly, through the party foundations, so that the SED cannot call them Western puppets."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_swing_credit:0 "The Swing"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_swing_credit_desc:0 "Inner-German trade runs on an interest-free overdraft, the 'Swing', which allows the GDR to buy more from the West than it sells. Raise the ceiling and East Berlin becomes a little more dependent on Bonn's goodwill - and a little more willing to grant concessions on travel and family visits. Lower it, and the planners in East Berlin feel it within a quarter."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_take_gorbachev_at_word:0 "Take Gorbachev at His Word"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_take_gorbachev_at_word_desc:0 "Davos, February 1987: Hans-Dietrich Genscher tells the West to take Mikhail Gorbachev at his word - to test whether glasnost and perestroika are real by offering the Soviet leader real agreements. In Washington and London they hear 'Genscherism' and suspect Bonn of going soft. In Moscow they hear an open door."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tax_reform_1990:0 "The Stoltenberg Tax Reform"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tax_reform_1990_desc:0 "Gerhard Stoltenberg's tax reform lowers income tax in three stages, cutting the entry rate and the top rate alike - the largest tax relief in the Republic's history so far. It is meant to reward effort and to bring the economy out of its stagnation. The opposition calls it a gift for the rich; the economists, overdue."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_ten_point_plan:0 "The Ten-Point Plan"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_ten_point_plan_desc:0 "28 November 1989: without telling his allies or his coalition partner, Helmut Kohl presents a ten-point plan to the Bundestag - aid for the GDR, confederative structures between the two states, and finally a federation. Washington is surprised, Paris and London are furious, Moscow warns. The chancellor has seized the initiative and will not let it go."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tennis_nation:0 "Boris and Steffi"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tennis_nation_desc:0 "A seventeen-year-old from Leimen wins Wimbledon with a dive across the grass; a girl from Brühl beats Martina Navratilova. Within a summer, tennis courts are sold out in every suburb and the whole country watches matches that start at two in the afternoon."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_textbook_commission:0 "The Textbook Commission"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_textbook_commission_desc:0 "German and Polish historians sit down to read each other's schoolbooks - the war, the expulsions, the Oder and the Neisse - and to agree on what children on both sides should learn. In Bavaria the expellees' associations call it a betrayal before the first page is written."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_third_way_paper:0 "Europe: The Third Way"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_third_way_paper_desc:0 "A joint paper with London: flexible labour markets, lower taxes for companies, a state that activates rather than provides. In Downing Street it is a manifesto for a new European social democracy. In the SPD's local branches it reads like a declaration of war."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_three_percent:0 "Three Percent Is Enough"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_three_percent_desc:0 "The five-per-cent hurdle was the Republic's answer to Weimar's splinter parties - and it keeps out new movements just as effectively. Lowering it to three per cent would make the Bundestag more colourful and more representative. Some of the new colours would be welcome; others have names that the Republic hoped never to hear in its parliament again."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tiananmen_business:0 "After Tiananmen: Business"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tiananmen_business_desc:0 "A year after the massacre the first German minister is back in Beijing; Volkswagen is building in Shanghai, Siemens wants the high-speed line. Change through trade, says the government. The human rights groups call it a licence to shoot."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tiananmen_sanctions:0 "After Tiananmen: Sanctions"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tiananmen_sanctions_desc:0 "Tanks on the Square of Heavenly Peace, students shot on the Avenue of Eternal Peace. The Community freezes arms sales and ministerial contacts with Beijing. For Bonn, which has courted China since 1972, the question is how long a freeze can last."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tied_aid:0 "Aid that Buys German"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tied_aid_desc:0 "Development credits, but with a condition: the turbines come from Siemens, the trucks from Daimler, the consultants from Frankfurt. The Ministry of Economics is delighted; the Development Ministry calls it an export subsidy with a humanitarian label."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tornado:0 "Tornado"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tornado_desc:0 "The Panavia Tornado is a European answer to an American question: Britain, Italy and Germany share the enormous cost of a low-level strike aircraft that can fly under the Warsaw Pact's radar and deliver conventional - and nuclear - weapons. It is late and expensive. It is also the first time Europe has built a front-line combat aircraft together."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tornado_ecr:0 "Tornado ECR"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tornado_ecr_desc:0 "Electronic combat and reconnaissance Tornados, armed with HARM missiles that home in on enemy radar: Germany's contribution to NATO air campaigns is not to drop bombs but to blind the enemy's air defence so that others can. It is a specialised role that the allies badly need - and a way for Germany to fight without being seen to fight too much."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_transparency_act:0 "The Transparency Act"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_transparency_act_desc:0 "Every donation above ten thousand marks published within a month, cash donations banned, prison for false accounts, the party's entire assets disclosed every year. After the scandals the Bundestag writes the strictest party finance law in Europe. The party treasurers sigh. The voters may begin to trust again."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_treaty_community:0 "Treaty Community"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_treaty_community_desc:0 "Hans Modrow, the reform communist, offers a contractual community between two sovereign states, then a confederation, and unity at the end - in years, not months. It is a serious offer from a serious man. The people in the streets have stopped chanting 'We are the people' and now chant 'We are one people'. They do not want to wait years."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_treuhand:0 "The Treuhandanstalt"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_treuhand_desc:0 "Eight and a half thousand state enterprises, four million employees, an economy built for the Comecon market that no longer exists. The Treuhandanstalt is to privatise, restructure or close them all. Its first president is murdered by the RAF; its second sells off the East's industry at a pace that leaves whole regions without work. The bill arrives with the unemployment."

 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tt_wende:0 "The Union and the FDP form a new government without an election."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_tt_win_two:0 "The government gains §Gtwo votes§!, and the FDP moves towards the chancellor's party."

 COLDWAR_GER_1970_two_plus_four_west:0 "Unity Inside NATO"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_two_plus_four_west_desc:0 "London fears a Fourth Reich, Paris wants a guarantee that Germany will stay in Europe, Moscow wants it out of NATO. Bonn needs Washington to persuade the others that a united Germany inside NATO is the safest Germany - anchored, contained and reliable. George Bush is the first to agree. The others will need longer."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_two_thirds_reforms:0 "The Power of Two Thirds"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_two_thirds_reforms_desc:0 "Together the two big parties hold the two-thirds majority in both chambers that every amendment of the Basic Law requires. What they agree on, nobody can stop: not the small parties, not the Länder, not the street. A grand coalition is the moment for the reforms that are too big for any single camp - and a temptation to rewrite the rules in its own favour."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_two_way_street:0 "Culture as a Two-Way Street"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_two_way_street_desc:0 "Hildegard Hamm-Brücher's guidelines turn cultural policy on its head: no more exporting Beethoven and the German idea, but exchange - partners invited to Germany, foreign artists in German theatres, a dialogue rather than a lecture."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_type_209:0 "The Type 209"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_type_209_desc:0 "HDW in Kiel builds a small, quiet, reliable diesel-electric submarine for export, and the world's navies queue up for it: Greece, Argentina, Peru, Turkey, India, South Korea. The Type 209 becomes the most successful submarine design of the post-war era. Every contract keeps the yard alive - and every contract is an argument about where German weapons should go."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_u_rr_fail:0 "§RNo agreement.§! The delegations could not find common ground."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_u_rr_ok:0 "§GAgreement.§! Both delegations accepted the same position."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_un_city_bonn:0 "Bonn, City of the United Nations"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_un_city_bonn_desc:0 "The government is moving to Berlin, and the federal city on the Rhine fears it will become a provincial town with too many empty ministries. The answer: the climate secretariat, the UN Volunteers and a dozen other agencies move into the old parliamentary quarter."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_un_entry:0 "Germany at the United Nations"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_un_entry_desc:0 "18 September 1973: on the East River in New York, the black, red and gold flag of the Federal Republic is raised in front of the United Nations - next to the flag of the GDR, admitted on the same day. Bonn now has a voice in the General Assembly and a delegation to staff. It also has a seat in a hall where the other German state speaks too."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_un_security_council:0 "A Seat at the Security Council"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_un_security_council_desc:0 "The Federal Republic serves as a non-permanent member of the Security Council in 1977-78 and 1987-88, and German diplomats prove themselves skilled at the work. After unity, the question becomes a bigger one: should the third-largest contributor to the United Nations' budget have a permanent seat at the table where the decisions are made?"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_union_opposition:0 "The Union in Opposition"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_union_opposition_desc:0 "For twenty years the CDU/CSU provided every chancellor. Now it sits on the opposition benches after losing power by a handful of seats, convinced that the state belongs to it and that the Eastern treaties are a sell-out of the German question. The Union has to decide what kind of opposition it wants to be - and whether it can bring down the government before the next election."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_unity_treaty:0 "The Unification Treaty"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_unity_treaty_desc:0 "Nine hundred pages that merge two legal systems, two pension systems, two education systems and two armies. Wolfgang Schäuble and Günther Krause negotiate it in a few weeks: property questions, abortion law, the fate of the Stasi files, the capital. Never has a treaty of this size been written so quickly - and never will one have so many consequences."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_university_framework:0 "The Universities Framework Act"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_university_framework_desc:0 "One federal law for all the universities of the Republic: the Universities Framework Act decides who governs the institution - the professors alone, as before 1968, or a group university in which assistants and students have a vote. The Constitutional Court has already said that professors must keep the majority on questions of research. Everything else is politics."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_untied_aid:0 "Aid without Strings"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_untied_aid_desc:0 "Bonn follows the OECD's advice and unties most of its development aid: partners may buy wherever it is cheapest, and the projects are judged by what they achieve, not by how many German machines they ship. Industry complains, the recipients notice."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_urengoy:0 "The Urengoy Pipeline"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_urengoy_desc:0 "A credit of 3.4 billion marks for a pipeline from the gas fields of Urengoy to Western Europe. The Reagan administration wants it stopped: it would make Europe dependent on Moscow and fill the Soviet treasury with hard currency. Bonn builds it anyway. It is the first time the Federal Republic openly defies Washington on a matter of economic security."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_uruguay_round:0 "The Uruguay Round"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_uruguay_round_desc:0 "Eight years of negotiations on free trade in goods, services and intellectual property, and a World Trade Organization at the end of them. The Federal Republic, which lives from its exports, has everything to gain. The fight is with the French farmers, who block the motorways with tractors - and with the German farmers, who would quietly prefer to do the same."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_venice_declaration:0 "The Venice Declaration"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_venice_declaration_desc:0 "June 1980, Venice: the Nine recognise the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination and call for the PLO to be associated with the peace negotiations. It is the first time Western Europe takes a position on the Middle East that differs openly from Washington's. Jerusalem compares it to Munich in 1938. Bonn's signature is on it."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_verfassungsschutz:0 "Counter-Espionage"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_verfassungsschutz_desc:0 "The HVA of Markus Wolf has hundreds of agents in the Federal Republic: secretaries in ministries, aides in the chancellery, officers in NATO headquarters. The Office for the Protection of the Constitution in Cologne needs more than files and filing cabinets. It needs agents of its own, defectors who talk, and the patience to turn the enemy's spies."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_vergangenheitsbewaeltigung:0 "Confronting the Past"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_vergangenheitsbewaeltigung_desc:0 "The Majdanek trial in Düsseldorf runs for five years; the American series 'Holocaust' is watched by twenty million West Germans in 1979 and does what decades of documentation could not; the Bundestag abolishes the statute of limitations for murder so that the perpetrators can still be tried. Coming to terms with the past is not a single act but a task without end."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_vocational_training:0 "The Dual System"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_vocational_training_desc:0 "Two days at the vocational school, three days at the workbench: the dual system of apprenticeship trains two-thirds of every generation as skilled workers and is the quiet strength behind 'Made in Germany'. Youth unemployment is lower than anywhere else in Europe. Other countries send delegations to study it; few manage to copy it."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_volga_germans:0 "Exit for the Soviet Germans"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_volga_germans_desc:0 "Two million Germans live in the Soviet Union - descendants of the settlers Catherine the Great invited to the Volga, deported to Kazakhstan by Stalin in 1941. Most of them want only one thing: to leave. Moscow lets out a few thousand a year, and Bonn wonders what the rest would cost."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_voting_age_18:0 "Voting Age Eighteen"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_voting_age_18_desc:0 "Students who marched against the emergency laws, apprentices who joined the unions at sixteen, conscripts who can be sent to the border but not to the ballot box: lowering the voting age to eighteen brings the generation of 1968 into the electorate. The SPD expects their gratitude. The young voters have not promised it."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_wackersdorf:0 "Wackersdorf"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_wackersdorf_desc:0 "A reprocessing plant for plutonium in the forests of the Upper Palatinate - Strauß's prestige project and the core of the German nuclear fuel cycle. It becomes the scene of the fiercest battles the anti-nuclear movement ever fought: tens of thousands in the woods, CS gas from helicopters, protests from neighbouring Austria. Bavaria never gives way, says the premier."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_waldsterben:0 "Forest Dieback"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_waldsterben_desc:0 "'The forest is dying', Der Spiegel announces on its cover: needles falling, crowns thinning, acid rain from the power stations' chimneys. No issue has moved the Germans like this one; the forest is a part of their soul. Environmental policy leaves the fringes and enters the chancellery. The power stations get scrubbers, the cars catalytic converters."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_wandel_durch_annaeherung:0 "Change through Rapprochement"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_wandel_durch_annaeherung_desc:0 "Tutzing, July 1963: Egon Bahr, Brandt's press spokesman in West Berlin, offers a formula that will shape two decades - change through rapprochement. Accept the realities in order to change them; small steps for people instead of big words about unity. The Union calls it capitulation. The people waiting at the crossing points call it hope."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_warsaw_treaty:0 "The Warsaw Treaty"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_warsaw_treaty_desc:0 "December 1970: the Treaty of Warsaw recognises the Oder-Neisse line as Poland's western border. Before signing it, Willy Brandt lays a wreath at the memorial to the heroes of the Warsaw Ghetto - and falls to his knees. The photograph travels around the world. At home, a majority of West Germans think the kneeling was exaggerated. History will disagree."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_wealth_tax:0 "Tax the Rich"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_wealth_tax_desc:0 "A wealth tax, a higher top rate of income tax and an end to the loopholes on capital gains: the money for rebuilding the East and for the jobs programme is to come from those who have it. The unions applaud, the business associations threaten to invest abroad, and the Bundesbank warns of capital flight. Social democracy has rediscovered its old enemy."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_weimar_triangle:0 "The Weimar Triangle"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_weimar_triangle_desc:0 "August 1991, in Weimar - the city of Goethe and Schiller and of the Republic that failed. The foreign ministers of Germany, France and Poland meet for the first time as a group. The idea is simple: Germany's eastern neighbour is to be anchored in the West as the Federal Republic once was, with France as the third partner so that no one fears a German Central Europe."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_weizsaecker_speech:0 "8 May 1985"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_weizsaecker_speech_desc:0 "8 May 1985, forty years after the end of the war. Richard von Weizsäcker tells the Bundestag that it was a day of liberation - also for the Germans - and that whoever closes his eyes to the past becomes blind to the present. The speech is printed in millions of copies and taught in schools. The Republic has found a language for its history."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_west_media_strategy:0 "Western Television for the East"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_west_media_strategy_desc:0 "ARD and ZDF can be watched across the entire GDR except for the 'valley of the clueless' around Dresden. Every evening at eight, millions of East Germans watch the Tagesschau and know more about the Federal Republic than about their own country. The West comes in through the aerial. Bonn can decide whether to make programmes that are meant for the East."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_wintex:0 "WINTEX"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_wintex_desc:0 "Every two years the federal government, the Joint Committee and NATO rehearse the state of defence for a fortnight in the government bunker under the Ahr valley - including the moment when NATO requests the release of nuclear weapons on targets in both German states. In 1989 the West German participants refuse to play that part of the script. The exercise is never held again."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_withdrawal_fund:0 "A Fund for the Soviet Withdrawal"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_withdrawal_fund_desc:0 "Barracks, flats, retraining and pensions for the soldiers of the Group of Soviet Forces in Germany, paid for by Bonn - in advance. Moscow cannot afford to bring its army home; the Soviet economy is collapsing. A fund for the withdrawal is the price of the Kremlin's signature under any treaty on unity. It is the cheapest liberation in history."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_working_longer:0 "The Pension Reform of 1992"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_working_longer_desc:0 "Fewer children, longer lives, and a pension system that pays today's retirees out of today's contributions. The pension reform of 1992 raises the retirement age step by step and ties pensions to net rather than gross wages. It is the first great reform that the opposition helps to write - and it is passed on the very day the Berlin Wall falls."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_working_time_385:0 "The 38.5-Hour Week"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_working_time_385_desc:0 "Spring 1984: IG Metall strikes for seven weeks for the 35-hour week, the employers lock out hundreds of thousands, and the car industry grinds to a halt. Georg Leber mediates the compromise: 38.5 hours, with flexible working time at plant level. Both sides claim victory. The road to the 35-hour week is open."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_works_constitution:0 "Works Constitution Act"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_works_constitution_desc:0 "The Works Constitution Act of 1972 gives the works councils a say in hiring, overtime and the layout of the shop floor, and lets the unions into the factory gates. For the DGB it is a down payment on economic democracy; for the employers' associations, a step towards the trade union state. On the shop floor it means one thing above all: the foreman no longer decides alone."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_world_cup_1974:0 "World Champions 1974"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_world_cup_1974_desc:0 "Gerd Müller turns and shoots in Munich's Olympic Stadium, Franz Beckenbauer lifts the cup, and the Federal Republic is world champion for the second time. But the tournament has another story: in Hamburg, in the only match ever played between the two German states, Jürgen Sparwasser scores for the GDR. Both Germanys celebrate - each for a different reason."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_world_cup_1990:0 "World Champions 1990"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_world_cup_1990_desc:0 "Rome, July 1990: Andreas Brehme's penalty in the eighty-fifth minute, Argentina beaten, and Franz Beckenbauer walking alone across the pitch of the Stadio Olimpico, lost in thought. Germany is world champion for the third time, in the year of unity. 'I am sorry for the rest of the world', says Beckenbauer, 'but we will be unbeatable for years.' He will be wrong."
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_yugoslav_partnership:0 "Tito's Germans"
 COLDWAR_GER_1970_yugoslav_partnership_desc:0 "Half a million Yugoslav guest workers live in the Federal Republic, and Tito's non-aligned Yugoslavia is the most open country of the socialist world. Belgrade wants credits instead of reparations for the occupation; Bonn wants Belgrade to stop sheltering terrorists and to hand over those it arrests. A partnership of interest, with Tito's death looming over it."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.1.a:0 "Continue."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.10.a:0 "Hold the crowds back."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.10.b:0 "Let them cheer. It changes nothing."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.10.desc:0 "When the West German chancellor arrives at the Erfurter Hof hotel, thousands break through the police lines and call for him to show himself at the window. The Stasi brings in trucks of loyal cadres for the next day."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.10.t:0 "'Willy Brandt ans Fenster!'"
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.11.a:0 "Sign - and demarcate."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.11.b:0 "Sign and open a little."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.11.desc:0 "Two German states, good-neighbourly relations, permanent missions. The GDR wins the recognition it has wanted for twenty years - and opens its border a crack for journalists, visitors and the telephone."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.11.t:0 "The Basic Treaty"
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.2.a:0 "Accept the credit."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.2.b:0 "We do not need Bonn's charity."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.2.desc:0 "The Federal Republic proposes to raise the interest-free overdraft in inner-German trade. More Western goods, fewer questions - and a little more dependence on the class enemy."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.2.t:0 "Bonn Offers a Larger Swing"
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.3.a:0 "Take the money, dismantle the SM-70."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.3.b:0 "No conditions on our border."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.3.desc:0 "Franz Josef Strauß himself has arranged a bank loan of one billion marks, guaranteed by the federal government. Schalck-Golodkowski brings the conditions: the self-firing devices on the border are to go, and the minimum exchange for children is to be dropped."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.3.t:0 "The Billion-Mark Credit"
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.30.a:0 "Continue."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.31.a:0 "Continue."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.32.a:0 "Continue."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.33.a:0 "Continue."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.34.a:0 "Continue."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.35.a:0 "Ask Bonn to open the existing treaty review."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.35.b:0 "Reject Bonn's timetable."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.35.desc:0 "The federal government has published a plan: free elections in the GDR, then 'confederative structures', then a federation. Nobody in East Berlin was consulted."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.35.t:0 "Bonn's Plan for Unity"
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.36.a:0 "Continue."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.37.a:0 "Continue."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.38.a:0 "Continue."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.39.a:0 "Continue."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.4.a:0 "Sell them."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.4.b:0 "Not this year."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.4.desc:0 "The lawyer Wolfgang Vogel brings a new list from Bonn. Every political prisoner released to the West brings tens of thousands of D-Marks - in goods delivered through the churches."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.4.t:0 "Prisoners for Hard Currency"
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.5.a:0 "Double it to 25 marks."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.5.b:0 "Leave it as it is."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.5.desc:0 "Every visitor from the West must exchange a fixed sum of D-Marks at a rate of one to one. Raising it would bring in hard currency - and keep pensioners from Hanover away from their relatives in Halle."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.5.t:0 "Raise the Minimum Exchange?"
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.6.a:0 "Expatriate him."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.6.b:0 "Let him come home and sing."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.6.desc:0 "The singer Wolf Biermann has been allowed to perform in Cologne - and the concert was broadcast by the WDR to the whole GDR. The Politburo considers withdrawing his citizenship."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.6.t:0 "Biermann in Cologne"
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.8.a:0 "Promise travel relief in return."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.8.b:0 "Recognition. Nothing else."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.8.desc:0 "Erich Honecker is received in Bonn with military honours, the GDR flag and the GDR anthem. He visits his birthplace in the Saarland. Kohl's speech at the dinner speaks of unity and freedom - and is broadcast live in the East."
 COLDWAR_GER_DDR.8.t:0 "The General Secretary on the Rhine"
 COLDWAR_GGR.10.a:0 "Back to business."
 COLDWAR_GGR.10.b:0 "Open the situation map."
 COLDWAR_GGR.10.desc1:0 "East Berlin has given way. In Bonn the government speaks of steadiness, in Neues Deutschland of 'provocations repelled'. The opposition has one argument fewer."
 COLDWAR_GGR.10.desc2:0 "East Berlin has had its way. The SED celebrates a victory over 'revanchism', the opposition in Bonn speaks of weakness, and in Washington people ask whether Bonn can be relied on."
 COLDWAR_GGR.10.desc3:0 "The crisis has not been settled - it has frozen. Nobody gave way, nobody won, and the issue is still there. It may flare up again."
 COLDWAR_GGR.10.desc4:0 "We gave way at the brink. The world breathes again, and the opposition sharpens its knives. East Berlin will remember that pressure works."
 COLDWAR_GGR.10.desc5:0 "East Berlin blinked first. Its troops stand down and its press falls silent. It is a victory - and the GDR leadership will not forgive the humiliation soon."
 COLDWAR_GGR.10.desc6:0 "Moscow has reined in its ally. The Soviet ambassador visited the SED leadership at night; by morning the crisis was over. Bonn has won - but the decision was taken in the Kremlin."
 COLDWAR_GGR.10.desc7:0 "Both sides have moved. Nobody calls it a victory, both governments call it a success - and the communiqué is long enough that everyone can find a sentence they like."
 COLDWAR_GGR.10.t:0 "The Crisis Is Over"
 COLDWAR_GGR.101.a:0 "Convene the crisis staff."
 COLDWAR_GGR.101.b:0 "Let the ministries handle it for now."
 COLDWAR_GGR.101.desc:0 "At Helmstedt and Dreilinden the East German border troops are taking every car apart. Lorries wait for twelve hours, coaches are turned back, a Bundestag deputy has been refused passage. East Berlin speaks of 'abuse of the transit routes'. West Berlin, a hundred and seventy kilometres inside the GDR, feels the noose tighten.\n\nA §YTransit Crisis§! has begun. Its intensity starts at §Y40§!. Every six months a round is resolved: both sides choose a course, and the crisis ends when its intensity falls to zero, reaches the brink at 100, or freezes after §Y4§! rounds."
 COLDWAR_GGR.101.t:0 "Trouble on the Transit Routes"
 COLDWAR_GGR.102.a:0 "Convene the crisis staff."
 COLDWAR_GGR.102.b:0 "Let the ministries handle it for now."
 COLDWAR_GGR.102.desc:0 "A young man from Thuringia tried to cross the fence near the Werra last night. The border troops opened fire. He bled to death in the strip while West German customs officers watched from fifty metres away. The pictures are on every front page; East Berlin calls it the defence of the state border.\n\nA §YBorder Incident§! has begun. Its intensity starts at §Y35§!. Every six months a round is resolved: both sides choose a course, and the crisis ends when its intensity falls to zero, reaches the brink at 100, or freezes after §Y3§! rounds."
 COLDWAR_GGR.102.t:0 "Shots at the Border"
 COLDWAR_GGR.103.a:0 "Convene the crisis staff."
 COLDWAR_GGR.103.b:0 "Let the ministries handle it for now."
 COLDWAR_GGR.103.desc:0 "The Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution has arrested a man with access to secrets he should never have seen. The trail leads to the HVA in East Berlin - and the newspapers are asking how high up it goes.\n\nA §YSpy Affair§! has begun. Its intensity starts at §Y45§!. Every six months a round is resolved: both sides choose a course, and the crisis ends when its intensity falls to zero, reaches the brink at 100, or freezes after §Y3§! rounds."
 COLDWAR_GGR.103.t:0 "A Spy in Bonn"
 COLDWAR_GGR.104.a:0 "Convene the crisis staff."
 COLDWAR_GGR.104.b:0 "Let the ministries handle it for now."
 COLDWAR_GGR.104.desc:0 "Hundreds of East Germans have climbed the fence of the West German embassy and refuse to leave until they can go west. More arrive every hour. The host government wants the problem gone; East Berlin wants them back.\n\nA §YEmbassy Refugees§! has begun. Its intensity starts at §Y50§!. Every six months a round is resolved: both sides choose a course, and the crisis ends when its intensity falls to zero, reaches the brink at 100, or freezes after §Y3§! rounds."
 COLDWAR_GGR.104.t:0 "Refugees in the Embassy"
 COLDWAR_GGR.105.a:0 "Convene the crisis staff."
 COLDWAR_GGR.105.b:0 "Let the ministries handle it for now."
 COLDWAR_GGR.105.desc:0 "Another government has recognised the GDR. Bonn's continuing sole-representation claim makes this a dispute over Germany's international position. The Foreign Office must weigh diplomatic pressure against the risk of losing a partner.\n\nA §YRecognition Crisis§! has begun. Its intensity starts at §Y30§!. Every six months a round is resolved: both sides choose a course, and the crisis ends when its intensity falls to zero, reaches the brink at 100, or freezes after §Y3§! rounds."
 COLDWAR_GGR.105.t:0 "A State Recognises the GDR"
 COLDWAR_GGR.106.a:0 "Convene the crisis staff."
 COLDWAR_GGR.106.b:0 "Let the ministries handle it for now."
 COLDWAR_GGR.106.desc:0 "Soviet SS-20 missiles can reach every capital in Western Europe. NATO answers with Pershing II and cruise missiles - to be stationed in the Federal Republic. East Berlin warns of an 'ice age' between the German states; hundreds of thousands march in the Hofgarten.\n\nA §YMissile Crisis§! has begun. Its intensity starts at §Y45§!. Every six months a round is resolved: both sides choose a course, and the crisis ends when its intensity falls to zero, reaches the brink at 100, or freezes after §Y4§! rounds."
 COLDWAR_GGR.106.t:0 "The Missiles of Europe"
 COLDWAR_GGR.107.a:0 "Convene the crisis staff."
 COLDWAR_GGR.107.b:0 "Let the ministries handle it for now."
 COLDWAR_GGR.107.desc:0 "NATO is rehearsing nuclear release procedures. In Moscow and East Berlin the intelligence services report that the exercise may be cover for a real attack. Soviet aircraft are on strip alert in the GDR, the National People's Army has cancelled leave.\n\nA §YManoeuvre Crisis§! has begun. Its intensity starts at §Y55§!. Every six months a round is resolved: both sides choose a course, and the crisis ends when its intensity falls to zero, reaches the brink at 100, or freezes after §Y2§! rounds."
 COLDWAR_GGR.107.t:0 "A Dangerous Exercise"
 COLDWAR_GGR.108.a:0 "Convene the crisis staff."
 COLDWAR_GGR.108.b:0 "Let the ministries handle it for now."
 COLDWAR_GGR.108.desc:0 "East Berlin has stripped a dissident of his citizenship while he was on a concert tour in the West. Writers and artists in the GDR have signed a protest letter. Every Western camera wants an interview; every SED newspaper calls him a traitor.\n\nA §YDissident Crisis§! has begun. Its intensity starts at §Y30§!. Every six months a round is resolved: both sides choose a course, and the crisis ends when its intensity falls to zero, reaches the brink at 100, or freezes after §Y3§! rounds."
 COLDWAR_GGR.108.t:0 "Expelled for His Songs"
 COLDWAR_GGR.109.a:0 "Convene the crisis staff."
 COLDWAR_GGR.109.b:0 "Let the ministries handle it for now."
 COLDWAR_GGR.109.desc:0 "Where exactly does the border run along the Elbe - in the middle of the river, as East Berlin insists, or on its eastern bank, as the Allied protocols of 1944 say? GDR patrol boats have turned back West German fishermen.\n\nA §YElbe Border Dispute§! has begun. Its intensity starts at §Y25§!. Every six months a round is resolved: both sides choose a course, and the crisis ends when its intensity falls to zero, reaches the brink at 100, or freezes after §Y4§! rounds."
 COLDWAR_GGR.109.t:0 "The Elbe Question"
 COLDWAR_GGR.11.a:0 "Keep the decision under review."
 COLDWAR_GGR.11.b:0 "Give way. Nothing is worth a war."
 COLDWAR_GGR.11.c:0 "Show resolve. Let them blink."
 COLDWAR_GGR.11.d:0 "Ask the superpowers to mediate."
 COLDWAR_GGR.11.desc:0 "The crisis has reached its peak. In East Berlin the Politburo is in permanent session, in Bonn the cabinet meets in the bunker plan of the Ahr valley. One side has to give way - or the next step is no longer politics."
 COLDWAR_GGR.11.t:0 "At the Brink"
 COLDWAR_GGR.110.a:0 "Convene the crisis staff."
 COLDWAR_GGR.110.b:0 "Let the ministries handle it for now."
 COLDWAR_GGR.110.desc:0 "The crushed protests are back - bigger. Factories are on strike, crowds have occupied SED district offices, and in some towns the police have taken off their caps and joined the demonstrators. In the East there are calls for help from the West. In Bonn there are people who want to give it.\n\nA §YUprising in the GDR§! has begun. Its intensity starts at §Y70§!. Every six months a round is resolved: both sides choose a course, and the crisis ends when its intensity falls to zero, reaches the brink at 100, or freezes after §Y3§! rounds."
 COLDWAR_GGR.110.t:0 "The People Rise"
 COLDWAR_GGR.121.a:0 "A wall made of money."
 COLDWAR_GGR.121.desc:0 "Every visitor from the West must now change more Deutschmarks into Ostmarks per day. Fewer pensioners will visit their sisters in Leipzig; more hard currency will flow to East Berlin."
 COLDWAR_GGR.121.t:0 "The Compulsory Exchange Is Raised"
 COLDWAR_GGR.122.a:0 "The world must see this."
 COLDWAR_GGR.122.desc:0 "New fences, new mines, new SM-70 spring guns along the inner-German border. East Berlin calls it the protection of the state border; in the West it is called the death strip."
 COLDWAR_GGR.122.t:0 "The Border Is Tightened"
 COLDWAR_GGR.123.a:0 "Small steps."
 COLDWAR_GGR.123.desc:0 "East Berlin has quietly lowered the compulsory exchange for pensioners and dismantled a stretch of spring guns. Its press says nothing; its diplomats say a great deal."
 COLDWAR_GGR.123.t:0 "A Gesture from East Berlin"
 COLDWAR_GGR.14.a:0 "Do not gloat."
 COLDWAR_GGR.14.desc:0 "In the middle of the night the GDR news agency announced that 'the measures have served their purpose'. The border troops are back in their barracks, the access routes are open. Our nerve has held."
 COLDWAR_GGR.14.t:0 "East Berlin Gives Way"
 COLDWAR_GGR.15.a:0 "Hold our course."
 COLDWAR_GGR.15.a.tt:0 "The countdown continues. Next month: another decision."
 COLDWAR_GGR.15.b:0 "Give way after all."
 COLDWAR_GGR.15.c:0 "Strike first."
 COLDWAR_GGR.15.desc:0 "East Berlin has not given way. The Soviet divisions in the GDR are on alert, NATO's commanders want instructions. Every day we hold our course, the risk grows - and so does the price of giving way.\n\nBundeswehr alert level: §Y[?cwgg_mob_brd|0]§! | NVA alert level: §Y[?cwgg_mob_ddr|0]§!"
 COLDWAR_GGR.15.t:0 "Countdown: [?cwgg_countdown|0] Months"
 COLDWAR_GGR.18.a:0 "Defer the decision."
 COLDWAR_GGR.18.b:0 "Open the border to everyone who flees instead."
 COLDWAR_GGR.18.c:0 "Send the Bundeswehr."
 COLDWAR_GGR.18.c.tt:0 "custom_effect_tooltip = COLDWAR_GER_1970_tt_brotherly"
 COLDWAR_GGR.18.desc:0 "The rising in the East is being crushed. The insurgents are asking the Federal Republic for help - the same help that Hungary in 1956 hoped for in vain. The Bundeswehr could be at the Elbe in two days. The question is who else would be."
 COLDWAR_GGR.18.t:0 "Brotherly Help?"
 COLDWAR_GGR.19.a:0 "Tear up the order."
 COLDWAR_GGR.19.a.tt:0 "The countdown continues."
 COLDWAR_GGR.19.b:0 "Sign."
 COLDWAR_GGR.19.b.tt:0 "custom_effect_tooltip = COLDWAR_GER_1970_tt_strike"
 COLDWAR_GGR.19.desc:0 "The Inspector General is waiting for a signature. Once it is given, the Bundeswehr crosses the inner-German border at dawn. Other governments decide whether to join through their existing alliance arrangements."
 COLDWAR_GGR.19.t:0 "The Order"
 COLDWAR_GGR.20.a:0 "Defer our response."
 COLDWAR_GGR.20.b:0 "Pay. Quiet is worth it."
 COLDWAR_GGR.20.c:0 "We do not pay for good behaviour."
 COLDWAR_GGR.20.desc:0 "Through the channel the other side has made an offer: the crisis ends quietly - for money. A credit, a transit payment, a few hundred million for 'humanitarian matters'."
 COLDWAR_GGR.20.t:0 "East Berlin Names a Price"
 COLDWAR_GGR.200.a:0 "Defer our order."
 COLDWAR_GGR.200.b:0 "Back down. The matter is not worth it."
 COLDWAR_GGR.200.b.tt:0 "We give way this round. Intensity falls - and Bonn will say it won."
 COLDWAR_GGR.200.c:0 "Stall. Time is on our side."
 COLDWAR_GGR.200.c.tt:0 "Neither yield nor push. This instruction must be submitted explicitly."
 COLDWAR_GGR.200.d:0 "Escalate. Bonn must learn what pressure means."
 COLDWAR_GGR.200.d.tt:0 "Costs §Y1§! initiative. Raises intensity, more so against a soft Bonn; blunted by a Bundeswehr on alert."
 COLDWAR_GGR.200.desc:0 "The Politburo meets in the Central Committee building on Werderscher Markt. Submit an explicit order for this round; it will remain confidential until the round resolves. The clock waits until every human player has chosen.\n\n§Y[RV_DDR_Crisis]§! | intensity §Y[?GER.cwgg_krise_int|0]§! | round §Y[?GER.cwgg_krise_runde|0]§! of §Y[?GER.cwgg_krise_max|0]§!\nBonn's course in the last round: §Y[RV_DDR_BonnLast]§! | our initiative §Y[?GER.cwgg_init_ddr|0]§!\nBundeswehr alert §Y[?GER.cwgg_mob_brd|0]§! | NVA alert §Y[?GER.cwgg_mob_ddr|0]§!"
 COLDWAR_GGR.200.e:0 "Call on Moscow."
 COLDWAR_GGR.200.e.tt:0 "Costs §Y1§! initiative. If Bonn calls the Allies at the same time, the superpowers take over."
 COLDWAR_GGR.200.f:0 "Name a price."
 COLDWAR_GGR.200.f.tt:0 "Costs §Y1§! initiative. If Bonn is talking, it may pay for quiet."
 COLDWAR_GGR.200.t:0 "Our Course in the Crisis"
 COLDWAR_GGR.201.a:0 "Noted."
 COLDWAR_GGR.201.desc1:0 "We have given way. Neues Deutschland speaks of 'provocations repelled'; in the Politburo nobody believes it, and the hard-liners are counting the cost."
 COLDWAR_GGR.201.desc2:0 "Bonn has given way. The Republic has defended its sovereignty, and the world has seen that the Federal Republic can be made to move."
 COLDWAR_GGR.201.desc3:0 "The crisis has frozen. Nobody gave way, nobody won - and the issue may flare up again."
 COLDWAR_GGR.201.desc4:0 "The Soviet ambassador came at night. By morning the crisis was over: Moscow has decided for us."
 COLDWAR_GGR.201.desc5:0 "A compromise. Both sides have moved, both governments call it a success, and the communiqué is long enough for everyone to find a sentence they like."
 COLDWAR_GGR.201.t:0 "The Crisis with Bonn Is Over"
 COLDWAR_GGR.21.a:0 "Verify the warning before issuing new orders."
 COLDWAR_GGR.21.b:0 "Call Moscow on the hotline."
 COLDWAR_GGR.21.c:0 "Stand down our own forces and hope they see it."
 COLDWAR_GGR.21.desc:0 "03:12. The early-warning radars of the Warsaw Pact report missiles in the air. The National People's Army has gone to combat readiness; in the GDR's air defence bunkers the officers are waiting for orders. Our own screens show nothing. In twenty minutes the question will answer itself."
 COLDWAR_GGR.21.t:0 "Launch Warning"
 COLDWAR_GGR.210.a:0 "Hold firm."
 COLDWAR_GGR.210.a.tt:0 "The countdown continues."
 COLDWAR_GGR.210.b:0 "Give way. The Republic will survive this."
 COLDWAR_GGR.210.desc:0 "Bonn will not give way. The Soviet divisions are on alert, the National People's Army waits for orders and the border troops have been told to expect anything. Every month we hold, the risk grows - and so does the price of giving way.\n\nWhen the countdown runs out and nobody has blinked, we decide between restraint and war.\n\n§Y[RV_DDR_Crisis]§! | intensity §Y[?GER.cwgg_krise_int|0]§! | round §Y[?GER.cwgg_krise_runde|0]§! of §Y[?GER.cwgg_krise_max|0]§!\nBonn's course in the last round: §Y[RV_DDR_BonnLast]§! | our initiative §Y[?GER.cwgg_init_ddr|0]§!\nBundeswehr alert §Y[?GER.cwgg_mob_brd|0]§! | NVA alert §Y[?GER.cwgg_mob_ddr|0]§!"
 COLDWAR_GGR.210.t:0 "Countdown: [?GER.cwgg_countdown|0] Months"
 COLDWAR_GGR.211.a:0 "Defer our decision."
 COLDWAR_GGR.211.b:0 "Accept Moscow's restraint."
 COLDWAR_GGR.211.b.tt:0 "The crisis ends. Bonn has won - but the decision was taken in the Kremlin."
 COLDWAR_GGR.211.c:0 "Order the attack on West Berlin."
 COLDWAR_GGR.211.c.tt:0 "§RWar with the Federal Republic begins.§! Needs the GDR to remain in the Soviet-led alliance, the NVA on alert level 2 and troops massed at the border."
 COLDWAR_GGR.211.d:0 "The order has lapsed. Return to the situation map."
 COLDWAR_GGR.211.desc:0 "Nobody has given way. Moscow's ambassador waits in the antechamber with a message from the Kremlin: the Soviet Union wants the crisis ended. Our generals have a different plan - West Berlin, in seventy-two hours.\n\n§Y[RV_DDR_Crisis]§! | intensity §Y[?GER.cwgg_krise_int|0]§! | round §Y[?GER.cwgg_krise_runde|0]§! of §Y[?GER.cwgg_krise_max|0]§!\nBonn's course in the last round: §Y[RV_DDR_BonnLast]§! | our initiative §Y[?GER.cwgg_init_ddr|0]§!\nBundeswehr alert §Y[?GER.cwgg_mob_brd|0]§! | NVA alert §Y[?GER.cwgg_mob_ddr|0]§!"
 COLDWAR_GGR.211.t:0 "The Countdown Has Run Out"
 COLDWAR_GGR.230.a:0 "For the socialist fatherland."
 COLDWAR_GGR.230.desc1:0 "The Bundeswehr has crossed the state border. The National People's Army is fighting on the Werra and the Elbe. Whether Moscow stands with us is decided in Moscow."
 COLDWAR_GGR.230.desc2:0 "Our divisions are moving on West Berlin. There is no way back now."
 COLDWAR_GGR.230.t:0 "War with the Federal Republic"
 COLDWAR_GGR.240.a:0 "Watch them closely."
 COLDWAR_GGR.240.b:0 "Open the situation map."
 COLDWAR_GGR.240.desc1:0 "BND and the border police report a concentration of troops of the National People's Army along the inner-German border. Escalation pressure and Cold War world tension rise every month the troops stay."
 COLDWAR_GGR.240.desc2:0 "BND and the border police report a deployment in force of the National People's Army along the inner-German border. Escalation pressure and Cold War world tension rise every month the troops stay. The ladder will not fall below §RCrisis§! while they are there."
 COLDWAR_GGR.240.desc3:0 "BND and the border police report a massive deployment of the National People's Army along the inner-German border. Escalation pressure and Cold War world tension rise every month the troops stay. The ladder will not fall below §RCrisis§! while they are there."
 COLDWAR_GGR.240.t:0 "Troops on the Other Side of the Border"
 COLDWAR_GGR.241.a:0 "The Republic will not be intimidated."
 COLDWAR_GGR.241.desc1:0 "Our border troops report a concentration of troops of the Bundeswehr and NATO along the state border. Escalation pressure and Cold War world tension rise every month the troops stay."
 COLDWAR_GGR.241.desc2:0 "Our border troops report a deployment in force of the Bundeswehr and NATO along the state border. Escalation pressure and Cold War world tension rise every month the troops stay. The ladder will not fall below §RCrisis§! while they are there."
 COLDWAR_GGR.241.desc3:0 "Our border troops report a massive deployment of the Bundeswehr and NATO along the state border. Escalation pressure and Cold War world tension rise every month the troops stay. The ladder will not fall below §RCrisis§! while they are there."
 COLDWAR_GGR.241.t:0 "The Bundeswehr at the Border"

 COLDWAR_GGR.251.b:0 "Accept the treaty."
 COLDWAR_GGR.251.c:0 "Refuse the treaty."
 COLDWAR_GGR.251.d:0 "The proposal has lapsed."
 COLDWAR_GGR.251.desc:0 "The Federal Government has signed the proposed Meeting of the Heads of Government. The agreement takes effect only if East Berlin accepts while its terms remain eligible. The treaty's existing negotiation costs have already been paid by its initiator."
 COLDWAR_GGR.251.t:0 "Bonn Signs: Meeting of the Heads of Government"
