 COLDWAR_GGR.260.a:0 "Keep the proposal under review."
 COLDWAR_GGR.260.b:0 "Accept the armistice."
 COLDWAR_GGR.260.c:0 "Reject the proposal."
 COLDWAR_GGR.260.desc:0 "The Federal Republic proposes an end to the fighting on the present lines. The decision rests with our government."
 COLDWAR_GGR.260.t:0 "Bonn Proposes an Armistice"
 COLDWAR_GGR.3.a:0 "Open the situation map."
 COLDWAR_GGR.3.b:0 "Noted."
 COLDWAR_GGR.3.desc1:0 "[RV_RoundReport]\n\nCrisis intensity: §Y[?cwgg_krise_int|0]§! after §Y[?cwgg_krise_runde|0]§! of §Y[?cwgg_krise_max|0]§! rounds.\n\nBoth governments must submit an order in the §YInner-German Relations§! window. The round remains open until every human player has chosen."
 COLDWAR_GGR.3.t:0 "Crisis Report: Round [?cwgg_krise_runde|0]"
 COLDWAR_GGR.30.a:0 "Defend the free part of Germany."
 COLDWAR_GGR.30.desc1:0 "We have attacked. The Bundestag and Bundesrat have declared the state of defence under Article 115a of the Basic Law - a constitution written for a defensive war now carries an offensive one. Command of the armed forces passes to the Chancellor."
 COLDWAR_GGR.30.desc2:0 "The National People's Army has crossed the border. West Berlin is under fire. The Bundestag and Bundesrat have declared the state of defence under Article 115a of the Basic Law; command of the armed forces passes to the Chancellor."
 COLDWAR_GGR.30.desc3:0 "The Bundeswehr is crossing the Elbe to help the rising in the East. The Bundestag has declared the state of defence; command passes to the Chancellor. Whether the Soviet Union will stand aside is the only question that matters now."
 COLDWAR_GGR.30.desc4:0 "A false alarm became a real war. Nobody in Bonn or East Berlin wanted it; both armies are now fighting it. The Bundestag has declared the state of defence under Article 115a."
 COLDWAR_GGR.30.t:0 "The State of Defence"
 COLDWAR_GGR.31.a:0 "Keep the question under review."
 COLDWAR_GGR.31.b:0 "Propose an armistice."
 COLDWAR_GGR.31.c:0 "Continue operations."
 COLDWAR_GGR.31.desc:0 "The fighting continues. The federal cabinet may propose an armistice on the current lines. East Berlin decides whether to accept."
 COLDWAR_GGR.31.t:0 "The Threshold"
 COLDWAR_GGR.40.a:0 "Review the settlement later."
 COLDWAR_GGR.40.b:0 "Now we must win the peace."
 COLDWAR_GGR.40.desc:0 "The GDR has fallen. The Bundeswehr stands on the Oder, the SED leadership has fled or been arrested, and in the East the flags of the Federal Republic hang next to white sheets. Germany is united - by force of arms, against the will of half of Europe and with a debt to the East that will take a generation to pay."
 COLDWAR_GGR.40.t:0 "Germany Under One Government"
 COLDWAR_GGR.41.a:0 "Review the terms later."
 COLDWAR_GGR.41.b:0 "Accept the terms."
 COLDWAR_GGR.41.desc:0 "The front has broken. West Berlin is lost, and in Moscow the terms are being written: a neutral Federal Republic, outside NATO, with an army the Warsaw Pact can count."
 COLDWAR_GGR.41.t:0 "Defeat"
 COLDWAR_GGR.42.a:0 "Never again."
 COLDWAR_GGR.42.desc:0 "The guns along the inner-German border have fallen silent. Nothing has been won; the dead are counted on both sides. The two German states remain - and hate each other more than at any time since 1961."
 COLDWAR_GGR.42.t:0 "An Armistice"
 COLDWAR_GGR.5.a:0 "Open the situation map."
 COLDWAR_GGR.5.b:0 "Noted."
 COLDWAR_GGR.5.desc1:0 "Relations with the GDR have reached the stage of §RConfrontation§!. Trade is halved, the armies watch each other along the border and every incident could turn into a crisis that neither side controls."
 COLDWAR_GGR.5.desc2:0 "§RWar danger.§! Both German armies are on alert, the superpowers are on the telephone and the newspapers are printing maps of the Fulda Gap. Every decision in the next weeks can decide between peace and war."
 COLDWAR_GGR.5.t:0 "The Inner-German Relationship Escalates"
 COLDWAR_GGR.50.a:0 "Review this offer later."
 COLDWAR_GGR.50.b:0 "Sign it."
 COLDWAR_GGR.50.c:0 "This proposal has lapsed."
 COLDWAR_GGR.50.d:0 "Decline the proposal."
 COLDWAR_GGR.50.desc1:0 "§YMeeting of the Heads of Government§!\n\nWilly Brandt and Willi Stoph met in Erfurt in March 1970 and in Kassel in May. Nothing was agreed - but for the first time the two German governments talked to each other.\n\nThe negotiators have finished their work. Bonn must sign, then a human East Berlin must accept or refuse."
 COLDWAR_GGR.50.desc2:0 "§YBerlin Settlement§!\n\nThe Quadripartite Agreement of September 1971 and the transit agreement that followed: unhindered traffic between the Federal Republic and West Berlin, guaranteed by the Four Powers.\n\nThe negotiators have finished their work. Bonn must sign, then a human East Berlin must accept or refuse."
 COLDWAR_GGR.50.desc3:0 "§YBasic Treaty§!\n\nThe Grundlagenvertrag of December 1972: two German states, equal rights, good-neighbourly relations - and Bonn's letter on German unity, so that nothing is given up for ever.\n\nThe negotiators have finished their work. Bonn must sign, then a human East Berlin must accept or refuse."
 COLDWAR_GGR.50.desc4:0 "§YJoint UN Membership Applications§!\n\nCoordinate applications for UN membership. Admission requires approval through the Security Council and General Assembly.\n\nThe negotiators have finished their work. Bonn must sign, then a human East Berlin must accept or refuse."
 COLDWAR_GGR.50.desc5:0 "§YPermanent Representations§!\n\nMissions, not embassies: Günter Gaus moved into Hannoversche Straße in East Berlin in 1974, Michael Kohl into Godesberger Allee in Bonn.\n\nThe negotiators have finished their work. Bonn must sign, then a human East Berlin must accept or refuse."
 COLDWAR_GGR.50.desc6:0 "§YTraffic, Post and Travel Agreements§!\n\nTelephone lines, new autobahn crossings, visits for pensioners and urgent family matters: the small steps of the 1970s and 1980s.\n\nThe negotiators have finished their work. Bonn must sign, then a human East Berlin must accept or refuse."
 COLDWAR_GGR.50.desc7:0 "§YCultural Agreement and Town Twinning§!\n\nAfter thirteen years of talks the cultural agreement was signed in May 1986; Saarlouis and Eisenhüttenstadt became the first twinned towns.\n\nThe negotiators have finished their work. Bonn must sign, then a human East Berlin must accept or refuse."
 COLDWAR_GGR.50.desc8:0 "§YState Visit of the SED Leader§!\n\nIn September 1987 Erich Honecker was received in Bonn with flags and anthems - and spoke of a border that would one day 'unite rather than divide'.\n\nThe negotiators have finished their work. Bonn must sign, then a human East Berlin must accept or refuse."
 COLDWAR_GGR.50.desc9:0 "§YTreaty Community and Confederation§!\n\nA treaty community between the two German states, with joint commissions, a common market and, one day, confederal institutions.\n\nThe negotiators have finished their work. Bonn must sign, then a human East Berlin must accept or refuse."
 COLDWAR_GGR.50.t:0 "A Treaty Is Ready"
 COLDWAR_GGR.51.a:0 "We will try again with a new majority."
 COLDWAR_GGR.51.desc:0 "The government no longer has a majority for the treaty. The opposition calls it a sell-out of German unity, and enough deputies of the coalition agree. The treaty stays unsigned."
 COLDWAR_GGR.51.t:0 "Ratification Fails"
 COLDWAR_GGR.60.a:0 "Leave the request under review."
 COLDWAR_GGR.60.b:0 "Grant it - for humanitarian concessions."
 COLDWAR_GGR.60.c:0 "Let them stew."
 COLDWAR_GGR.60.desc:0 "Through the Schalck-Golodkowski channel East Berlin lets it be known that the GDR's hard-currency position is 'tight'. A credit would be received with gratitude - and with gestures in return."
 COLDWAR_GGR.60.t:0 "East Berlin Needs Money"
 COLDWAR_GGR.70.a:0 "Make it public."
 COLDWAR_GGR.70.b:0 "Use it quietly."
 COLDWAR_GGR.70.desc:0 "The arrests of the HVA network have brought out something nobody expected: since 1980 the Stasi has given new identities to members of the Red Army Faction who wanted to leave the underground - and has trained others. East Berlin denies everything."
 COLDWAR_GGR.70.t:0 "RAF Fugitives in the GDR"
 COLDWAR_GGU.1.a:0 "Defer our answer."
 COLDWAR_GGU.1.b:0 "We will negotiate - on equal terms."
 COLDWAR_GGU.1.c:0 "The GDR is a sovereign socialist state. No."
 COLDWAR_GGU.1.desc:0 "The Federal Chancellor has proposed formal negotiations on the unity of Germany - not as an annexation, Bonn insists, but as a treaty between equals. Five chapters would be on the table: the constitution, the economic order, the alliance, the capital and the borders. Every one of the Four Powers would have to agree."
 COLDWAR_GGU.1.t:0 "Bonn Proposes Unity Talks"
 COLDWAR_GGU.2.a:0 "Defer our answer."
 COLDWAR_GGU.2.b:0 "We accept."
 COLDWAR_GGU.2.c:0 "Not under these conditions."
 COLDWAR_GGU.2.desc:0 "The GDR's government has proposed formal negotiations on the unity of Germany. Some in Bonn call it a trap, some the chance of a century. If we accept, every chapter - the constitution, the economy, the alliance, the capital, the borders - is open."
 COLDWAR_GGU.2.t:0 "East Berlin Proposes Unity Talks"
 COLDWAR_GGU.20.a:0 "Next chapter."
 COLDWAR_GGU.20.desc1:0 "Chapter: §Y[U_LastChapter]§!. We proposed §Y[U_LastPos]§!, East Berlin §Y[U_LastDPos]§!. $COLDWAR_GER_1970_u_rr_ok$\n\nAgreed so far: §Y[?cwgg_u_agreed|0]§! of five chapters. Failed rounds: §Y[?cwgg_u_fail|0]§!/8."
 COLDWAR_GGU.20.desc2:0 "Chapter: §Y[U_LastChapter]§!. We proposed §Y[U_LastPos]§!, East Berlin §Y[U_LastDPos]§!. $COLDWAR_GER_1970_u_rr_fail$\n\nFailed rounds: §Y[?cwgg_u_fail|0]§!/8. A delegation that has failed on a chapter often enough tends to soften its line - but nothing obliges it to."
 COLDWAR_GGU.20.t:0 "A Round of Unity Talks"
 COLDWAR_GGU.21.a:0 "Next chapter."
 COLDWAR_GGU.21.desc1:0 "Chapter: §Y[U_LastChapterG]§!. Bonn proposed §Y[U_LastPosG]§!, we §Y[U_LastDPosG]§!. $COLDWAR_GER_1970_u_rr_ok$"
 COLDWAR_GGU.21.desc2:0 "Chapter: §Y[U_LastChapterG]§!. Bonn proposed §Y[U_LastPosG]§!, we §Y[U_LastDPosG]§!. $COLDWAR_GER_1970_u_rr_fail$\n\nFailed rounds: §Y[?GER.cwgg_u_fail|0]§!/8."
 COLDWAR_GGU.21.t:0 "A Round of Unity Talks"
 COLDWAR_GGU.3.a:0 "Then we keep building trust."
 COLDWAR_GGU.3.desc:0 "The GDR has rejected unity talks. 'Socialism and imperialism cannot be united, any more than fire and water,' says the Politburo's statement. For two years the subject is closed."
 COLDWAR_GGU.3.t:0 "East Berlin Says No"
 COLDWAR_GGU.31.a:0 "Defer our position."
 COLDWAR_GGU.31.b:0 "The Basic Law (Article 23)"
 COLDWAR_GGU.31.c:0 "A New Constitution (Article 146)"
 COLDWAR_GGU.31.d:0 "A Socialist Constitution"
 COLDWAR_GGU.31.desc:0 "Under which constitution do the Germans live together? The round is decided in three months. Bonn's delegation will state its own position; if both are the same, the chapter is agreed.\n\n§YThe Basic Law (Article 23)§!: The GDR's Länder accede to the Federal Republic. The Basic Law applies everywhere.\n§YA New Constitution (Article 146)§!: A constituent assembly from both states writes a new constitution for all Germans.\n§YA Socialist Constitution§!: The united Germany is built on the GDR's constitution: a people's republic with a leading party."
 COLDWAR_GGU.31.e:0 "We refuse to discuss this chapter now."
 COLDWAR_GGU.31.t:0 "Unity Talks: The Constitution"
 COLDWAR_GGU.32.a:0 "Defer our position."
 COLDWAR_GGU.32.b:0 "Social Market Economy"
 COLDWAR_GGU.32.c:0 "A Mixed Economy"
 COLDWAR_GGU.32.d:0 "Planned Economy"
 COLDWAR_GGU.32.desc:0 "Which economic order does the united state have? The round is decided in three months. Bonn's delegation will state its own position; if both are the same, the chapter is agreed.\n\n§YSocial Market Economy§!: The Deutschmark, private property and free prices - the GDR's combines are privatised.\n§YA Mixed Economy§!: Key industries, banks and land stay public; the rest is market. A 'third way' between the systems.\n§YPlanned Economy§!: Central planning, people's enterprises, prices set by the state - the Federal Republic's industry is nationalised."
 COLDWAR_GGU.32.e:0 "We refuse to discuss this chapter now."
 COLDWAR_GGU.32.t:0 "Unity Talks: The Economy"
 COLDWAR_GGU.33.a:0 "Defer our position."
 COLDWAR_GGU.33.b:0 "In NATO"
 COLDWAR_GGU.33.c:0 "Armed Neutrality"
 COLDWAR_GGU.33.d:0 "In the Warsaw Pact"
 COLDWAR_GGU.33.desc:0 "In which alliance - if any - does the united Germany stand? The round is decided in three months. Bonn's delegation will state its own position; if both are the same, the chapter is agreed.\n\n§YIn NATO§!: The united Germany stays in NATO; Soviet troops leave the East.\n§YArmed Neutrality§!: Germany leaves both blocs: an army of its own, no foreign troops, guaranteed by the Four Powers.\n§YIn the Warsaw Pact§!: The united Germany joins the Warsaw Treaty Organisation; American troops leave the West."
 COLDWAR_GGU.33.e:0 "We refuse to discuss this chapter now."
 COLDWAR_GGU.33.t:0 "Unity Talks: The Alliance"
 COLDWAR_GGU.34.a:0 "Defer our position."
 COLDWAR_GGU.34.b:0 "Bonn, Federal"
 COLDWAR_GGU.34.c:0 "Berlin, Federal"
 COLDWAR_GGU.34.d:0 "Berlin, Centralised"
 COLDWAR_GGU.34.desc:0 "Where does the united Germany govern from - and how centralised is it? The round is decided in three months. Bonn's delegation will state its own position; if both are the same, the chapter is agreed.\n\n§YBonn, Federal§!: Government and parliament stay on the Rhine; the GDR is divided into Länder again.\n§YBerlin, Federal§!: Berlin becomes the capital of a federal Germany; the eastern Länder are restored.\n§YBerlin, Centralised§!: Berlin governs a centralised state; the Länder become administrative districts."
 COLDWAR_GGU.34.e:0 "We refuse to discuss this chapter now."
 COLDWAR_GGU.34.t:0 "Unity Talks: The Capital"
 COLDWAR_GGU.35.a:0 "Defer our position."
 COLDWAR_GGU.35.b:0 "Reserve the Peace Treaty"
 COLDWAR_GGU.35.c:0 "The Oder-Neisse Line, Final"
 COLDWAR_GGU.35.d:0 "Border and Peace Treaty"
 COLDWAR_GGU.35.desc:0 "What becomes of the Oder-Neisse line and of a peace treaty for Germany? The round is decided in three months. Bonn's delegation will state its own position; if both are the same, the chapter is agreed.\n\n§YReserve the Peace Treaty§!: The border question stays open until a peace treaty - as the Federal Constitutional Court demands.\n§YThe Oder-Neisse Line, Final§!: The united Germany recognises its eastern border for ever in a treaty with Poland.\n§YBorder and Peace Treaty§!: A formal peace treaty with the Four Powers and recognition of every post-war border."
 COLDWAR_GGU.35.e:0 "We refuse to discuss this chapter now."
 COLDWAR_GGU.35.t:0 "Unity Talks: The Borders"
 COLDWAR_GGU.4.a:0 "To work."
 COLDWAR_GGU.4.desc:0 "Delegations from Bonn and East Berlin meet at a long table. First on the agenda: the constitution. One chapter is negotiated every three months; set our position in the §YUnity§! tab of the inner-German relations window."
 COLDWAR_GGU.4.t:0 "The Unity Talks Begin"
 COLDWAR_GGU.41.a:0 "Defer the decision."
 COLDWAR_GGU.41.b:0 "We consent."
 COLDWAR_GGU.41.c:0 "Veto: a united Germany cannot stay in NATO."
 COLDWAR_GGU.41.d:0 "Veto: we will not hand the GDR to capitalism."
 COLDWAR_GGU.41.desc:0 "Bonn and East Berlin have initialled a treaty on German unity. As one of the Four Powers responsible for Germany as a whole, the Soviet Union must agree - or say what it demands.\n\nThe treaty: constitution §Y[U_ChG1]§!, economy §Y[U_ChG2]§!, alliance §Y[U_ChG3]§!, capital §Y[U_ChG4]§!, borders §Y[U_ChG5]§!."
 COLDWAR_GGU.41.e:0 "Veto outright: two German states, now and for ever."
 COLDWAR_GGU.41.t:0 "The Germans Want to Unite"
 COLDWAR_GGU.42.a:0 "Defer the decision."
 COLDWAR_GGU.42.b:0 "We consent."
 COLDWAR_GGU.42.c:0 "Veto: Germany must stay in the Western alliance."
 COLDWAR_GGU.42.d:0 "Veto: no socialist Germany."
 COLDWAR_GGU.42.desc:0 "Bonn and East Berlin have initialled a treaty on German unity. As one of the Four Powers that still hold rights for Germany as a whole and Berlin, the United States must agree - or say what it demands.\n\nThe treaty: constitution §Y[U_ChG1]§!, economy §Y[U_ChG2]§!, alliance §Y[U_ChG3]§!, capital §Y[U_ChG4]§!, borders §Y[U_ChG5]§!."
 COLDWAR_GGU.42.e:0 "Veto outright: we prefer two Germanies."

 COLDWAR_GGU.43.d:0 "Veto: the border must be settled for good first."

As one of the Four Powers that still hold rights for Germany as a whole and Berlin, the United Kingdom must agree - or say what it demands.\n\nThe treaty: constitution §Y[U_ChG1]§!, economy §Y[U_ChG2]§!, alliance §Y[U_ChG3]§!, capital §Y[U_ChG4]§!, borders §Y[U_ChG5]§!."

As one of the Four Powers that still hold rights for Germany as a whole and Berlin, France must agree - or say what it demands.\n\nThe treaty: constitution §Y[U_ChG1]§!, economy §Y[U_ChG2]§!, alliance §Y[U_ChG3]§!, capital §Y[U_ChG4]§!, borders §Y[U_ChG5]§!."

 COLDWAR_GGU.45.a:0 "Back to the table."
 COLDWAR_GGU.45.desc:0 "One of the Four Powers has vetoed the treaty and named its price. The chapter it objects to is open again - the delegations must go back to the table. A third veto would end the talks."
 COLDWAR_GGU.45.t:0 "The Powers Demand Changes"
 COLDWAR_GGU.50.a:0 "Defer ratification."
 COLDWAR_GGU.50.b:0 "The Bundestag ratifies."
 COLDWAR_GGU.50.c:0 "Pay the opposition's price for its votes."
 COLDWAR_GGU.50.d:0 "Let the people decide: a referendum on unity."
 COLDWAR_GGU.50.desc:0 "The Four Powers have agreed. Now the Bundestag must ratify the treaty - with a simple majority, or with two thirds if Germany is to receive a new constitution."
 COLDWAR_GGU.50.e:0 "The Bundestag rejects the treaty."
 COLDWAR_GGU.50.t:0 "The Bundestag and the Unity Treaty"
 COLDWAR_GGU.51.a:0 "Defer ratification."
 COLDWAR_GGU.51.b:0 "The People's Chamber ratifies."
 COLDWAR_GGU.51.c:0 "The People's Chamber rejects it."
 COLDWAR_GGU.51.desc:0 "The Four Powers have agreed. The People's Chamber must now ratify the treaty that ends the German Democratic Republic as a separate state."
 COLDWAR_GGU.51.t:0 "The Volkskammer and the Unity Treaty"
 COLDWAR_GGU.60.a:0 "History has not finished with us."
 COLDWAR_GGU.60.desc:0 "The negotiations on German unity have ended without a treaty. Both governments blame each other; the climate between the two states suffers. The subject is closed for at least three years."
 COLDWAR_GGU.60.t:0 "The Unity Talks Have Failed"
 COLDWAR_GGW.1.a:0 "Let the families come - and pay for the schools."
 COLDWAR_GGW.1.b:0 "Age limits and waiting periods."
 COLDWAR_GGW.1.desc:0 "The Bundesrat has asked for a decision. The cities want money for schools, language courses and housing; the interior ministers of the Union-led Länder want age limits for children who may join their parents. Employers point out that a worker with his family at home works better than one who is homesick."
 COLDWAR_GGW.1.t:0 "Family Reunification"
 COLDWAR_GGW.2.a:0 "The refugees only. The factories need the workers."
 COLDWAR_GGW.2.b:0 "The guest workers go as well."
 COLDWAR_GGW.2.desc:0 "The Directorate proposes extending repatriation to guest workers and their families. Industry warns of disruption, while the sending countries demand consultation. Any return must be authorised community by community."
 COLDWAR_GGW.2.t:0 "The Guest Workers"
 COLDWAR_GSEC.1.a:0 "ok"
 COLDWAR_GSEC.10.a:0 "The protection details have earned their pay."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.10.desc1:0 "A commando was waiting outside the home of a senior judge. The protection detail noticed the parked van an hour too early for the attackers; the suspects fled, leaving weapons and a target file behind."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.10.desc2:0 "The car of a bank chairman took a different route this morning. Where it would have passed, the police found a bomb wired to a light barrier."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.10.desc3:0 "Military police at a US Army depot stopped a car with forged papers. In the boot: explosives and the plan of the officers' mess."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.10.desc4:0 "A minister's convoy was ready for the ambush its escorts had trained for. Shots were exchanged; the commando escaped, but the minister is unhurt."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.10.desc5:0 "Guards at the building site of a new prison surprised a group carrying explosives over the fence at night."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.10.desc6:0 "The embassy in a neighbouring capital had been warned by the BKA. When armed men tried to enter, the doors were locked and the local police waiting."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.10.t:0 "Attack Foiled"
 COLDWAR_GSEC.11.a:0 "One fewer."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.11.desc:0 "Special commandos have arrested §Y[SEC_LastName]§!, one of the most wanted members of the Red Army Faction. Weapons, forged papers and a list of possible targets were found in the flat."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.11.t:0 "Arrested"
 COLDWAR_GSEC.12.a:0 "Defend the officers."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.12.b:0 "Order an inquiry."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.12.desc:0 "The flat was empty, or the shooting started too early. The suspect has escaped - and a raid that went wrong is on every front page. Whose fault was it?"
 COLDWAR_GSEC.12.t:0 "The Trap Closes on Nothing"
 COLDWAR_GSEC.13.a:0 "The state could not prevent it."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.13.desc:0 "A prisoner has died after weeks without food. Thousands march in Berlin, Frankfurt and Hamburg; on the walls of the universities new slogans appear overnight. The movement has a martyr."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.13.t:0 "A Hunger Striker Dies"
 COLDWAR_GSEC.14.a:0 "Order a full inquiry."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.14.b:0 "The officers acted in self-defence."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.14.desc:0 "The commando opened fire the moment the door gave way. When the smoke cleared, a police officer lay dead on the landing - and the suspect was either dead too or gone over the rooftops. By the evening there are two versions of what happened, and the sympathisers believe only one."
 COLDWAR_GSEC.14.t:0 "Shots in the Stairwell"

 cwgg_rv_al_ddr_lbl:0 "National People's Army: alert level §Y[?cwgg_mob_ddr|0]§!"
 cwgg_rv_al_tt:0 "§YAlert levels§! (0-3) of the Bundeswehr and the National People's Army. Each step speeds up mobilisation and hardens war support:\n  level 1: mobilisation speed +10%, war support +2%\n  level 2: mobilisation speed +25%, war support +5%\n  level 3: mobilisation speed +50%, war support +10%\n\nHigher readiness deters the other side from escalating in a crisis and feeds the peace movement. Both armies on level 3 means §Rwar danger§!. Bonn raises its level in the §YLevers§! tab; a human East Berlin uses its decisions."

 cwgg_rv_ans_yield:0 "§Ybacks down§!"
 cwgg_rv_aufm_0:0 "§Gpeacetime garrisons§!"
 cwgg_rv_aufm_1:0 "§Yconcentration§!"

 cwgg_rv_aufm_brd:0 "Troops at the border: §Y[?cwgg_aufm_brd_div|0]§! div. - [RV_Aufm_brd]"
 cwgg_rv_aufm_ddr:0 "Troops at the border: §Y[?cwgg_aufm_ddr_div|0]§! div. - [RV_Aufm_ddr]"
 cwgg_rv_aufm_tt:0 "§YTroops at the inner-German border§!\nThe divisions each side has stationed in its border states - Schleswig-Holstein, Lower Saxony, Hesse, Franconia, Bavaria and West Berlin on our side; Mecklenburg, Saxony-Anhalt, Thuringia, Saxony, Brandenburg and East Berlin on theirs. The count is updated whenever this window refreshes; its effects apply once a month.\n\n  concentration (4+ divisions): escalation pressure +3, climate -1 a month\n  deployment in force (10+ divisions): escalation pressure +6, climate -2, Cold War world tension +0.25 a month\n  massive deployment (20+ divisions): escalation pressure +10, climate -4, Cold War world tension +0.5 a month\n\nA deployment in force by either side keeps the ladder at §RCrisis§! or worse; both sides deployed means §RConfrontation§!, both massively deployed and on alert means §Rwar danger§!. Border exercises, a first strike or brotherly help need our troops there."

 cwgg_rv_btn_alert_down:0 "Stand Down"
 cwgg_rv_btn_alert_down_tt:0 "§YLower Alert Level§!\nStand the forces down by one level.\nCosts nothing; climate §G+2§!.\n[RV_Avail_alert_down]"
 cwgg_rv_btn_alert_up:0 "Raise Alert"
 cwgg_rv_btn_alert_up_tt:0 "§YRaise Alert Level§!\nPut the Bundeswehr on a higher state of readiness. Each level speeds up mobilisation and hardens war support: level 1 §G+10%§! / §G+2%§!, level 2 §G+25%§! / §G+5%§!, level 3 §G+50%§! / §G+10%§!.\n\nCost: §Y2 initiative§!. Can be repeated after 1 months.\nRequires: the stage Crisis for level 1, Confrontation for level 2, War Danger (or the focus §YPrepare the State of Defence§!) for level 3.\n[RV_Avail_alert_up]"
 cwgg_rv_btn_church:0 "Church Aid"
 cwgg_rv_btn_church_tt:0 "§YAid for the Church Groups§!\nMoney, paper and photocopiers for the peace and environment groups sheltering under the Protestant church in the East.\n\nCost: §Y1 initiative, 25 political power§!. Can be repeated after 18 months.\nRequires: the church channel open.\n[RV_Avail_church]"
 cwgg_rv_btn_credit:0 "Billion Credit"
 cwgg_rv_btn_credit_tt:0 "§YThe Milliardenkredit§!\nA state-guaranteed bank loan of one billion marks for a GDR close to insolvency - in exchange for gestures at the border.\n\nCost: §Y2 initiative, 50 political power§!. Once only.\nRequires: a CDU/CSU chancellor or the Schalck-Golodkowski channel open; the GDR's hard-currency shortage above 40; once only.\n[RV_Avail_credit]"
 cwgg_rv_btn_escape:0 "Escape Help"
 cwgg_rv_btn_escape_tt:0 "§YTolerate Escape Helpers§!\nLook away while students and professional smugglers dig tunnels and fit out cars with hidden compartments.\n\nCost: §Y1 initiative§!. Can be repeated after 12 months.\nRequires: -.\n[RV_Avail_escape]"
 cwgg_rv_btn_freeze:0 "Freeze"
 cwgg_rv_btn_freeze_tt:0 "§YFreeze Credits and Deliveries§!\nSuspend credits and slow deliveries in inner-German trade until East Berlin moves.\n\nCost: §Y2 initiative, 25 political power§!. Can be repeated after 24 months.\nRequires: the trade lever above 0.\n[RV_Avail_freeze]"
 cwgg_rv_btn_freikauf:0 "Buy Free"
 cwgg_rv_btn_freikauf_tt:0 "§YBuy Prisoners Free§!\nPay for the release of political prisoners through the lawyers' channel.\n\nCost: §Y1 initiative§!. Can be repeated after 12 months.\nRequires: the Vogel - Stange channel open.\n[RV_Avail_freikauf]"
 cwgg_rv_btn_mandate:0 "Mandate"
 cwgg_rv_btn_mandate_tt:0 "§YReassert the Sole Mandate§!\nRemind the world that only the Federal Republic speaks for Germany. Third states that recognise the GDR will hear from Bonn.\n\nCost: §Y1 initiative, 25 political power§!. Can be repeated after 12 months.\nRequires: no Basic Treaty yet.\n[RV_Avail_mandate]"
 cwgg_rv_btn_manoeuvre:0 "Manoeuvres"
 cwgg_rv_btn_manoeuvre_tt:0 "§YExercises Near the Border§!\nLarge Bundeswehr and NATO exercises along the inner-German border: a signal to East Berlin and Moscow.\n\nCost: §Y2 initiative, 25 political power§!. Can be repeated after 12 months.\nRequires: the focus §YForward Defence§! and Bundeswehr divisions massed at the border (at least a concentration).\n[RV_Avail_manoeuvre]"
 cwgg_rv_btn_media:0 "Media Push"
 cwgg_rv_btn_media_tt:0 "§YMedia Offensive§!\nMore airtime for the GDR on RIAS and Deutsche Welle, more correspondents in East Berlin, more pictures of what happens at the border.\n\nCost: §Y1 initiative, 25 political power§!. Can be repeated after 12 months.\nRequires: the media lever above 0.\n[RV_Avail_media]"
 cwgg_rv_btn_raid:0 "Stasi Raid"
 cwgg_rv_btn_raid_tt:0 "§YRoll Up Stasi Networks§!\nA coordinated strike by the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution and the Federal Prosecutor against the HVA's networks.\n\nCost: §Y2 initiative, 50 political power§!. Can be repeated after 12 months.\nRequires: -.\n[RV_Avail_raid]"
 cwgg_rv_btn_swing:0 "Raise Swing"
 cwgg_rv_btn_swing_tt:0 "§YRaise the Swing§!\nOffer a larger interest-free overdraft in inner-German trade, delivered as an Imperia §YConsumer Supply Credits§! programme if East Berlin accepts.\n\nCost: §Y1 initiative, 25 political power§!. Can be repeated after 36 months.\nRequires: the Swing is unlocked or the hard-currency lever is above 0; the GDR's border is still closed.\n[RV_Avail_swing]"
 cwgg_rv_btn_transit:0 "Transit Sum"
 cwgg_rv_btn_transit_tt:0 "§YTransit Lump Sum§!\nPay East Berlin a fixed annual sum for unhindered transit to West Berlin.\n\nCost: §Y1 initiative§!. Can be repeated after 61 months.\nRequires: the Berlin settlement in force.\n[RV_Avail_transit]"

 cwgg_rv_st_allies:0 "Call in the Allies"
 cwgg_rv_st_allies_row:0 "§Y1 initiative§! - the Three Powers speak for Berlin (NATO members only)."
 cwgg_rv_st_allies_tt:0 "§YCall in the Allies§!\nAsk Washington, London and Paris to speak for Berlin and Germany as a whole. Needs NATO membership - and if Moscow is called too, the crisis is no longer ours.\n\nAgainst each answer of East Berlin:\n  East Berlin backs down: intensity -22\n  East Berlin stalls: intensity -8\n  East Berlin escalates: intensity +8\n  East Berlin calls on moscow: intensity +15\n  East Berlin makes a counter-offer: intensity -8\n\n§GThe right answer to:§! Transit Crisis, Missile Crisis (intensity §G-10§!).\n\nIt only costs anything when the round is resolved. Without enough initiative at that moment, Bonn waits and sees."
 cwgg_rv_st_deescalate:0 "De-escalate"
 cwgg_rv_st_deescalate_row:0 "§Y1 initiative§! - conciliatory signals; lowers intensity, invites pressure."
 cwgg_rv_st_deescalate_tt:0 "§YDe-escalate§!\nLower the temperature: conciliatory statements, a postponed visit, a quiet word in the ear of the Permanent Representation.\n\nAgainst each answer of East Berlin:\n  East Berlin backs down: intensity -30\n  East Berlin stalls: intensity -15\n  East Berlin escalates: intensity +8\n  East Berlin calls on moscow: intensity +0\n  East Berlin makes a counter-offer: intensity -22\n\n§GThe right answer to:§! Manoeuvre Crisis (intensity §G-10§!).\n\nIt only costs anything when the round is resolved. Without enough initiative at that moment, Bonn waits and sees."
 cwgg_rv_st_firm:0 "Stand Firm"
 cwgg_rv_st_firm_row:0 "§Y1 initiative, 10 political power§! - hold the line without adding pressure."
 cwgg_rv_st_firm_tt:0 "§YStand Firm§!\nMake clear that Bonn will not give way - without adding new pressure of its own.\n\nAgainst each answer of East Berlin:\n  East Berlin backs down: intensity -15\n  East Berlin stalls: intensity +8\n  East Berlin escalates: intensity +22\n  East Berlin calls on moscow: intensity +22\n  East Berlin makes a counter-offer: intensity +8\n\n§GThe right answer to:§! Border Incident, Recognition Crisis, Elbe Border Dispute (intensity §G-10§!).\n\nIt only costs anything when the round is resolved. Without enough initiative at that moment, Bonn waits and sees."
 cwgg_rv_st_mobilise:0 "Prepare Mobilisation"
 cwgg_rv_st_mobilise_row:0 "§Y3 initiative§! - raise readiness: deters escalation - and escalates."
 cwgg_rv_st_mobilise_tt:0 "§YPrepare Mobilisation§!\nRaise readiness and say so. Deters escalation - and escalates.\n\nAgainst each answer of East Berlin:\n  East Berlin backs down: intensity -22\n  East Berlin stalls: intensity +15\n  East Berlin escalates: intensity +45\n  East Berlin calls on moscow: intensity +45\n  East Berlin makes a counter-offer: intensity +22\n\nIt only costs anything when the round is resolved.  cwgg_rv_st_pressure_row:0 "§Y2 initiative§! - use the lever that bites in this crisis."
 cwgg_rv_st_pressure_tt:0 "§YCounter-Pressure§!\nUse the lever that hurts East Berlin most in this crisis. Strong if the lever is strong, a bluff if it is not.\n\nAgainst each answer of East Berlin:\n  East Berlin backs down: intensity -15\n  East Berlin stalls: intensity +8\n  East Berlin escalates: intensity +38\n  East Berlin calls on moscow: intensity +38\n  East Berlin makes a counter-offer: intensity +15\n\n§GThe right answer to:§! Dissident Crisis (intensity §G-10§!).\n\nIt only costs anything when the round is resolved. Without enough initiative at that moment, Bonn waits and sees."

 cwgg_rv_stage_tt_0:0 "§Y0: Modus Vivendi§!\nTwo states have settled into a working relationship: visits, credits, treaties and a border that is quieter than it has ever been.\n\nStability +3%, war support -5%, consumer goods -1%, Cold War world tension -0.3 a month."
 cwgg_rv_stage_tt_1:0 "§Y1: Cool Coexistence§!\nCorrect, cautious and transactional. Neither side expects much, neither side wants trouble.\n\nStability +1%, war support +0%."
 cwgg_rv_stage_tt_2:0 "§Y2: Tensions§!\nHarsh words in Neues Deutschland and the Bundestag, incidents at the border, channels running cold.\n\nStability -2%, war support +3%, Cold War world tension +0.2 a month."
 cwgg_rv_stage_tt_3:0 "§Y3: Crisis§!\nA confrontation is under way. Every move is watched in Washington and Moscow.\n\nStability -4%, war support +6%, Cold War world tension +0.5 a month."
 cwgg_rv_stage_tt_4:0 "§Y4: Confrontation§!\nBoth states treat each other as enemies. Trade has halved, the armies are watching the border.\n\nStability -6%, war support +10%, consumer goods +2%, Cold War world tension +1.0 a month."
 cwgg_rv_stage_tt_5:0 "§Y5: War Danger§!\nTroops on alert on both sides of the Iron Curtain. One mistake could start a war in the middle of Europe.\n\nStability -8%, war support +15%, consumer goods +2%, factory output -5%, Cold War world tension +2.0 a month."
 cwgg_rv_stage_tt_6:0 "§Y6: War§!\nGerman soldiers are fighting Germans.\n\nStability -5%, war support +20%."

 cwgg_rv_tr_1_line:0 "[RV_Treaty_1]"
 cwgg_rv_tr_1_name:0 "1. Meeting of the Heads of Government"
 cwgg_rv_tr_1_tt:0 "§YMeeting of the Heads of Government§!\nWilly Brandt and Willi Stoph met in Erfurt in March 1970 and in Kassel in May. Nothing was agreed - but for the first time the two German governments talked to each other.\n\nRequires: climate at least §Y-10§!; Needs the focus §YChange through Rapprochement§!; no crisis at stage 3 or worse; 2 initiative and 25 political power to open talks.\n\nNegotiations advance every month with the climate, the Bahr - Kohl channel, the Permanent Representation and the hard-currency lever; a crisis halts them, a confrontation breaks them off."
 cwgg_rv_tr_2_line:0 "[RV_Treaty_2]"
 cwgg_rv_tr_2_name:0 "2. Berlin Settlement"
 cwgg_rv_tr_2_tt:0 "§YBerlin Settlement§!\nThe Quadripartite Agreement of September 1971 and the transit agreement that followed: unhindered traffic between the Federal Republic and West Berlin, guaranteed by the Four Powers.\n\nRequires: climate at least §Y-5§!; in force: Meeting of the Heads of Government; no crisis at stage 3 or worse; 2 initiative and 25 political power to open talks.\n\nNegotiations advance every month with the climate, the Bahr - Kohl channel, the Permanent Representation and the hard-currency lever; a crisis halts them, a confrontation breaks them off."
 cwgg_rv_tr_3_line:0 "[RV_Treaty_3]"
 cwgg_rv_tr_3_name:0 "3. Basic Treaty"
 cwgg_rv_tr_3_tt:0 "§YBasic Treaty§!\nThe Grundlagenvertrag of December 1972: two German states, equal rights, good-neighbourly relations - and Bonn's letter on German unity, so that nothing is given up for ever.\n\nRequires: climate at least §Y0§!; in force: Meeting of the Heads of Government, Berlin Settlement; Needs the focus §YThe Basic Treaty§!; a majority in the Bundestag to ratify; no crisis at stage 3 or worse; 2 initiative and 25 political power to open talks.\n\nNegotiations advance every month with the climate, the Bahr - Kohl channel, the Permanent Representation and the hard-currency lever; a crisis halts them, a confrontation breaks them off."
 cwgg_rv_tr_4_line:0 "[RV_Treaty_4]"
 cwgg_rv_tr_4_name:0 "4. Joint UN Membership Applications"
 cwgg_rv_tr_4_tt:0 "§YJoint UN Membership Applications§!\nCoordinate applications for UN membership. Admission requires approval through the Security Council and General Assembly.\n\nFederal Republic: [COLDWAR_GER_UN_status]\nGerman Democratic Republic: [COLDWAR_DDR_UN_status]\n\nRequires: climate at least §Y0§!; in force: Basic Treaty; no crisis at stage 3 or worse; 2 initiative and 25 political power to open talks."
 cwgg_rv_tr_5_line:0 "[RV_Treaty_5]"
 cwgg_rv_tr_5_name:0 "5. Permanent Representations"
 cwgg_rv_tr_5_tt:0 "§YPermanent Representations§!\nMissions, not embassies: Günter Gaus moved into Hannoversche Straße in East Berlin in 1974, Michael Kohl into Godesberger Allee in Bonn.\n\nRequires: climate at least §Y5§!; in force: Basic Treaty; no crisis at stage 3 or worse; 2 initiative and 25 political power to open talks.\n\nNegotiations advance every month with the climate, the Bahr - Kohl channel, the Permanent Representation and the hard-currency lever; a crisis halts them, a confrontation breaks them off."
 cwgg_rv_tr_6_line:0 "[RV_Treaty_6]"
 cwgg_rv_tr_6_name:0 "6. Traffic, Post and Travel Agreements"
 cwgg_rv_tr_6_tt:0 "§YTraffic, Post and Travel Agreements§!\nTelephone lines, new autobahn crossings, visits for pensioners and urgent family matters: the small steps of the 1970s and 1980s.\n\nRequires: climate at least §Y20§!; in force: Basic Treaty; no crisis at stage 3 or worse; 2 initiative and 25 political power to open talks.\n\nNegotiations advance every month with the climate, the Bahr - Kohl channel, the Permanent Representation and the hard-currency lever; a crisis halts them, a confrontation breaks them off."
 cwgg_rv_tr_7_line:0 "[RV_Treaty_7]"
 cwgg_rv_tr_7_name:0 "7. Cultural Agreement and Town Twinning"
 cwgg_rv_tr_7_tt:0 "§YCultural Agreement and Town Twinning§!\nAfter thirteen years of talks the cultural agreement was signed in May 1986; Saarlouis and Eisenhüttenstadt became the first twinned towns.\n\nRequires: climate at least §Y30§!; in force: Permanent Representations; no crisis at stage 3 or worse; 2 initiative and 25 political power to open talks.\n\nNegotiations advance every month with the climate, the Bahr - Kohl channel, the Permanent Representation and the hard-currency lever; a crisis halts them, a confrontation breaks them off."
 cwgg_rv_tr_8_line:0 "[RV_Treaty_8]"
 cwgg_rv_tr_8_name:0 "8. State Visit of the SED Leader"
 cwgg_rv_tr_8_tt:0 "§YState Visit of the SED Leader§!\nIn September 1987 Erich Honecker was received in Bonn with flags and anthems - and spoke of a border that would one day 'unite rather than divide'.\n\nRequires: climate at least §Y40§!; in force: Permanent Representations, Traffic, Post and Travel Agreements; Needs the focus §YCoalition of Reason§!; no crisis at stage 3 or worse; 2 initiative and 25 political power to open talks.\n\nNegotiations advance every month with the climate, the Bahr - Kohl channel, the Permanent Representation and the hard-currency lever; a crisis halts them, a confrontation breaks them off."
 cwgg_rv_tr_9_line:0 "[RV_Treaty_9]"
 cwgg_rv_tr_9_name:0 "9. Treaty Community and Confederation"
 cwgg_rv_tr_9_tt:0 "§YTreaty Community and Confederation§!\nA treaty community between the two German states, with joint commissions, a common market and, one day, confederal institutions.\n\nRequires: climate at least §Y70§!; in force: Basic Treaty, Permanent Representations; Requires an open border; a majority in the Bundestag to ratify; no crisis at stage 3 or worse; 2 initiative and 25 political power to open talks.\n\nNegotiations advance every month with the climate, the Bahr - Kohl channel, the Permanent Representation and the hard-currency lever; a crisis halts them, a confrontation breaks them off."
 cwgg_rv_tr_avail:0 "§GReady to negotiate.§!"
 cwgg_rv_tr_done:0 "§GIn force.§!"
 cwgg_rv_tr_locked:0 "§gNot yet possible - see the tooltip.§!"

 cwgg_rv_tr_signature:0 "§YAwaiting signature.§!"
 cwgg_rv_treaty_review:0 "Review Proposal"
 cwgg_rv_treaty_review_tt:0 "Review or defer the current agreement. Reviewing costs no political power. The agreement takes effect only after both governments sign."
 cwgg_rv_waiting_orders:0 "§YWaiting for both governments to submit instructions.§!"
 cwgg_sec_access:0 "Access"
 cwgg_sec_access_tt:0 "§YAccess§!\nSend the special commando. Costs §Y35§! political power; one access every 45 days.\nBase chance about §Y1 in 3§!; better with the trace (§G+8§! from 75, §G+10§! from 90), the GSG 9 tier and BKA level 2.\n§RFailure§! (most likely): the suspect escapes and the trace falls by 35. §RShootout§! (rarer with a trained GSG 9): the suspect dies or escapes - and the movement gets a martyr.\nA traced suspect may also notice the surveillance and move on before you act."
 cwgg_sec_bal_l:0 "Security state\n§R[?cwger_security|0]§!"
 cwgg_sec_bal_r:0 "Rule of law\n§G[?cwger_rechtsstaat|0]§!"
 cwgg_sec_bal_tt:0 "§YThe balance§!\nEvery hard measure - dragnet, contact ban, isolation, force-feeding - strengthens the security state and weakens the credibility of the rule of law. A security state above 65 invites abuses (Traube affair, Celle Hole, Kießling affair); a weak rule of law feeds the sympathiser milieu."
 cwgg_sec_btn_ban_pkk:0 "Ban PKK"
 cwgg_sec_btn_ban_pkk_tt:0 "§YBan the PKK§!\nBan the Kurdistan Workers' Party and its front organisations.\n\nCost: §Y50§! political power.\n[SEC_Avail_ban_pkk]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_ban_right:0 "Ban Group"
 cwgg_sec_btn_ban_right_tt:0 "§YBan an Extremist Organisation§!\nArticle 9 of the Basic Law lets the Interior Minister dissolve associations directed against the constitutional order.\n\nCost: §Y60§! political power. Can be repeated after 24 months.\n[SEC_Avail_ban_right]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_contactban:0 "Contact Ban"
 cwgg_sec_btn_contactban_tt:0 "§YImpose a Contact Ban§!\nCut the imprisoned terrorists off from their lawyers and from each other while the hostage is held.\n\nCost: §Y25§! political power. Can be repeated after 2 months.\n[SEC_Avail_contactban]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_counterspy:0 "Counter-Spy"
 cwgg_sec_btn_counterspy_tt:0 "§YCounter-Espionage Campaign§!\nUnmask the 'Romeos' who court secretaries in Bonn ministries and the moles inside the BND.\n\nCost: §Y75§! political power. Can be repeated after 12 months.\n[SEC_Avail_counterspy]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_double:0 "Double Agent"
 cwgg_sec_btn_double_tt:0 "§YTurn a Double Agent§!\nAn HVA courier has been caught. Let him go home - and report what we want East Berlin to hear.\n\nCost: §Y60§! political power. Can be repeated after 12 months.\n[SEC_Avail_double]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_dropout:0 "Exit Offer"
 cwgg_sec_btn_dropout_tt:0 "§YExit Programme§!\nA quiet offer to members who want out: a new identity, reduced sentences, protection.\n\nCost: §Y50§! political power. Can be repeated after 12 months.\n[SEC_Avail_dropout]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_forcefeed:0 "Force-Feed"
 cwgg_sec_btn_forcefeed_tt:0 "§YForce-Feeding§!\nDoctors under police protection keep the hunger strikers alive.\n\nCost: §Y25§! political power. Can be repeated after 4 months.\n[SEC_Avail_forcefeed]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_givein:0 "Give In"
 cwgg_sec_btn_givein_tt:0 "§YGive In to the Demands§!\nRelease the prisoners. The hostage comes home - and every terrorist learns that the Federal Republic can be blackmailed.\n\nCost: No political power.\n[SEC_Avail_givein]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_informant:0 "Informant"
 cwgg_sec_btn_informant_tt:0 "§YRun an Informant§!\nAn informant inside the RAF's logistics could lead the BKA to the commando level - if the operation goes right.\n\nCost: §Y50§! political power. Can be repeated after 24 months.\n[SEC_Avail_informant]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_kinkel:0 "Release"
 cwgg_sec_btn_kinkel_tt:0 "§YRelease Renouncing Prisoners§!\nParole for RAF prisoners who have served long sentences and renounce violence.\n\nCost: §Y40§! political power. Can be repeated after 12 months.\n[SEC_Avail_kinkel]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_kronzeuge:0 "Witness"
 cwgg_sec_btn_kronzeuge_tt:0 "§YRecruit a Crown Witness§!\nLower sentences for those who testify against their former comrades.\n\nCost: §Y50§! political power. Can be repeated after 12 months.\n[SEC_Avail_kronzeuge]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_posters:0 "Posters"
 cwgg_sec_btn_posters_tt:0 "§YWanted Posters§!\nFaces of the most wanted in every post office, every bank, every border crossing.\n\nCost: §Y40§! political power. Can be repeated after 6 months.\n[SEC_Avail_posters]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_raster:0 "Dragnet"
 cwgg_sec_btn_raster_tt:0 "§YComputer Dragnet (Rasterfahndung)§!\nRun the BKA's computers in Wiesbaden against every database the state owns: electricity bills paid in cash, rented flats, car registrations.\n\nCost: §Y50§! political power. Can be repeated after 8 months.\n[SEC_Avail_raster]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_reward:0 "Reward"
 cwgg_sec_btn_reward_tt:0 "§YOffer a Reward§!\nHundreds of thousands of marks for information leading to an arrest.\n\nCost: No political power. Can be repeated after 12 months.\n[SEC_Avail_reward]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_safehouse:0 "Raid"
 cwgg_sec_btn_safehouse_tt:0 "§YRaid the Safe Houses§!\nDragnet results, informants and door-to-door searches in the district where the hostage is thought to be.\n\nCost: §Y50§! political power.\n[SEC_Avail_safehouse]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_stall:0 "Stall"
 cwgg_sec_btn_stall_tt:0 "§YPlay for Time§!\nMessages through the lawyers, a request for proof of life, a television statement that says nothing.\n\nCost: §Y25§! political power.\n[SEC_Avail_stall]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_storm:0 "Storm"
 cwgg_sec_btn_storm_tt:0 "§YSend In GSG 9§!\nThe commandos are ready. Their chance of success depends on their training and on how well the hiding place is known.\n\nCost: §Y25§! political power.\n[SEC_Avail_storm]"
 cwgg_sec_btn_vetting:0 "Vetting"
 cwgg_sec_btn_vetting_tt:0 "§YVet the Chancellery§!\nBackground checks for everyone with access to the chancellor's papers.\n\nCost: §Y40§! political power. Can be repeated after 12 months.\n[SEC_Avail_vetting]"
 cwgg_sec_capab:0 "BKA level §Y[?cwger_bka_level|0]§!/3\nGSG 9 tier §Y[?cwger_gsg9_tier|0]§!/3\nCounter-intel §Y[?cwger_counterintel|0]§!"
 cwgg_sec_capab_tt:0 "§YCapabilities§!\nThe BKA level speeds up the manhunt, slows the RAF's planning and improves foiled attacks. GSG 9 decides raids and rescues. Both are built through the focus tree."

 cwgg_sec_policy_txt:0 "Counter-espionage protects Bonn's channels to East Berlin as much as its secrets. The exit programme, the crown witness rule and the Kinkel initiative drain the milieu - the road that led to the RAF's declaration of 1992 and its dissolution in 1998."
 cwgg_sec_prot_btn_business:0 "[SEC_ProtBtn_business]"

 cwgg_sec_prot_off:0 "Withdraw"
 cwgg_sec_prot_on:0 "Protect"
 cwgg_sec_prot_tt:0 "Assign or withdraw a protection detail (§Y10§! political power to assign). Details: §Y[?cwsec_used|0]§! of §Y[?cwsec_slots|0]§!. More come from the focus tree."
 cwgg_sec_prot_txt:0 "The RAF picks its targets by generation: the first fought the 'imperialist' Americans and the Springer press, the second the justice system and business to free its prisoners, the third the 'military-industrial complex'. Planning speed grows with the active cadre and the milieu and falls with every BKA level. With BKA level 1 we know where an attack is coming; from level 2 we see how far it has got."

 cwgg_sec_r_prisoners_v:0 "[SEC_Value_prisoners]"
 cwgg_sec_raf_inactive:0 "The RAF case is not active. Formation: 14 May 1970; closed cases do not recruit or plan attacks."
 cwgg_sec_raf_tt:0 "§YThe RAF§!\nThe §Yactive cadre§! recruits from the §Ysympathiser milieu§!; repression and a weak rule of law feed the milieu, exit offers and calm drain it. Kidnappings need §Yprisoners§! to free. A generation ends when its leaders are in prison - the next one fights to free them."
 cwgg_sec_reg_association:0 "Association"
 cwgg_sec_reg_association_tt:0 "§YAssociation§!\nHeld together in small groups, as the prisoners demand. The movement calms down - and the prisoners can coordinate with the commandos outside.\n\nChanging the regime costs §Y25§! political power and is possible every six months."
 cwgg_sec_reg_isolation:0 "Isolation"
 cwgg_sec_reg_isolation_tt:0 "§YIsolation§!\nHigh-security isolation: the prisoners cannot organise - and the movement outside calls it torture. Milieu grows, hunger strikes come faster.\n\nChanging the regime costs §Y25§! political power and is possible every six months."
 cwgg_sec_reg_normal:0 "Normal Regime"
 cwgg_sec_reg_normal_tt:0 "§YNormal Regime§!\nOrdinary rules for high-security prisoners.\n\nChanging the regime costs §Y25§! political power and is possible every six months."
 cwgg_sec_right_label:0 "Rote Armee Fraktion"
 cwgg_sec_right_value:0 "[SEC_ThreatColored]"
 cwgg_sec_right_value_tt:0 "§YRote Armee Fraktion§!\nThe threat from the Red Army Faction and the wider left-wing underground. It grows with the RAF's active cadre and its sympathiser milieu - the students who lend a flat, the lawyers who carry a message, the professors who sign the open letters - and with the Movement 2 June and the Revolutionary Cells while they still exist."

 cwgg_stage_0:0 "Modus Vivendi"
 cwgg_stage_0_desc:0 "Two states have settled into a working relationship: visits, credits, treaties and a border that is quieter than it has ever been."
 cwgg_stage_1:0 "Cool Coexistence"
 cwgg_stage_1_desc:0 "Correct, cautious and transactional. Neither side expects much, neither side wants trouble."
 cwgg_stage_2:0 "Tensions"
 cwgg_stage_2_desc:0 "Harsh words in Neues Deutschland and the Bundestag, incidents at the border, channels running cold."
 cwgg_stage_3:0 "Crisis"
 cwgg_stage_3_desc:0 "A confrontation is under way. Every move is watched in Washington and Moscow."
 cwgg_stage_4:0 "Confrontation"
 cwgg_stage_4_desc:0 "Both states treat each other as enemies. Trade has halved, the armies are watching the border."
 cwgg_stage_5:0 "War Danger"
 cwgg_stage_5_desc:0 "Troops on alert on both sides of the Iron Curtain. One mistake could start a war in the middle of Europe."
 cwgg_stage_6:0 "War"
 cwgg_stage_6_desc:0 "German soldiers are fighting Germans."
 cwgg_stance_allies:0 "Call in the Allies"
 cwgg_stance_allies_desc:0 "Ask Washington, London and Paris to speak for Berlin and Germany as a whole. Needs NATO membership - and if Moscow is called too, the crisis is no longer ours."
 cwgg_stance_deescalate:0 "De-escalate"
 cwgg_stance_deescalate_desc:0 "Lower the temperature: conciliatory statements, a postponed visit, a quiet word in the ear of the Permanent Representation."
 cwgg_stance_firm:0 "Stand Firm"
 cwgg_stance_firm_desc:0 "Make clear that Bonn will not give way - without adding new pressure of its own."
 cwgg_stance_mobilise:0 "Prepare Mobilisation"
 cwgg_stance_mobilise_desc:0 "Raise readiness and say so. Deters escalation - and escalates."
 cwgg_stance_pressure:0 "Counter-Pressure"
 cwgg_stance_pressure_desc:0 "Use the lever that hurts East Berlin most in this crisis. Strong if the lever is strong, a bluff if it is not."
 cwgg_stance_secret:0 "Secret Channel"
 cwgg_stance_secret_desc:0 "Settle it quietly through an open channel. Effective, but the Stasi listens on every line it can reach."
 cwgg_stance_wait:0 "Wait and See"
 cwgg_stance_wait_desc:0 "Let the ministries handle it. Costs nothing and signals little - East Berlin sets the pace."
 cwgg_treaty_1:0 "Meeting of the Heads of Government"
 cwgg_treaty_1_desc:0 "Willy Brandt and Willi Stoph met in Erfurt in March 1970 and in Kassel in May. Nothing was agreed - but for the first time the two German governments talked to each other."
 cwgg_treaty_1_unlock:0 "Needs the focus §YChange through Rapprochement§!."
 cwgg_treaty_2:0 "Berlin Settlement"
 cwgg_treaty_2_desc:0 "The Quadripartite Agreement of September 1971 and the transit agreement that followed: unhindered traffic between the Federal Republic and West Berlin, guaranteed by the Four Powers."
 cwgg_treaty_3:0 "Basic Treaty"
 cwgg_treaty_3_desc:0 "The Grundlagenvertrag of December 1972: two German states, equal rights, good-neighbourly relations - and Bonn's letter on German unity, so that nothing is given up for ever."
 cwgg_treaty_3_unlock:0 "Needs the focus §YThe Basic Treaty§!."
 cwgg_treaty_4:0 "Joint UN Membership Applications"
 cwgg_treaty_4_desc:0 "Coordinate applications for UN membership. Admission requires approval through the Security Council and General Assembly.\n\nFederal Republic: [COLDWAR_GER_UN_status]\nGerman Democratic Republic: [COLDWAR_DDR_UN_status]"
 cwgg_treaty_5:0 "Permanent Representations"
 cwgg_treaty_5_desc:0 "Missions, not embassies: Günter Gaus moved into Hannoversche Straße in East Berlin in 1974, Michael Kohl into Godesberger Allee in Bonn."
 cwgg_treaty_6:0 "Traffic, Post and Travel Agreements"
 cwgg_treaty_6_desc:0 "Telephone lines, new autobahn crossings, visits for pensioners and urgent family matters: the small steps of the 1970s and 1980s."
 cwgg_treaty_7:0 "Cultural Agreement and Town Twinning"
 cwgg_treaty_7_desc:0 "After thirteen years of talks the cultural agreement was signed in May 1986; Saarlouis and Eisenhüttenstadt became the first twinned towns."
 cwgg_treaty_8:0 "State Visit of the SED Leader"
 cwgg_treaty_8_desc:0 "In September 1987 Erich Honecker was received in Bonn with flags and anthems - and spoke of a border that would one day 'unite rather than divide'."
 cwgg_treaty_8_unlock:0 "Needs the focus §YCoalition of Reason§!."
 cwgg_treaty_9:0 "Treaty Community and Confederation"
 cwgg_treaty_9_desc:0 "A treaty community between the two German states, with joint commissions, a common market and, one day, confederal institutions."
 cwgg_treaty_9_unlock:0 "Requires an open border."
 cwgg_u_before:0 "Unity by treaty is the hardest road in this game. Both German governments must want it and must agree on five chapters, one every three months. Then the United States, the Soviet Union, Britain and France each consent or veto - a veto reopens the chapter it objects to. Finally the Bundestag and the Volkskammer ratify.\n\nThe existing unity focuses only become available when relations are at §YCool Coexistence§! or better with a climate above §Y40§!; during the talks they move East Berlin and the Four Powers."
 cwgg_u_break:0 "Break Off"
 cwgg_u_break_tt:0 "§YBreak Off the Talks§!\nEnd the unity negotiations. The climate falls by 15 and the subject is closed for three years."
 cwgg_u_c1:0 "Unbroken détente: §Y[?cwgg_detente_m|0]§!/§Y36§! months (Modus Vivendi, climate 60+, no crisis)"
 cwgg_u_c2:0 "Climate now §Y[?cwgg_klima|0]§! (needs §Y70§!) · stage [RV_StageColored] (needs §G0§!)"
 cwgg_u_c3:0 "In force: Basic Treaty, Representations, Traffic, Culture or Visit"

 cwgg_u_ch_1_n:0 "1. The Constitution"
 cwgg_u_ch_1_ok_1:0 "§GAgreed:§! The Basic Law (Article 23)"
 cwgg_u_ch_1_ok_2:0 "§GAgreed:§! A New Constitution (Article 146)"
 cwgg_u_ch_1_ok_3:0 "§GAgreed:§! A Socialist Constitution"
 cwgg_u_ch_1_s:0 "[U_Ch1]"
 cwgg_u_ch_1_tt:0 "§YThe Constitution§!\nUnder which constitution do the Germans live together?\n\n§YThe Basic Law (Article 23)§! (western line): The GDR's Länder accede to the Federal Republic. The Basic Law applies everywhere.\n§YA New Constitution (Article 146)§! (compromise): A constituent assembly from both states writes a new constitution for all Germans.\n§YA Socialist Constitution§! (eastern line): The united Germany is built on the GDR's constitution: a people's republic with a leading party."
 cwgg_u_ch_2_n:0 "2. The Economy"
 cwgg_u_ch_2_ok_1:0 "§GAgreed:§! Social Market Economy"
 cwgg_u_ch_2_ok_2:0 "§GAgreed:§! A Mixed Economy"
 cwgg_u_ch_2_ok_3:0 "§GAgreed:§! Planned Economy"
 cwgg_u_ch_2_s:0 "[U_Ch2]"
 cwgg_u_ch_2_tt:0 "§YThe Economy§!\nWhich economic order does the united state have?\n\n§YSocial Market Economy§! (western line): The Deutschmark, private property and free prices - the GDR's combines are privatised.\n§YA Mixed Economy§! (compromise): Key industries, banks and land stay public; the rest is market. A 'third way' between the systems.\n§YPlanned Economy§! (eastern line): Central planning, people's enterprises, prices set by the state - the Federal Republic's industry is nationalised."
 cwgg_u_ch_3_n:0 "3. The Alliance"
 cwgg_u_ch_3_ok_1:0 "§GAgreed:§! In NATO"
 cwgg_u_ch_3_ok_2:0 "§GAgreed:§! Armed Neutrality"
 cwgg_u_ch_3_ok_3:0 "§GAgreed:§! In the Warsaw Pact"
 cwgg_u_ch_3_s:0 "[U_Ch3]"
 cwgg_u_ch_3_tt:0 "§YThe Alliance§!\nIn which alliance - if any - does the united Germany stand?\n\n§YIn NATO§! (western line): The united Germany stays in NATO; Soviet troops leave the East.\n§YArmed Neutrality§! (compromise): Germany leaves both blocs: an army of its own, no foreign troops, guaranteed by the Four Powers.\n§YIn the Warsaw Pact§! (eastern line): The united Germany joins the Warsaw Treaty Organisation; American troops leave the West."
 cwgg_u_ch_4_n:0 "4. The Capital"
 cwgg_u_ch_4_ok_1:0 "§GAgreed:§! Bonn, Federal"
 cwgg_u_ch_4_ok_2:0 "§GAgreed:§! Berlin, Federal"
 cwgg_u_ch_4_ok_3:0 "§GAgreed:§! Berlin, Centralised"
 cwgg_u_ch_4_s:0 "[U_Ch4]"
 cwgg_u_ch_4_tt:0 "§YThe Capital§!\nWhere does the united Germany govern from - and how centralised is it?\n\n§YBonn, Federal§! (western line): Government and parliament stay on the Rhine; the GDR is divided into Länder again.\n§YBerlin, Federal§! (compromise): Berlin becomes the capital of a federal Germany; the eastern Länder are restored.\n§YBerlin, Centralised§! (eastern line): Berlin governs a centralised state; the Länder become administrative districts."
 cwgg_u_ch_5_n:0 "5. The Borders"
 cwgg_u_ch_5_ok_1:0 "§GAgreed:§! Reserve the Peace Treaty"
 cwgg_u_ch_5_ok_2:0 "§GAgreed:§! The Oder-Neisse Line, Final"
 cwgg_u_ch_5_ok_3:0 "§GAgreed:§! Border and Peace Treaty"
 cwgg_u_ch_5_s:0 "[U_Ch5]"
 cwgg_u_ch_5_tt:0 "§YThe Borders§!\nWhat becomes of the Oder-Neisse line and of a peace treaty for Germany?\n\n§YReserve the Peace Treaty§! (western line): The border question stays open until a peace treaty - as the Federal Constitutional Court demands.\n§YThe Oder-Neisse Line, Final§! (compromise): The united Germany recognises its eastern border for ever in a treaty with Poland.\n§YBorder and Peace Treaty§! (eastern line): A formal peace treaty with the Four Powers and recognition of every post-war border."

 cwgg_u_propose:0 "Propose Talks"
 cwgg_u_propose_tt:0 "§YPropose Unity Talks§!\nOffer East Berlin formal negotiations on one German state. The Politburo will weigh its own survival, its dependence on Bonn's money and Moscow's line - a hardline leadership will almost certainly refuse.\n\nNeeds: three years of unbroken détente, climate 70, Modus Vivendi without a crisis, the Basic Treaty, the Permanent Representations and the traffic agreements in force plus culture or the state visit, the focus §YA European Peace Order§!, 3 initiative and 100 political power. After failed talks: three years' pause."
